Meet Ell!  She is looking for a loving home where she can continue to build her confidence.  When you first meet Ell, she can be very nervous and timid.  New people and unfamiliar situations can be overwhelming for her, but once she knows and trusts you, her sweet personality begins to shine.  She simply needs an experienced, patient owner who will give her time and space to settle at her own pace.  Once she’s comfortable, Ell is incredibly friendly and affectionate.  She loves belly rubs and enjoys lots of fuss.  She’s not particularly interested in toys, but she does love exploring the world and having a good sniff on walks.  In kennels, Ell can be very vocal, so she will need understanding neighbours and owners who appreciate that she may bark at first but this is just her way of expressing herself.  She can sometimes be a bit growly when she’s at the vets, but this is fear-related, and she benefits from calm, gentle handling during stressful situations.  Ell is currently carrying a little extra weight, so her new adopter will need to help her on a healthy weight-loss journey with sensible exercise and a balanced diet.  This will help improve her overall health and wellbeing.  Ell is looking for a kind, patient home that will see past her initial nerves and give her the chance to blossom. She would benefit from a private secure garden.

Ell has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel she could live with another dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Ell came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her and as she can be a little nervous we would like any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Stanley
description:
Meet Stanley!!  He is a handsome boy with a big personality and an even bigger zest for life!  Stanley is a very lively, playful, and giddy boy who loves being around people.  He’s friendly and affectionate, always ready for fun and eager to make new friends.  His enthusiasm for life is infectious, and he will make a fantastic companion for someone who enjoys the outdoors and has an active lifestyle.  Like many young, energetic dogs, Stanley will benefit from some continued training.  He still needs to learn his basic commands and can be quite strong on the lead, so his new adopter should be prepared to put in time and consistency to help him develop good manners.  Stanley can also get overexcited and does display humping behaviour.  This is something that can be managed with positive, consistent training and appropriate redirection.  Stanley is looking for an active home where he’ll receive plenty of exercise, mental stimulation, and ongoing training.  He will need a private secure garden.

Stanley has socialised well with other dogs while in our care, and is very giddy and playful.  We do feel he could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy level following a successful meet and greet.

As Stanley came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him and as he can be quite humpy, we would like any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Ripley
description:
Meet Ripley!! He is a gorgeous boy looking for an active, committed home where he can continue to learn and thrive.  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a fun-loving personality and is always ready for a game with his favourite toys.  He is full of energy and loves to play, so he will need an active family who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and ongoing training.  Like many young dogs, he can become a little mouthy and nippy when he’s excited, so he will benefit from patient guidance and positive reinforcement to help him learn appropriate manners.  He is still working on his basic commands and will need someone willing to continue his training.  He can also occasionally rag his lead, so further lead training will be important.  Previous experience with Shar-pei’s would be a real advantage, as they can have their own unique characteristics and training needs.  He currently has a cherry eye, which will be surgically repaired before he goes to his new home, so he’ll be ready to start his next chapter feeling his best.  If you’re looking for a playful, lively young dog and have to time and commitment to help him become the wonderful companion we know he can be, Ripley could be the boy for you.

Ripley has socialised well with other dogs and is very playful with them.  He can sometimes get frustrated and bark if he can’t get to them straight away.  We feel he could potentially be rehomed with another playful dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Ripley came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him and as he can be a little nippy when over-excited we would like any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Morgan
description:
Morgan came into our care through no fault of his own. Due to him being a rehome we do have some knowledge of what he was like in the home and he is already toilet trained. Morgan is a very friendly boy and loves to say hello to everyone he meets. Morgan spends most of his day relaxing on his comfy bed surrounded by his fluffy toys, which he likes to show off. Morgan is currently on a weight loss journey and will need to continue this when he goes home. Morgan is after a loving retirement home where he can spend his days lounging on his own comfy sofa. Morgan loves to go out for little walks and lots of sniffs!

Morgan can be rehomed with children who are 16 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Morgan needs to be the only dog in the house as he is after a peaceful and calm retirement home.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Bob
description:
Bob is a sweet boy but can be nervous of new people, especially around men. Bob is currently under training to help to reduce his nervousness around men and new people, his new family will need to be patient and may need to have extra meets to ensure that he is familiar of everyone in the house before he goes home. Bob will need continuous training to help with his socialisation skills. Once bob is comfortable his goofy personality soon comes out, he loves to play with his toys and all of the staff here. Bob loves his walks, due to his size he can be strong on the lead but with a little more training that would improve. Bob loves his treats and enrichment activities in between walks. Bob is a clever boy as he already knows a few tricks such as sit, down and paw.

Bob needs an adult only home where he can have plenty of space to settle in and gain more confidence. He will need an experienced home that has had large breed dogs before and can handle his size and boisterous behaviour once he is settled.

Bob has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care, he is still only young so he does like to bounce around and try and play with dogs. Further training is needed to help him improve his manners. Bob could potentially be rehomed with another dog – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Tess
description:
Meet beautiful Tess!  She is looking for a calm and understanding home where she can truly settle and blossom.  Tess can be a nervous girl when she first meets you and needs a little time to feel safe.  Once she gets to know and trust you, her lovely personality starts to shine through, and you see her friendly and affectionate side.  She is naturally quite quiet and would really benefit from an adopter who can take things at her pace and help build her confidence.  Experience with the breed would be an advantage, as someone who understands her nature will be best placed to help her thrive.  Tess came into our care suffering from Conjunctivitis, which is now being treated by our vet.  She has been such a good girl having her eye drops every day and takes it all in her stride.  Tess has interacted with other dogs while with us, but at the moment she tends to avoid them and will sometimes bark if she feels uncomfortable.  For this reason, we feel she would be happiest as the only dog in the home. The adopter will need to continue gently working on her confidence around other dogs so she can become more comfortable in their presence.   Tess is looking for a quiet, patient home with someone who won’t expect too much from her too soon.  Given time, reassurance and kindness, this sweet girl will form a wonderful bond with her new family.  Tess just needs someone willing to give her the chance to feel safe, build her confidence and discover how lovely life in a forever home can be.  She will benefit from a private secure garden.

As Tess came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Arlo
description:
Meet Arlo! Arlo is a gorgeous, sweet-natured boy who is very friendly and absolutely loves lots of fuss.  He’s a real people dog and enjoys getting plenty of attention and affection.  He is a very energetic and boisterous lad who can get extremely giddy when he’s excited.  He sometimes forgets just how big he is and will jump up to say hello, so he would benefit from some basic training to help him learn his manners and channel all that enthusiasm.  Arlo recently had a bath, and although he was a little nervous to begin with, he was a very good boy.  Once it was all over, he celebrated in true Arlo style with a case of the zoomies!  He also has a funny habit of rearranging his bed and moving it to wherever he thinks it should be.  Arlo is a loveable, fun, lively character with bags of personality.  He would thrive in a very active home with someone who can give him plenty of exercise, long walks and consistency with his training.  He would need a private secure garden so he can practice his zoomies!

Arlo has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful, so we feel following a successful meet and greet he could live with another dog of similar size and energy level.

As Arlo came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Ruby
description:
Meet Ruby!   This lovely girl is looking for an active, loving home where she can continue to grow in confidence.  Ruby can be nervous and unsure when she first meets you, so she will need a patient home who will allow her to settle and build trust at her own pace.  Once she gets to know you, her lovely personality really starts to shine.  She is an incredibly sweet and affectionate girl who loves a fuss and enjoys being close to the people she trusts.  As you would expect from a young Collie, Ruby has lots of energy!  She is giddy, playful and full of enthusiasm, and when she gets particularly excited, you may be treated to some brilliant zoomies!  Ruby will need an active home that can provide plenty of long walks, adventures and, just as importantly, lots of mental stimulation to keep her clever Collie brain busy.  Ruby is still very much a youngster and has plenty to learn. She will need help with her basic commands, along with continued training and socialisation to help her develop into a well-rounded adult dog.  She is also unsure about being groomed, so this will need to be introduced slowly and positively to help build her confidence.  Ruby would thrive with adopters who understand the needs of an intelligent, energetic breed and who have the time and commitment to continue her training.  Ruby will need a private secure garden.

She has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, although she can be a little unsure at first with some dogs.  We do feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where her new adopter can build up her confidence around other dogs in a controlled environment with lots of positive reinforcement.

Ruby does have a Grade 3 Heart Murmur.  This will be discussed further with the successful applicant.

As Ruby came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Tara
description:
Meet Tara!  This gorgeous girl is looking for an active, understanding home where she can continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything life has to offer.  When Tara first meets new people or finds herself in unfamiliar situations, she can be nervous and unsure and may need a little time and patience to feel comfortable.  Once she gets to know you, though, her affectionate personality really starts to shine.  She is a friendly and loving girl who enjoys being around people she trusts.  Tara is still very much a youngster and is playful, energetic and full of enthusiasm.  She would love an active home with people who can give her plenty of exercise, playtime and positive mental stimulation.  She already knows some basic commands and is keen to learn, but she will benefit from continued training to help her become the best version of herself.  Tara can also be strong on the lead, so her new adopters will need to be comfortable handling her and willing to continue working on her lead manners.  Most importantly, Tara needs adopters who will give her the time, patience and reassurance she needs to build her confidence.  With consistent, positive training and a secure home, we feel this affectionate young girl has so much potential.  She will need a private secure garden.

Tara has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care.  She can be nervous initially and is then very jumpy and boisterous with them, with no off switch, so we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where her adopters can work with her on her manners around other dogs.

As Tara came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Churro
description:
Churrocame into our care as a stray so we don’t have any history on him. He’s a young excitable boy who is in need of a family that has plenty of time to put into his training. He will need to work on all of the basic training to help with his manners.Churroneeds an active home so he can go on plenty of adventures to help to burn off all of his energy.Churrowill need a lot of mental stimulation in between walks too to keep him entertained, also he would enjoy participating in activities such as scent work.Churroneeds an experienced home; owned a Patterdale before or had a lot of experience with young rescues dogs.

Churroneeds to be the only dog in the home so he can have all the attention to help with his training.Churrohas interacted well with dogs whilst in our care but can be quite intense so will need more training to help him socialise appropriately.

Churrois after an adult only home with no visiting children either.Churrocan be quite cheeky and does like to nip fingers at times so needs an understanding family to help him over come this.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Star
description:
Star can be a little shy and quiet at first whilst she gets to know you but does like a fuss. She is now starting to come out of her shell a little and can get giddy and excited at times. She loves her walks and can pull when she is interested in a certain smell. As she gets more confident and settles we do believe her cheeky terrier side will come out. She certainly has plenty of energy!

Due to her still being a little nervous Star may require multiple meets so she can get to know her new family before going home. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding whilst she is settling in and getting used to her new surroundings.

We think that it is best for Star to be rehomed with children who are 16 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Star has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so can potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar temperament – subject to a successful meet.

We wouldn’t recommend Star to be rehomed with cats due to her breed.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Kong
description:
Kong is a loveable and friendly giant who is always happy,  and maybe a little too enthusiastic, to say hello to everyone he meets. Kong is still only a young boy so doesn’t know his strength and size. Further training will need to be done to ensure he can be taught manners. Kong does currently like to jump up so a family with experience around large breeds would be beneficial. Kong is a sweet boy and always greets staff in the morning with a blanket in his mouth and a very waggy tail!

Kong came into our care as a stray from another kennels so we don’t have any history on him or know if he has lived in a home before. Due to this and his size, Kong is best to be rehomed to an adult only home.

Kong has interacted well with friendly dogs whilst in our care but can be very boisterous and over the top. He will need continuous socialisation to help train him to react appropriately around dogs. He could potentially be rehomed with another dog that has a calm and friendly temperament but it is preferred for him to be the only dog in the home so that he can get all of the attention to help with his training. This would be subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Ebony
description:
Meet our gorgeous Ebony!  She was a little nervous and unsure at first, but it didn’t take her long to warm up and show us her lovely personality.  She is a very sweet and affectionate girl who really enjoys attention and being around people.  Once she feels comfortable, her giddy and playful side quickly comes out.  Ebony can sometimes forget just how big she is, especially when she gets excited, but it’s all part of her fun and loveable character.  Ebony knows her basic commands and is very keen to learn.  She is a very strong girl on the lead, so she will need someone who is confident and able to manage her strength while continuing her lead training.  She was also a very good girl during her visit to the vets and behaved brilliantly while having her vaccination.  Overall, Ebony is a big, affectionate, playful girl with lots of love to give.  Once she gets to know you, her sweet and silly personality really shines through.  She would benefit from a private secure garden. Previous experience with large breed dogs would be preferred.

Ebony has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet.

As Ebony came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Lyra
description:
Meet Lyra!  This beautiful girl is looking for an active, experienced home where she can thrive.  She is a lovely, sweet-natured girl with a very giddy and playful personality.  Lyra absolutely loves attention and fuss and is always happy to be involved in whatever is going on.  She has lots of enthusiasm for life and certainly isn’t shy about showing it! Lyra can jump up quite a lot when she gets excited, so this is something her new adopter will need to be prepared to work on.  She is also very strong on the lead and will need someone confident and capable of handling her while they continue training.  As you would expect from a Malinois, Lyra is an active, energetic dog who will need plenty of physical exercise, mental stimulation and ongoing training and socialisation.  Due to the needs and characteristics of the breed previous knowledge and experience of the breed or similar high-drive working breeds is required. Underneath all that energy is an incredibly sweet girl who loves affection and companionship. She will need a private secure garden.

Lyra has socialised well with other dogs, and is very giddy and playful with them.  We do feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered).

As she came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Zola
description:
Beautiful Zola is looking for a loving new home where she can enjoy plenty of adventures, affection and attention.  She is a very sweet and friendly girl with a lovely nature.  Zola absolutely loves a fuss and will happily soak up all the affection you have to offer.  As you would expect from her breed, Zola will need an active home with people who can provide her with plenty of daily exercise, enrichment and stimulation.  She would love an active lifestyle where she can enjoy good walks, exploring new places and spending lots of quality time with her family.  Zola has a gorgeous thick coat which will need daily brushing to help keep it healthy, comfortable and in good condition.  Luckily, grooming can also be another lovely opportunity for some one-to-one attention with this affectionate girl! She will need a private secure garden.

Zola has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel following a successful meet and greet could potentially live with another similar sized dog. (must be neutered).

As Zola came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Duke
description:
This lovely boy is Duke!  He is looking for a patient and understanding home where he can truly thrive.  When he first came into us he was very nervous, but given the time and space to build trust his friendly and affectionate nature shines through.  He can be quite vocal and will bark to let you know when he’d like some attention.  When he gets over excited or over stimulated he can become a little mouthy, so he will need owners who can calmly redirect this behaviour and continue his training and socialisation.  He already knows some basic commands and is eager to engage.  Being a large, strong boy, he does pull on the lead, so he will benefit from ongoing lead training and someone confident enough to manage his strength.  He is currently unsure around other dogs and would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where his new adopter can continue his socialisation with other dogs in a controlled environment with lots of positive reinforcement.  This handsome lad is looking for an active home, that can provide patience, consistency and plenty of exercise and mental enrichment.  He will need a private secure garden.

As he came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Raven
description:
Raven is a gentle, sweet-natured girl looking for a patient and understanding home where she can build her confidence at her own pace.

She has been no trouble in our care and has no issues with feeding or cleaning. When she first arrived, she was extremely nervous and wouldn’t approach for attention. By day five she had made small steps, coming over for a sniff, but she is still very worried about being stroked and is understandably wary of new people, often keeping her tail tucked between her legs.

As Raven came into our care as a stray, we don’t know what she may have experienced in the past, but it’s clear she will need kind, committed owners who are willing to give her the time, patience and reassurance she needs to flourish.

Although she has coped around other dogs in our environment, she is very unsure of them and would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where she can have her own space and settle without added pressure.

With time, patience and plenty of love, Raven has every chance of growing in confidence and becoming a wonderful, loyal companion.

name: Marshall
description:
This handsome boy is full of life and absolutely loves people! Friendly, affectionate, and always ready for attention, he has a big personality and an even bigger heart.

He can be very excitable and still behaves very much like a puppy, so he’ll need owners who are committed to continuing his training. He is strong on the lead and pulls when walking, but with consistency and patience he is eager to learn. Once he settles, he enjoys being stroked and is happy to be handled all over.

He is looking for an active home that can give him the time, guidance, and love he deserves to help him become the best companion he can be.

Suitable for children aged 14+due to his size, strength, and bouncy nature.

name: Prism
description:
Prism is an ex racing greyhound that has come into our care after retiring. Prism is looking for a home to call her own after always living in kennels. Prism is a sweet and gentle girl who enjoys attention and a cuddle. Prism walks lovely on the lead but can still react to certain wildlife due to her prey drive. Prism has never lived in a home before so will need a patient family that is willing to give her time to settle and adjust to her new surroundings.

Prism has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care and has had a kennel mate previously. Due to this prism can be rehomed with another dog of similar size – subject to a successful meet. Prism isn’t yet spade so any male dogs would have to be castrated.

Prism has interacted well with staff and volunteers so we believe that she can be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

name: Elias
description:
Elias is a very sweet and friendly boy. He came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on him. He has always been friendly with staff and volunteers whilst here. Elias can be a little strong on the lead due to his size so some basic lead training would be beneficial for him. We are looking for an active home for Elias as he has a lot of energy and would enjoy going on lots of adventures. Elias is a calm boy in his kennel and loves to have some down time with a tasty chew.

Elias is a friendly boy but due to his size we believe that it would be best for him to be rehomed with children over 14 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Elias has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care, he has a submissive nature around other dogs. We believe that Elias can be rehomed with another dog with the same energy levels.

name: Dakota
description:
Dakota is looking for her forever home, and she has so much love to give.  She’s an incredibly sweet, friendly girl who absolutely adores people.  If you’re happy to give her plenty of fuss, she’ll be in her element!  Despite her size, she is a gentle soul with a lovely nature and enjoys spending time with her favourite humans.  She already knows some basic commands and is very eager to please so would benefit from further training.  Being a young, strong dog, she can be powerful on the lead, so her new adopter will need to be confident and committed to continue her lead training.  Because of this, she will be best suited to an active home where she can enjoy plenty of exercise, adventures and mental stimulation.  If you are looking for a loyal, affectionate companion with a heart as big as she is, this lovely girl could be the one for you.  She will need a private secure garden.

She has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, and is very playful and can be too much for other dogs as she does get in their face so for this reason we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where she can continue to learn manners and boundaries around other dogs will the full support of her new adopter with lots of positive reinforcement.

As Dakota came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Coco
description:
Coco came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on her. She is a sweet but shy girl at times. She does get excitable once she gets to know you. With time and patience she will be a great companion for any home. She loves her walks and going outside for plenty of sniffs. As she came in as a stray, she would benefit from some basic training to help her flourish.

Coco can be rehomed with children 12+ – subject to a successful meet.

Coco has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care but can be a little nervous at first. We believe that she could potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar size and with a calm temperament.

name: Daisy
description:
Daisy was previously a racing greyhound who has been brought up in kennels. She is a smaller girl in comparison to a typical greyhound but still does have quite a high prey drive. She makes up for her size with her big personality, she is a very sweet and loving girl but can be a little cheeky at times. As like most greyhounds, Daisy enjoys a good walk and sniff in the woods, with the occasional time off lead in an enclosed area to burn off energy but will equally spend lots time relaxing on a comfy cosy bed. Daisy is after someone that is looking to give a dog lots of love and companionship, which she hasn’t previously had in her life. She in return will give you unconditional love.

Daisy can be a little nippy at times so we feel that it would be best for her to be rehomed with children who are 14 years or older – subject to a successful meet.

Daisy is currently paired and used to living with another greyhound in kennels. She has also interacted well with other dogs whilst on walks so we believe that she could be rehomed with another dog of a similar size and temperament – again subject to a successful meet.

Due to Daisy being an ex-racer it wouldn’t be suitable for him to be rehomed with cats or small furries.

name: Treats
description:
Treats is a retired racing greyhound who has spent all of his life in kennels and is now ready to find his forever home. Treats is an affectionate boy who is after someone who wants to give him the life that he deserves full of adventures and love. Treats is an energetic boy who loves going for his walks and having off lead time zooming around the enclosed compound area. Once he has burnt off his energy he is ready to snooze away the day on his comfy bed.

With his out going personality and loving heart, he would fit into many different households that can offer him kindness, exercise, and plenty of cosy spots to curl up in. In return, this gorgeous soul will bring warmth, devotion, and endless companionship.

We believe that Treats can be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Treats is currently paired and is used to living with other greyhounds in kennels, he has also walked and interacted well with other dogs during his time as the home so could possibly be rehomed with another dog of similar size and temperament – again subject to a successful meet.

Due to treats being an ex-racer it wouldn’t be suitable for him to be rehomed with cats or small furries.

name: Eileen
description:
This gorgeous girl is Eileen.  She is searching for her forever home where she can enjoy all the fuss and attention she deserves.  She is an incredibly friendly girl who absolutely loves being around people.  Whether it’s cuddles on the sofa, a gentle scratch behind the ears, or simply spending time by your side, she’s happiest when she’s receiving attention from her favourite humans.  Out and about, she is a pleasure to walk and is good on the lead, making her an enjoyable companion for daily strolls and adventures.  Don’t let her laid-back Bulldog looks fool you – this girl has a playful side too!  Tennis balls are her absolute favourite, and she loves nothing more than a game of fetch or carrying her prized ball around with her.  As with many Bulldogs, we would prefer applicants to have previous breed experience and a good understanding of the breed’s specific needs.  Her new adopter should be committed to providing the care, companionship and lifestyle that will allow her to thrive.  This sweet natured girl has so much love to give and is ready to become a cherished member of her forever family.  She would benefit from a private secure garden.

Eileen has been rehomed previously but was returned to us as she wasn’t too keen on the man in the house but she was absolutely fine with the lady.  We are now looking for an all female home where we think Eileen would be most relaxed, where the new adopters can work with her issues surrounding males.  We have male staff here at the home and she has been absolutely fine with them.  She will need an experienced home with adopters that have previous experience with the breed.  She would be best suited to an adult only home.

Eileen has socialised well with other dogs and is very playful, so we feel she could be rehomed with another dog (must be neutered) of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet.

name: Ranger
description:
This handsome boy is Ranger!  He is guaranteed to bring fun, energy and plenty of personality into his new home.  Affectionately known by the staff as their ‘Social butterfly’ he loves meeting new people and is always ready to make new friends wherever he goes.  He is a friendly, giddy and playful boy who approaches life with enthusiasm.  His excitement can sometimes get the better of him, and he can be quite boisterous, often jumping up to greet people.  Ongoing training and consistent boundaries will help him learn more appropriate ways to say hello.  Like many hounds, he is very vocal in his kennel and isn’t shy about letting everyone know he’s there! He thrives on interaction and enjoys being involved in the action, so will need a very active home.  Potential adopters should be aware that he may display typical hound traits like unreliable recall and great at escaping so he will need a private secure garden and careful management when outside of the house.  He is also very strong on the lead and will benefit from continued lead training and handlers who are confident managing a powerful dog.  This lad is full of energy and would suit an active home that can provide plenty of exercise, mental stimulation and opportunities for adventure.  He’ll make a fantastic companion for someone who enjoys an outdoor lifestyle and is prepared to continue his training.  In return, you’ll gain a fun-loving affectionate character with a huge zest for life and enough enthusiasm to keep a smile on your face every day.

Ranger has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care although he can be very full on with them and extremely playful.  We feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where he can get 100% of the training he needs.

As Ranger came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Pudding
description:
This handsome boy is Pudding.  He is a friendly, affectionate lad who loves nothing more than a good fuss and plenty of attention from his people.  He is a big, strong boy with a bouncy personality and can be a little over-enthusiastic when meeting people.  He does have a habit of jumping up for attention and sometimes forgets just how big he is, so his new adopter will need to be prepared to continue working on his manners and help him channel his excitement appropriately.  On walks, he does sometimes rag his lead at first as he gets over excited, but does settle down and walk nicely and more calmly, he does enjoy getting out and about.  Due to his size and exuberant nature, we are looking for an adopter with experience of large, strong and bouncy dogs who can provide consistent guidance, ongoing training and plenty of exercise and mental stimulation.  In return, you will gain a loving, loyal companion who thrives on human interaction and is sure to bring lots of fun and affection into his new home.  He will need a private secure garden.

Pudding has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he could potentially live with another dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As pudding came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Scooby
description:
Meet our handsome boy Scooby, who is slowly learning that the world isn’t such a scary place after all.  When he first arrived with us, he was extremely timid and unsure around people. Since, then he has made lovely progress in the care of our kennel staff.  He will now happily take treats from familiar people and is beginning to enjoy gentle strokes and attention once he feels comfortable.  One thing that brings out his personality is playtime – he absolutely loves his toys.  Because of his nervous nature, he will need patient adopters who are willing to give him the time he needs to build trust.  Multiple meet and greets will be required before any adoption can take place so he can get to know his new family at his own pace.  He gains a lot of confidence from other dogs, so we feel he would thrive in a home with a calm and friendly resident dog who can help show him the ropes and continue building his confidence. He will need an experienced owner that has previously had very timid dogs.  With time, understanding and patience, this sweet boy has so much potential to blossom into a loyal and loving companion.  Scooby will need a private secure garden.

As Scooby came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him and as he is extremely timid we would prefer any children/visiting children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Ivan
description:
This handsome lad is Ivan!  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a big personality and an even bigger heart.  Full of energy and enthusiasm, he’s always ready for fun and loves nothing more than chasing after tennis balls.  He’s a very excitable and giddy dog who doesn’t always realise his own size, so he can jump up when greeting people or when he’s excited.  He is also quite vocal at times, especially when he wants your attention.   He knows his basic commands and is eager to interact with people, but he will need continued training and guidance, particularly when out walking as he is very strong on the lead.  Due to his size and strength, he would benefit from an experienced and active owner who can continue his training and provide him with plenty of exercise and mental stimulation.  Ivan would benefit from a private secure garden where he can safely have off lead time to play fetch with his tennis balls.

Ivan has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he potentially could be rehomed with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet.

As Ivan came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Buddy
description:
This loveable boy is Buddy! He is the perfect mix of playful energy and affectionate companionship. He’s a friendly, easy-going lad who absolutely adores people and loves being the centre of attention.  Full of character, he’s excitable, giddy and always ready to make you smile.  Whether it’s cuddles on the sofa or a game in the garden, he just wants to be involved in everything you do.  He is bursting with energy and would thrive in an active home where he can enjoy plenty of exercise, playtime and mental stimulation.  Fetch is one of his favourite games, and he will happily keep you entertained for hours chasing after a ball.  Buddy is incredibly affectionate and loves a fuss, he will make a loyal, loving companion.  One thing to note : He is quite the escape artist, so he will need a private secure garden and owners who are mindful of doors, gates and fencing.  When Buddy came into us he had an Entropian (an eye condition) which has now been repaired and he is healing nicely.

Buddy has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he could potentially live with another high energy dog following a successful meet and greet.

As Buddy came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Mercy
description:
Mercy came into our care as a stray, very shut down and scared. With time and patience staff managed to win her round and she slowly came out of her shell. Little by little we are seeing her lovely personality shine through. With those she trusts, Mercy has shown to be very affectionate and sweet lady.

She is still a little unsure, especially around men. However, this is something we are currently helping her with, and her new family must be willing to continue this.

With Mercy being nervous and unsure she is looking for a very patient and understanding adult only home, where she can develop and settle in at her own pace. Her new family must have the time to be able to come and meet her multiple times so she can get to know you before she goes home.

Mercy is currently also having socialisation training around dogs to build up her confidence. She is still unsure of other dogs so needs to be the only dog in the home.

name: Toby
description:
Toby is a very loveable bouncy boy. He is still just a puppy so is going to need all of the basic training to help him grow up to be a well behaved boy. Toby is bouncy and pulls a lot of the lead due to excitement. Toby needs an enclosed garden where he is able to spend time zooming around and playing with toys to help burn off all of the energy that he has. Toby needs a family who has a lot of time to put into his training and exercise each day, especially for the first few months. Toby will need to be with a very active family who can take him on lots of adventures to help burn off his energy and to help socialise him.  Toby is a loveable and friendly boy but needs training to teach him manners.

Toby can be rehomed with dog savvy children who are 12 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Toby is a typical puppy around other dogs, always wanting to play and goes in feet first. Toby needs more socialsiation around other dogs to teach him how to appropriately interact. When toby meets a dog he is very friendly and just wants to play.  We think that he could be rehomed with another young dog of similar size and a dog who has a lot of energy and a high tolerance to dogs to keep up with toby’s playfulness.

Due to Toby’s breed, it is not advisable for him to live with cats.

Toby has lived in a home previously so we do have more information to provide to potential adopters.

Please do not apply for Toby if you are going on holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Cali
description:
Cali was a very nervous girl when she first arrived at the home, she came in as a stray so we don’t know much about her history. It has taken a lot of time and patience for Cali to show us her excitable, bubbly personality. Due to this we are after an experienced home that has the time to get to know Cali here before she goes home. Once Cali gets to know you she loves a fuss and attention.  She loves going out for woodland walks and gets very giddy for her lead, she pulls a little on the lead, due to her size, so would benefit from some on going training. Cali enjoys an offlead run in the enclosed compound where she can chase after a tennis ball.

Cali will need to live in an Adult only home with an enclosed garden where she has space to roam about at her leisure.  She used to be a little nervous and unsure around certain dogs, we have been working with her on this and introducing her to dogs which is helping her social interactions. She is now a friendly girl with most of the dogs on site and can say a lovely face to face hello and even tries to play with others. She will need continued training to help with her socialisation. We still feel that Cali will need to be the only dog in the house.

If you think you can give this gorgeous girl her forever home please apply!

name: Pearl
description:
This talkative girl is Pearl.  She is a very affectionate, confident and friendly girl that is always up for lots of fuss and strokes.  She can be very vocal when she wants your attention so probably not suitable for an apartment/flat.  She enjoys her walks everyday having a sniff about and saying hello to everyone she meets.  She is very strong on the lead so will need an experienced owner that is used to powerful dogs. Pearl would benefit from a private secure garden.

Pearl has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, she can be a little unsure at first but does come around after a bit, so we feel she may be best suited as the only dog in the home where she can take her time getting used to other dogs with lots of positive reinforcement from her new adopter.

As Pearl came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Mabel
description:
Mabel came in to our care as an ex racer, meaning she does have quite a high prey drive when out on her walks! She does walk beautifully until she sees a squirrel and then she’s off! She is a very chilled out girl in her kennel and does love to give you a scare when she’s under a blanket hiding!

This lovely girl is looking for a home where she can relax and enjoy her retirement years curled up in a bed or sprawled out on a couch! We do feel she could live in a home with another dog as she has interacted well with other dogs whilst being in our care. This would be subject to a successful meet. However shecannotlive in home with small animals such as cats, due to her high prey drive. We also feel she could potentially live in a home with a family where children are 12 years and older – subject to a successful meet.

Although Mabel does love being in her beds, she really does enjoy being out and about on her walks with her greyhound pals! So she would appreciate a home that would give her the best of both worlds – a lovely walk followed by snuggles with her favourite people! Please apply today to give her a forever home that she deserves so much!

name: Shadow
description:
Shadow is a very cheeky boy has been super friendly to our staff and volunteers since he came in to our care. With him being an ex racer, he does have a high prey drive so can try to chase squirrels whilst out for his walks! He was paired in his kennel prior to her going home and will walk well with other greyhounds. He does seem unsure around other breeds of dogs, especially smaller breeds and will be quite vocal towards them. The staff and volunteers have been doing socialisation training with him here and he is improving slowly, his new family would need to continue this to help with improve further.

Shadow will have spent most of his life in kennels with his racing background, so he may feel a little nervous going in to a home environment. We also do not know if he is house trained or toilet trained due to this. He loves to lie in his comfy beds after his walks – we sometimes catch him upside down showing his belly off!

We think Shadow would prefer to be the only dog in the home, with him being a little unsure around other dogs at moment. However, he could potentially live with another greyhound if a meet and greet with him went well and depending on the other dogs temperament. He could also potentially live with children 12 years and older – subject to a successful meet.

Shadow would love a home where he could relax and enjoy his retirement years and rest on a comfy bed (or couch) of his own!

name: Willow
description:
This stunning girl is Willow.  Willow was very nervous and unsure for the first few weeks she was with us.  She was very vocal when the staff went in her kennel and would hide in the back.  The staff have worked hard with her to gain her trust and she has come out of her shell now and is showing her playful friendly side.  We are looking for an experienced owner for Willow that have had nervous large breed dogs previously and will work with her on her confidence, doing this at Willow’s pace and not too rushed.  She is a very independent girl who will come to you when she wants some attention, her toys are her number 1 priority in life.  Willow is very food orientated and will sit nicely for her treats.  This said she is a little bit chunky at the moment so is on weight management food to help her loose a few pounds, and well done to Willow and the staff as she has managed to lose 3kg up to now!  She will need continued training and socialisation. Willow will benefit from a private secure garden where she can have off lead time to relax and have a sniff about.

Willow has socialised ok with other dogs whilst in our care but we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home as she does prefer her own space.

As Willow came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer an adult only household.

name: Bruce
description:
Bruce is a very active and playful boy who absolutely loves chasing around our compound with his toys.  He can be quite boisterous and bouncy when he is excited so would definitely benefit from continued training and socialisation. He can be quite a strong boy on his lead too.

He will need an active home where he can get all the exercise and mental stimulation he will need every day. Bruce would benefit from a private secure garden where he can have off lead time with his toys in between his walks.

Bruce has interacted well with most dogs whilst in our care but can be very dominant with them so we feel he would be best suited to be the only dog in the home.  The new adopter will need to continue his socialisation with other dogs to improve his interactions with them.

As Bruce can get nervous and overwhelmed meeting new people, especially men, we feel that it would be best for him to go to an adult only home. He will need time to get to know you before going home. His new family will need to be able to commit to multiple meets.

Bruce is a wonderful, vibrant boy with lots of love to give to his new family! He has spent a while in kennels now so would love to find his forever home and someone to be the person to throw his ball endlessly! Do you think this could be you?

name: Todd
description:
Todd is a super friendly, but very energetic boy! He can be quite vocal towards other dogs whilst out on his walks due to wanting to play so would benefit from further training and socialisation. He enjoys treats and toys and loves a good play around with the staff in his kennel and on walks. Todd is the happiest when he is outside in our enclosed compound area off lead and running around with his toys. He would happily stay there all day! We think that Todd needs a reasonably sized fully enclosed garden that he can spend a lot of time in burning off all of his energy in between walks. Todd needs a family that is around a lot so he isn’t alone in the house for too long. His new family will need to have the time to ensure he is getting a lot of exercise every day and be able to take him to extra activities such as agility or scent work to help engage his brain and keep it stimulated.

We believe that Todd needs to be the only dog in the home so that he has all of the focus on him whilst he still needs extra training. Todd loves other dogs but can be very over the top whilst out on walks.

Additionally, we think that Todd needs to be in an adult only home.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Clover
description:
This gorgeous girl is Clover!  We are looking for an experienced owner for her.  Once Clover has bonded with you she shows off her loving side, it just takes some time for her to trust new people. Once she has got to know you she doesn’t leave your side.  Clover is a very boisterous and bouncy girl who does forget just how big she is when she is jumping up at you to say hello. She would definitely benefit from puppy training classes.  She can be very silly at times but in the nicest possible way and will definitely keep you smiling.  Her new adopter must give her all the support she will need whilst she gets used to new people and places and will have to commit to regular meet and greets before the adoption could take place.  Clover will need a private secure garden.

Please only apply for this gorgeous girl if you have the experience and can commit to the training and socialisation she will need.

Clover has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care but we do feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog so she can get 100% of the training and socialisation she will need.

As Clover came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children/visiting children to be 14+ years.

name: Frankie
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

06-08-26 Frankie is a shy boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. He has a gentle nature and, although he is a little unsure at the moment, he will happily accept a gentle fuss and some attention. Frankie is still learning that people can be trusted, so he will need a patient family who will allow him to build his confidence at his own pace.

Frankie gets on wonderfully with his kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so he will need a kind resident dog in his new home to help guide him and give him the reassurance he needs as he settles in and finds his paws. He will need a home that has experience with ex-breeders, and an extra secure garden to keep him safe as he continues to settle.

As Frankie has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. His new family will need to give him plenty of time and encouragement as he adjusts to his new surroundings. He is new to lead walking, but would love to continue this training in his new home once he has settled, so that he can go on plenty of adventures.

Frankie could share his home with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space while he settles in.

Frankie is a lovely boy with so much potential. With a calm, understanding family and a confident canine companion by his side, we hope he will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything that a loving home has to offer.

Frankie has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Jasmine
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

08-08-26 Jasmine has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. She is a lovely little lady who is understandably a little worried by all the recent changes in her life. Despite this, she is growing in confidence each day and will slowly approach you for a gentle fuss, showing the sweet nature that is waiting to blossom.

Jasmine is looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time, patience and reassurance to settle into her new life. She is a gentle soul who will thrive with a family who are happy to let her build confidence at her own pace.

She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help show her the ropes and reassure her as she adjusts to her new life. Having a canine companion will give Jasmine the confidence she needs as she learns that the world can be a safe and happy place.

She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She has not yet learnt to walk on a lead or harness, so this will need to be introduced gradually and positively once she has settled into her new surroundings.

Jasmine is a truly sweet little girl who is already beginning to come out of her shell and we think whoever adopts her will adore her.

When Jasmine arrived, she was walking with a noticeable limp and struggling to use her right hind leg. Our vets found that an old injury had healed with significant scar tissue, which was restricting her movement and preventing her from fully extending her leg. Jasmine has since undergone surgery to remove some of the excess scarred tissue. She is recovering well and is now using her leg much more. She will need to continue building up the muscle in her leg, but we are really pleased with her progress. She may always have a slightly unusual gait due to her old injury, but this certainly doesn’t stop her from getting on with life! Jasmine also has an old healed break in her tail.

Jasmine has been given the Gift of Life by Marjory Dexter

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Molly
description:
I can live with dog-savvy teens, and would love an active home!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I would love plenty of adventures once I am fully vaccinated!

I am just a puppy! Please be patient with me while I learn the basics!

My adopter will need to agree to have me spayed when I'm old enough.

01-08-26 Molly is an amazing puppy who has come to us with her siblings following an accidental litter. She is a happy, confident girl who is full of fun and has a wonderful zest for life.Mollyis already a big girl for her age, and we believe she is a Cane Corso Cross, so her adopters will need to be prepared for her to grow into a large adult dog.

Mollyis a friendly and affectionate pup who is looking for a loving home where she can continue to learn and explore the world. She has started learning about walking on a harness, and would like to continue this, out and about, once she is fully vaccinated and settled into her new home, she will love getting out and about on plenty of adventures with her family.

Mollycould live with older, dog-savvy children, aged 13+ who understand that she is a large, boisterous puppy and will need help learning her manners as she grows. She could happily live with another friendly dog who doesn't mind sharing their home with a playful youngster, or she could be an only dog, providing her new family have plenty of time to dedicate to her training, socialisation, and exercise.

As with all puppies,Mollywill need continued guidance with house training, lead walking, and all the basics of family life. Her adopters must be committed to taking her to puppy socialisation and training classes to help her develop into a confident, well-mannered adult and agree to have her spayed when she is of age.

Mollyis a truly lovely girl with so much potential. She is looking for a family who will give her the love, time, and commitment she deserves, and in return she is sure to become a wonderful and loyal companion.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved to a foster home and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people and enjoy all the love and affection he has missed out on. While he is still worried by some men due to his past experiences, once he trusts you his affectionate nature really shines through. Crispin lives alongside two cats in his foster home and he is not bothered by their presence.

Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He gets on wonderfully with the other dogs in his foster home and sleeps happily alongside them through the night. Although he enjoys their company, his foster carer feels he could also be very happy as an only dog, where he can soak up all the cuddles and attention he so craves. In the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he would thrive.

One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. He now walks beautifully on both a lead and harness, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. He has settled quickly into his foster home's routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, but this has already improved over the last few days as he has established a routine. His adopters should still be prepared to continue his house training with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.

Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly, and you would hardly know he has any issues with his eyesight. He has also had all of his teeth removed, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.

Crispin really is a special little boy who has had a difficult start in life but has so much love to give. He is looking for a very special family who will understand his worries, cherish the affectionate little dog he has become, and give him the love and security he so deserves. In return, they will gain the most devoted and loving companion.

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin recently moved foster homes through no fault of his own. He is a gorgeous, well mannered, cuddly boy who loves his walks, his humans and his food.

He gets along with the cats and dogs in my home, though initially Crispin demanded all the attention and would push the other dogs out of the way to get his cuddles first but with careful handling this has improved over the week.

He loves to cuddle up on my bed with my own dogs and sleeps all night there. He lives for his walks and gets very excited when his lead/harness appear. He can walk on his own or with another dog for company.

He happily shares his food bowl with his foster friend Lemon Pie. Even the cats dig in with him sometimes. He is getting used to being left when I go shopping and I am extending these trips so he gets used to being without humans for a while. Crispin does bark initially when visitors come into my home but this soon subsides when he realises they will do him no harm. Keep up the good work Crispin, you've got this my boy

Crispin has been back in foster care for a week and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be loved. Sadly, he was returned because he became anxious and barked whenever the man in the household moved around.

He walks beautifully on a lead and harness, sleeps soundly through the night alongside the other foster dog, and travels well. Although he is perfectly happy living with other dogs, he could also be an only dog so he can enjoy all the cuddles and affection he deserves. He has had a few little accidents indoors first thing in the morning, but over the last few days he has settled into a much better routine.

Crispin has no teeth, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He also has a cataract in one eye and the beginnings of a cataract in the other, but you would hardly know he has any sight issues as he gets around so well.

He really is a very special little boy who simply needs a loving home where he can feel safe, secure, and cherished.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.Crispin is a dear little boy who can still be worried and unsure at times. It is clear that he had very little socialisation in the past, and although he has made lovely progress since living in a home, he still needs patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He can be touch-sensitive when he is feeling anxious, so gentle handling and allowing him to approach in his own time will help him continue to gain confidence.Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He would be happy to share his home with another kind and confident resident dog in his new home. However, in the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he could also be the only dog in the home.One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. Once out, he walks beautifully on a lead, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. However, he hasn't quite mastered house training yet, so his adopters will need to continue helping him learn with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. He has had dental work and unfortunately did need to have all of his teeth removed, so he will need to stay on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.Crispin is a gentle soul who has had a difficult start in life, but he has already shown that, with kindness and patience, he is capable of making wonderful progress. He is looking for a very special person who will understand his worries, celebrate his achievements, and enjoy watching him continue to blossom into the loyal and loving companion we know he can be.Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

name: Jenny
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I will need to learn how to walk on a lead, and would like quiet walks.

I have lived in a home before so I may already know the basics.

I have severe dry eyes, and a small lump. I will be spayed before adoption.

06-08-26 Jenny is a sweet and friendly older lady who has come to us from a breeder but has lived in a home in the past. She has a gentle, affectionate nature and loves to show her love by giving little kisses and gently nibbling your fingers, which is her own special way of asking for attention.

Jenny is a lovely girl who can be a little timid at times, so she is looking for a calm and peaceful home where she can enjoy her golden years surrounded by love and kindness. She would thrive with adopters who are happy to let her settle at her own pace and enjoy a quieter way of life.

Jenny could be an only dog in a home where her family have plenty of time to spend with her, or she could happily live with calm and gentle resident dogs who don't mind sharing their home. She could also live with sensible, older children who will respect her gentle nature and allow her the peace and quiet she enjoys.

As Jenny has previously lived in a home, she should already be familiar with many aspects of family life, including house training, although she may need a little reminder as she settles into a new routine. She will also need to learn to walk comfortably on a harness so that she can enjoy gentle strolls with her new family.

Jenny is a truly wonderful older lady who has so much love to give. She is looking for a calm, caring home where she can relax, be cherished, and enjoy all the comforts she deserves. In return, she will make a loyal and loving companion.

Jenny has come to us with severe dry eye and a small lump that at this time, does not need to be removed. She will receive treatment for her dry eye and this may need to be continued in the home.

Jenny has been given the Gift of Life by Vicki Webb

name: Whispy
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have not met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 2 mammary lumps removed and 2 teeth extracted.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes grumble or bark, but this has always come from a place of pure fear rather than aggression.

After spending a couple of weeks settling into her kennel routine, it is clear that Whispy has experienced very little kindness in her life. Her fears are deeply ingrained, and she has no understanding of what people's intentions are. When someone enters her kennel, she will often bark and grumble in panic because she is so frightened of what might happen next. Despite this, she allows gentle handling, strokes, and being picked up without any fuss, almost as though she has simply resigned herself to it. It is incredibly sad to see, and all she really needs is someone who will show her that people can be kind.

Whispy takes enormous comfort from other dogs and has formed lovely bonds with her two current kennel companions, who she happily shares everything with. She can be selective about the dogs she befriends and seems to prefer smaller, calm, gentle dogs rather than larger or more boisterous companions. Once she trusts another dog, they become an enormous source of reassurance, so she will need at least one kind, quiet, confident resident dog in her forever home who can help her navigate the world and show her that life doesn't have to be so frightening.

Whispy is looking for a calm, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with very scared ex-breeding dogs and who understand that trust cannot be rushed. As she has never lived in a home before, she will need help learning everything from house training to settling into a routine. Walks are not something she is ready for at the moment, and her adopters must be prepared to let her progress entirely at her own pace. Gentle garden exploration will be much more appropriate until she feels safe enough to take the next steps.

Because Whispy is an older girl and her fears are so deeply rooted, she may never completely lose all of her worries or become the confident dog people often imagine. Her adopters will need to love and accept her exactly as she is, celebrating every tiny step forward without expecting her to become a different dog. For the right family, watching Whispy slowly learn to feel safe will be incredibly rewarding.

Whispy is a very special little lady who has spent far too much of her life living in fear. She deserves a safe place to call home, where she knows nobody will ever hurt or give up on her again. With endless patience, understanding, and unconditional love, we hope she can finally experience the peaceful and happy life she has always deserved.

She has had two mammary lumps removed at the time of her spay and has also had two teeth extracted.

Whispy has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Smith

Whispy has been on my section for a couple of weeks now and oh my goodness is she a heartbreaker. I have no idea what she’s been through in her life, but her fears are deeply ingrained. She has no trust in anything or anyone, apart from a select few dogs at the rescue that she has dropped her guard with. She has absolutely no idea about human kindness, nor what our intentions are. She grumbles and barks when we enter her kennel in pure panic, as she’s so scared of what we’re going to do to her. Even though she may sound a little scary, she lets me stroke her and pick her up absolutely fine .. kind of like she’s just given up. It’s quite sad actually.Whispy currently has 2 kennel friends who she gets on well with and shares everything with. One is a Shih Tzu Cross and one is a Poodle Cross. I have tried quite a few dogs with her and it does seem as though she favours smaller dogs to larger ones. And definitely calmer, quieter ones that don’t get in her face.Whispy will need a very patient and understanding home with adopters who have experience with very scared dogs. Because she’s on the older side, she may never truly lose all of her worries and fears, and may never become a ‘normal’ dog, and this is something her adopters will need to be okay with, and love her and accept her anyway. Things such as going out for walks are not currently in the near future for Whipsy, and it’s going to take a lot of time and gentle guidance to ease her into such things.This poor, sweet girl does not deserve to live her life in fear and panic mode. She deserves to have a safe place to call her own, where she knows nobody is going to hurt her. She deserves to be loved unconditionally, and to not be given up on no matter what.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down, and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes be a little grumbly, but this was simply because she is so frightened and overwhelmed by her surroundings.

Since then, she has started to settle in and is trying so hard to be brave. She can be vocal with people and is still nervous to approach you but with patience and kind handling she has been joining in on yard times and taking treats, but she still has a ways to go. Whispy has never known the kindness of people so will retreat to a corner when she feels stressed.

Whispy will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her all the time, patience and understanding she needs to settle and learn to trust.

She relies on other dogs for reassurance and so she will need at least one other confident, laid back resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and provide reassurance as she begins to build confidence. She can be selective over the dogs she enjoys spending time with however once she takes to a friend, she does so well with them and it boosts her confidence. She will need a very placid dog in the home who won’t worry when she is scared. She has had a few grumbles when meeting new dogs but she is just scared and needs time to develop a bond with them.

As she has never lived in a home before, Whispy will need kind and understanding adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will be too overwhelming for her at the moment and once she is more comfortable she can begin learning in a secure garden until she feels brave enough to venture further.

Whispy is a very special lady looking for an equally special home. She has missed out on so much in her life and will need a home who will take things day by day with her and give her the support and love she’s so desperate for.
