name: Monet
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 12 teeth extracted at the time of my spay.

06-08-26 Monet is a very timid little lady who has come to us from a breeder and relies heavily on her canine friends for comfort and reassurance. She is easy enough to handle but can be quite skittish when approached, so she will need plenty of time, patience, and TLC to help her build her confidence.

Monet will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can rely on as she begins to trust, learn about companionship, and discover that the world isn't such a scary place. As Monet has never lived in a home before, she will need a calm and quiet, adult-only home will be patient as she learns about house training, walking on a lead, and all the other basics of home life.

Monet is a very sweet little lady who simply needs a kind and understanding family willing to give her the time she deserves. As her confidence continues to grow, we're sure her lovely personality will shine through.

Monet has had 12 teeth extracted and would benefit from a soft food diet.

name: Martha
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy children who allow me time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have had most teeth extracted and only have a few left.

07-08-26 Martha is a stunning girl who has come to us from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a little apprehensive at first, but once she feels comfortable she really enjoys a gentle fuss and begins to relax. Martha is still adjusting to all the changes around her, so she will need kind adopters who are happy to let her settle at her own pace.

Martha gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws. She can live with older, dog-savvy children who allow her time to settle in. But she is so sweet, this shouldn't take her long.

As Martha has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding while she learns that home life can be safe and enjoyable. She already walks well on a lead and would love to continue this in her new home, and go on plenty of adventures!

Martha is a lovely, gentle girl with so much potential. With the support of a friendly canine companion and a calm, patient family, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything that a loving home has to offer.

Martha has had to have an extensive dental while in our care and has had most teeth extracted with only a few teeth remaining, so would benefit from a soft food diet moving forward.

Martha has been given the Gift of Life by Barbara Halstead

name: Toby
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog and no cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead but can be reactive to bikes.

I was born with some deformed toes, which have been amputated.

Toby is a handsome Cocker Spaniel who has been through a lot in his young life and is now looking for a special someone to help him write his next chapter. Originally coming to us from a breeder at just three months old, Toby was a very scared little puppy who found the world overwhelming. Although he found a loving home, he was sadly returned to our care after his adopters felt unable to manage some of his behaviours.

Toby is still a sensitive soul and will need a calm, adult-only home with no visiting children. His new family should have experience with worried or complex dogs and be confident in helping him feel safe. He will need a home without cats as he has met them at the rescue, and was too interested. While he is generally affectionate and loving, Toby has shown some resource guarding tendencies, such as grumbling when people pass by his bed or the sofa when he is resting there. He did once nip his adopter. This was an isolated incident, but it’s important that any new adopters are comfortable managing and working with these behaviours using gentle, positive methods. That said, since being back with us Toby has come out of his shell beautifully. He greets staff with a wagging tail, and absolutely loves attention, affection, and food, especially food! Those who work with him absolutely adore him and think he is the most special and wonderful boy!

Toby will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog. He did live with another dog previously and while they did get along, he did sometimes guard his adopter’s attention, so for this reason he is best suited to being homed as an only dog.

Out and about, Toby enjoys his walks and is lovely on and off the lead. He has good recall and mixes well with other dogs, although he can be reactive to bicycles, so should only be let off lead in safe, secure areas away from the public.

Toby was born with some deformed toes that were later amputated. He has always had a slightly unusual gait due to this, but our vets have noted he does also have a luxating patella and is on pain relief for this at the moment, but this may improve with gentle exercise. He also has a naturally short tail, which just adds to his unique charm.

Toby is a sweet, loving boy who truly wants to connect. He has already won the hearts of everyone here, and we’re all rooting for him to find a calm, understanding home where he can feel safe, build trust, and thrive.

If you have the time, patience, and experience to offer Toby the gentle guidance he needs, he will reward you with loyalty, love, and plenty of cuddles.

Tobywill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

This week, Toby’s kennel mum celebrated his 1 year anniversary by breaking him out of the rescue for a couple of hours of fun!!Toby travelled good as hold in the car, and happily climbed into the back of the car & had his seatbelt harness fitted with no issues at all.He travelled to Pupstars Paddock with his kennel mum & another staff member who was new to him. He was absolutely brilliant with that staff member who could only sing his praises!!Toby absolutely LOVED the secure field, his tail did not stop wagging, he followed his kennel mum around everywhere and was (very gently) taking treats of both staff members.Once Toby bonds with you, he is the most loyal boy in the world. His circle of trust is only getting bigger, with more and more staff members falling in love with him as time goes on. He may have a stricter criteria than most, but it just means he is just an incredibly special boy in need of a special home. He is such a darling and we wish more people would be able to see it!

Toby’s one year anniversary with us is slowly approaching, and it honestly breaks my heart every day knowing he’s still not curled up on a sofa in a home of his own.

Toby is literally such an amazing dog when he knows you, all he wants to do is spend time with you, whether that be sitting with you, or going out for a gentle stroll!

Recently, I’ve been working on Toby’s lead reactivity, and he’s been doing incredibly well. He’s making such good progress, and I’m so proud of how far he’s come!

I really hope this is the last update I have to write about toby, hopefully his next updates will be coming from his new pawrents, showing us him blossoming in a home and how truly special he really is!

I’ve had the absolute joy of working with Toby for a couple of months now, and he truly is one of my more sensitive, special boys!

Once Toby gets to know you, he turns into the happiest, most affectionate little soul you could ever meet! He absolutely loves zooming around our big play yard, or heading out for a calm, gentle stroll along the lanes taking everything in at his own pace, Toby can be reactive towards passing cars or other dogs, it is something we are currently working on with him!

With the weather getting nicer, I decided it was the perfect day for a little adventure down to the river! To get there, we walk through a huge open field, so I popped Toby on a long line to give him some extra freedom to explore.I don’t think I’ve ever seen a dog so happy he spent most of his time rolling around on his back in the grass with the biggest grin on his face!

When we reached the river, Toby was a little unsure at first. He sat at the edge, watching the water. But after a few minutes of building up his courage, he dipped his paws in and that was it, he was happily paddling back and forth, enjoying every second. It was such a special moment to watch.

I truly adore Toby with my whole heart, he’s one of those dogs who just stays with you, always on your mind.

He can still feel a bit unsure when meeting new people and might bark or back away at first, but give him a little time and patience, and he’ll become your most loyal, loving best friend.

I honestly can’t believe Toby is still waiting for his forever home. He is such a gentle, beautiful soul who deserves the absolute best life has to offer!

Toby is a sweet older gentleman who truly enjoys the quieter side of life. He loves nothing more than snuggling up for a nap and being close to his people.

Toby still has a playful spark and enjoys his daily walks as well as pottering around the yard. He would thrive in a calm, peaceful home and is best suited to a household with no children or cats, where he can relax and enjoy his golden years in comfort.

I love Toby. He is so loved by many of us here at the rescue. He's a confident boy once he knows you, but until he feels comfortable around you he can bark and sometimes be a bit standoffish.

Toby is a big cuddle bunny, he absolutely loves a fuss, and will happily accept butt scratches any time of the day.

He enjoys going out for walks but absolutely loves being off lead and running around the big play yard, when his butt wiggles with happiness and excitement it really doesn't stop, it's super adorable. He likes chasing a tennis ball but he won't bring it back, instead he rolls around with it usually in his mouth and will then lay with it and play with it, he's a comical boy.

Again, once he's comfortable with you he's very easy to handle, I can get a coat or a jumper on him with no problems, I can pick him up and I can brush him with no problems, he had a groom recently and he was no issue at all.

It's a shame he keeps getting overlooked, yes he might have some typical cocker issues such as guarding, but it hasn't been a huge issue since he's been here, I can go in and out of his kennel, pick things up etc and he's been fine. I've also been yarding him with other dogs to try and socialise him more, and although he can be selective of who he likes, once he's found a friend then he just wants to play. He is a beautiful boy inside and out, and in my opinion anyone would be lucky to have him as part of their family.

Also he is kennel clean so house training shouldn't take any time at all.

Please, don't let Toby spend another year in kennels, he truly deserves to find his forever home, as they all do. It's getting colder, it's been snowing, a nice warm, cosy house with a loving family is what he wants, I know his forever home is out there somewhere so please come and find him.

Toby is still doing incredibly well with us here and hasn’t shown any signs of guarding, while this has stopped with us here we still are unsure how he will react in a home environment.

It is an absolute pleasure working with Toby and he always brings a smile to your face throughout the day. Toby is a gentle, loving and happy boy and is desperate to have somebody he can give all his love to.

Toby has definitely come out of his shell since he's been here, he still barks when you first see him but it's a happy bark and his tail doesn't stop, before he would stay for scratches for a little bit, but know he doesn't want to leave you and wants all the attention. He is a very loving dog.

Toby originally came to us from a breeder when he was around 3 months old. He was a terrified puppy who was worried about everything and would even squeak in fear when being handled. He was quickly adopted and found a loving home, but he has sadly been returned to our care as he was displaying some behaviours that his adopters felt unable to cope with.

Toby was homed with another dog and while they got along well, he did show some signs of guarding his adopter from the other dog, for this reason we now think he would be most suited to being homed as an only dog.

Toby can also sometimes grumble if people walk past the sofa or his bed and he is on them, so he will be looking for an adult only home with no visiting children, with adopters who have experience with dogs with similar issues and will be able to work on this with him. He did nip his adopter once around 18 months ago, but that was the only time that resulted in more than a grumble.

Toby is still quite a scared boy in some aspects and certain things will make him extremely nervous, such as the hoover or sometimes even minor things like the sounds of a drawer closing, but with confident owners with experience of scared dogs we do believe he will progress further. He would be best suited to a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and follow a routine.

He enjoys going for walks and is very good both on and off lead. He has good recall and gets along well with other dogs outside of the home. He can be reactive to bikes, so his adopters would need to be mindful of this and keep him on lead in any areas where he may encounter bikes and only let him off lead in secure areas.

As he has lived in a home before, we believe he is house trained, but he may need some reminders.

Toby is a sweet boy at heart and in the right home and with the right adopters we think he will thrive. Since his arrival with us he has been on his best behaviour and already adores all of the staff that work with him and they adore him too. He absolutely loves his food and has a true zest for life which makes us smile each day, so we are so hopeful that his perfect home is out there and will find him soon.

Toby was born with some deformed toes, which have since been amputated but don't seem to bother him, though he does walk with a slightly abnormal gait. He also has a short tail.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Topps
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I would like a daily walk and lots of cuddle time.

I'm learning house training and building confidence on the lead.

I have a slight click in my left stifle joint, read below for more info!

Topps arrived with us from a breeder and, at first, was an extremely worried and shut-down little girl. Everything was overwhelming for her, and she found human contact very frightening, as she didn’t yet understand how gentle and loving hands could be. With time, patience, and kindness, Topps has started to blossom and has already made such wonderful progress. From barking at her kennel mummy and wanting little to do with people, she now feels comfortable sitting close, taking treats, giving sweet nose nudges, and even sharing little kisses. She has recently begun to accept gentle ear tickles when she is feeling brave, a huge step for her!

Topps has now moved to a foster home, where she is starting to learn all about home life and new skills like house training for the first time. In the home, she is still a little nervous as she adjusts to her new environment. Despite this, she will spend time in the same room as her carers, happily follow for food or to venture outside, and is comfortable moving throughout the home. Although she approaches her carers with encouragement from her canine friend or the help of a treat, she will avoid close contact at times. However, she is still very waggy-tailed and really gains confidence from her furry friends.

Topps still has a way to go and will need an experienced, adult-only home where she can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. She must have at least one kind and confident resident dog, who will play an important role in showing her the ropes and helping her feel safe. A secure garden is essential for her as she continues to learn about lead walking and house training. Topps will tolerate being handled for check overs or to have her harness put on, but she is wary and needs slow handling and reassurance.

This lovely girl may be worried at first in her new home, but with patience, reassurance, and love, she has every chance of blossoming further into the happy, content little dog she was always meant to be. Topps has already shown us what she is capable of; now she just needs someone to take a chance on her and give her the forever home she so truly deserves.

Our vet has noted a slight click in her left stifle joint on palpation. This is not currently causing her any discomfort and does not require treatment at this time, but it may need monitoring in the future. We recommend being mindful of excessive jumping on and off furniture or other jarring movements. Gentle exercises to help build and maintain muscle, such as controlled walking and stepping up and down kerbs, will be beneficial.

Topps is coming along really well, although she is still quite cautious at times. Despite this, she is such a happy girl and will happily come over when she would like some attention. She absolutely loves going out for walks and gets very excited as soon as the harness comes out. She also really enjoys seeing other dogs while out and about, often going over to greet them, and she has even started to approach people on walks too. Topps is very food-motivated and takes treats from people very gently.

Topps is a happy, tail-wagging girl who has settled in wonderfully with the other dogs in the house. She loves cuddling up and sleeping alongside her canine friends, and she gets along well with other dogs she meets too.

While Topps is confident around dogs, she is still a little cautious and hesitant around people. That said, when she feels ready, she will happily come over for a gentle chin scratch or an ear rub, all on her own terms.

Topps would thrive in a home that is patient and understanding, giving her the time she needs to build trust and feel completely comfortable. With her cheerful nature and love for canine company, she is sure to bring joy and companionship to the right family.

My cheeky little lady Topps has been with me for just over a month now and she’s come out of her shell SO much in that time. When she arrived on my section she really didn’t want anything to do with me and would more or less bark at me constantly. Progress has been slow and steady over the past few weeks, but now she’s very comfortable being around me, she’ll sit near me, she’ll take treats from me, she’ll give me little kisses and nudges with her nose, AND she’s just started to accept a little tickle under her ears when she’s feeling brave … which is huge!!! I’m super happy with how well she’s doing and it gives me great hope for her future. If she can progress this much in a kennel environment, just imagine what she could do in a home with her own humans!?Topps will still need a resident dog in her new home and still no children as I do think that would be too overwhelming for her. She may be quite worried when she first gets home, but with lots of reassurance and patience, I do think she will blossom in time. She really just needs somebody to take a chance on her now, and show her how beautiful life can actually be. She deserves the world and more, so please don’t keep her waiting much longer.

Topps has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is an extremely worried and shut down girl at the moment who is finding everything very overwhelming. She is very frightened of being handled, as she doesn’t yet understand that human hands can be gentle and loving.

Topps is looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs. She will need lots of patience, time and understanding to help her slowly come out of her shell.

She must have at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and take her under their wing. This will play a vital role in helping Topps build confidence and settle in to life in a loving home.

Topps has never lived in a home before, and she will likely find this new environment very overwhelming at first. She will need gentle support and encouragement as she begins to learn about house training, and her adopters will need to take things at her pace.

She does not yet walk on a lead and will need to start slowly, practicing in a secure garden once she is ready. Because of how fearful she currently is, a secure garden is essential for her safety and confidence building.

Topps has a long journey ahead of her, but with the right family, she has the potential to transform into a happy and content dog. If you have the time, love, and experience to help her on this journey, please consider offering Topps the second chance she so desperately deserves.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Uma
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy children who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk on a harness and would enjoy a daily walk when settled in to my new home.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

18-07-26 Uma is a gorgeous girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She can be a little shy when you first meet her, but it doesn't take long before her playful side begins to appear. After a few minutes, she'll often invite you to play with a sweet little play bow. Uma enjoys gentle handling and is happy to take treats from our hands, although she does appreciate people taking things slowly when picking her up. Her favourite thing is to sit right next to you for fusses

Uma loses confidence when she is away from her doggy friends, so she will need another kind and confident resident dog in the home to help her feel safe and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in. She has a lovely fun personality that's just waiting to come out. We would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy teenagers.

As Uma has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, practice her skills walking, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she adjusts to her new surroundings and discovers everything that home life has to offer.

Uma has arrived slightly overweight, so she will need a good diet and gentle exercise to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home.

Uma is a real sweetheart with so much potential. She's already showing us glimpses of the happy, playful dog she is, and with the support of another dog and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow.

Uma has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Davies

name: Kelly
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have a very overshot jaw, and I have been spayed.

Kelly is a lovely girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived, she was quite worried but she soon started to settle in and come out of her shell. She has since moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in well and experiencing home life for the first time.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home, where she can settle in at her own pace. She would love her adopters to be around most of the time and we would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy teenagers.

Kelly has taken to home life well andreally enjoys pottering around the garden and laying in the shade. She is also happy to take treats nicely and loves her food too! She is happy to accept a fuss, has a waggy little tail and is learning all about playing with toys too. She gets very excited to see her fosterers when they come downstairs in the morning, which is lovely.

Kelly loves other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her settle in to her new life.

She had never lived in a home before moving to foster, so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to learn all about home life. She is already doing well learning about house training. She has already learned how to walk on a lead and harness and we think she will really enjoy going for walks in quiet areas as she builds up her confidence.

She is a truly wonderful girl and we think that whoever adopts her is going to adore her!

She has arrived with an overshot jaw that does not bother her, but should be monitored in her new home to ensure she is comfortable.

Kelly has been given the Gift of Life by Hannah Wadsworth

Kelly arrived last Sunday and has settled really well in foster.  She enjoys pottering around the garden and lying in the shade - she has her favourite spots.

She has lived happily with our 4 small dogs and has been polite and friendly with all dogs she has met outside the home. She has been on two walks so far - on a longline so she can choose her pace and have a sniff in the shade - and she absolutely loves it.

In just a week she has progressed so well - she takes treats nicely and very gently and loves her food. She is accepting a fuss from us, starting to play with toys, wagging her tail and very pleased to see us when we come downstairs in the mornings.

It is great to see her look so relaxed and happy already. She is going to be a fabulous little addition to any household.

Kelly is a lovely girl who has come to us from a breeder. She would very much like to be your friend, but she is feeling a little worried and lacking in confidence at the moment.

She is still adjusting to her new surroundings and will need time, patience, and understanding to help her settle. We believe that with plenty of reassurance and gentle encouragement, Kelly will soon begin to come out of her shell and show her true personality.

Kelly will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home. Having a canine companion to look up to will help her learn about home life and continue to build her confidence. She can live with older dog-savvy teens who are sensible and allow her to settle in at her own pace.

As she has never lived in a home before, Kelly will need patient adopters who can help her learn all the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. To begin with, she may prefer gentle garden explorations while she gains confidence and gets used to her new environment.

Given the time, love, and support she needs, Kelly is sure to blossom into a wonderful companion. She is looking for a calm and understanding home where she can continue her journey and enjoy plenty of TLC.

name: Missie
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have an ear infection which is being treated & I have been spayed.

05-08-26 Missie is an apprehensive little soul who has come into our care from a breeder. She is easy to handle, but you can see that she feels uneasy about it and would much rather have all four paws back on the floor with her doggy friends.

Missie gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Missie has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and other basics of home life. Missie will need a quiet and calm home that she where she can learn about trust and companionship. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Missie is a gentle little girl who is simply looking for a calm, understanding family to help her feel safe again. With a friendly canine companion and plenty of patience, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy all the comforts that a loving home has to offer.

Missie has arrived with an ear infection. Our vets have flushed her ear and prescribed medication, and they will continue to monitor her while she is in our care.

Missie has been given the Gift of Life by Catherine Holcombe

name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

I'm fully vaccinated and have been neutered.

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

name: Holiday
description:
I need a quiet adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I’m frightened and will need a secure garden to learn about being outside.

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need a careful introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Holiday originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted and found a lovely home, but sadly it wasn't the right match for her as the resident dog wouldn't accept her, so she came back into our care. Holiday has since moved to a foster home where she is settling beautifully and continuing to learn all about life in a home.

Holiday is a very sensitive girl who had very little socialisation before coming into our care. When she first returned to us, she found people incredibly worrying and was very hand-shy. Her first instinct was always to run away, and she wasn't comfortable being picked up or handled. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could react by nipping out of fear, and she did nip her previous adopter once when she became overwhelmed during handling.

Holiday will still be looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with no visiting children. She will need adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who are happy to let her settle at her own pace, without pressure or expectations. She relies heavily on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her.

Since moving into foster care, Holiday has made some really lovely progress and is growing in confidence every week. She now happily comes into the sitting room and chooses to settle nearby while her foster family relax. She enjoys being part of family life and likes to know where everyone is, often coming to find them and quietly checking in throughout the day.

She is now happily taking treats from our hands and has recently started giving gentle little nose bumps to our hands, which is a wonderful sign that her trust is growing. She also greets us with a wagging tail and will happily sit and listen while we talk to her, maintaining eye contact. When she first arrived, she would run away as soon as anyone spoke to her, so this has been a huge milestone.

Although Holiday is becoming much more confident, she still isn't ready to be handled much and is not yet comfortable wearing a harness or going for walks. Her adopter will need to be happy to continue building her confidence at her own pace, allowing her to decide when she is ready for each new step.

Minus her brief adoption, Holiday had never lived in a home before, but she has settled brilliantly into foster care. She is now 99% clean in the house and has established a lovely routine. She absolutely adores the other dogs, taking great comfort from them and often following their lead. She enjoys spending time in the garden and small secure field, where she loves exploring, relaxing and watching the world go by. She has also been left at home with the other dogs for a few hours and has coped very well.

Holiday is a very special little girl who has already come such a long way. She is learning that people can be kind and that home life isn't so scary after all. She still has a journey ahead of her, but with plenty of patience, understanding and the support of another dog, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything her new life has to offer.

Holiday has been given the Gift of Life by Ellie Worron

Holiday has made some lovely progress since coming into foster care and is growing in confidence every week. She now happily comes into the sitting room and chooses to settle close by while we relax. She enjoys being part of family life and likes to know where we are, often coming to find us and checking in throughout the day.

She is happily taking treats from our hands and has recently started giving gentle little nose bumps to our hands, which is a wonderful sign that her trust is growing. She also wags her tail when she sees us and will happily listen while we talk to her, maintaining eye contact. When she first arrived, she would run away as soon as we spoke to her, so this is a huge milestone for her.

Holiday is now 99% clean in the house and has settled brilliantly into a routine. She absolutely adores the other dogs and takes great comfort from them, often following their lead. She loves spending time in the garden and our small field, where she enjoys exploring and relaxing.

At the moment, Holiday is not yet ready to wear a harness or go for walks, and she will need an adopter who is happy to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She is making steady progress and, with patience and kindness, continues to blossom.

Holiday is a very gentle, sweet little girl with the softest, kindest eyes. She has such a lovely nature, and it is a privilege to watch her confidence grow a little more each day.

Holiday has settled well into foster care. She is worried about being handled at the moment so we haven’t tried to stroke her or pick her up, we wanted to give her the chance to settle and feel safe first.

She will take treats from our hands, walk through doorways easily, even with us there, and she seeks us out if she doesn’t know where we are. This all indicates that it won’t be long until we can begin gentles strokes etc. When we are fussing our dogs she gets closer to watch and has touched my hand or sniffed my legs. Holiday is not as jumpy as I thought she would be, which is great, and we can walk quite close to her without her moving away.

When we are all settled in the evening, she comes into the sitting room to see where we all are and what we are doing. She isn’t phased by the TV and will often sit on a rug next to my chair.

We have a very small field which most new fosters are a bit scared of as they are not used to big spaces, Holiday loves spending time out there exploring and watching the other dogs play, we’ve even seen her do the odd little sprint!

She has been clean in the house and loves snuggling with the dogs at night in the kitchen, she is left overnight and we can go out for a couple of hours and she is fine as long as the dogs are with her too.

She has the potential to be the best dog and I don’t think it will be long before she is seeking attention and ready to try her harness again. She has very gentle eyes and you can see the sadness ebbing away a little more each day.

This week Holiday has been making lovely progress with lead work. We have been helping her get used to having a lead clipped onto her harness and trailing behind her, and she is becoming much more comfortable with this. Clipping the lead onto her harness is now far less of a concern for her, which is a big step forward, and when she is out in the yard she barely seems aware of it anymore.

She is also doing wonderfully with different people putting her harness on, which is a very significant achievement for Holiday given how sensitive she has been around handling. She is taking these steps in her stride and continues to make really encouraging progress.

Recently, I’ve been spending some dedicated time working with Holiday, and she’s making such lovely progress. She’s beginning to trust me more each day and has even allowed me to gently put a harness on her. Everything is done slowly and at her pace, with plenty of treats and reassurance, but this is a huge milestone for this sensitive girl.

We’ve also been working on gentle touch, always on her terms. When she chooses to come and sit beside me in her bed, we take things one small step at a time, building her confidence with each positive experience (and a few tasty rewards along the way!).

Holiday is starting to show more of her personality now. She’s often one of the first up for a treat and has even begun wagging her tail. It might sound like a small thing, but for Holiday, it’s truly something special.

She’s a wonderful dog who just needs a patient, understanding home where she can continue to grow in confidence and feel safe. Watching her come out of her shell is incredibly rewarding, and she’s so ready for someone to give her the love she deserves.

I am writing this update as someone who has not had much interaction with Holiday although I have worked with her on a few occasions. It is obvious from her previous update that there has been progress in her coming out of her shell and I was surprised to discover that Holiday would accept treats from my hand although when trying to smooth her coat, Holiday swiftly moved out of reach.

She is getting there but slowy and anyone wanting to adopt her will need to go slowly and earn that important trust. Holiday's regular carer can stroke Holiday when she is settled in a bed but only in one place. If a position is changed, Holiday will become scared and move.

It is apparent after speaking with Holiday's regular carer that for Holiday to make that important next step in her progress, it would be better for her to be in a home situation. Holiday is fantastic with other dogs and would definitely need to live with at least one other dog to give her that hope of progress and comfort. There is always someone out there for every dog and vice versa Holiday is waiting.

Holiday originally came to us from a breeder a few months ago. She was adopted and found a lovely home, but sadly it wasn't the right match for her and the resident dog wouldn't accept her, so she is now back in our care.

Holiday is a very scared girl who is very overwhelmed to find herself here and clearly hasn't had much socialisation before. She finds human interaction quite difficult at the moment and is very hand-shy, so she will need a patient and understanding home that can help her come out of her shell at her own pace. Holiday will run away from you when you enter her kennel and isn't keen on being picked up or handled. She finds this so scary, that if she feels like she is being pushed out of her comfort zone she can choose nip or bite, purely through fear. She did bite her previous adopter once when she was being handled as she became so worried.

For this reason, Holiday will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where there are no visiting children. She will need adopters who hav experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will let her settle in slowly at her own pace with no pressure or expectations.

Holiday finds comfort and reassurance from the company of her canine friends and so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing. This dog will need to allow her to snuggle up to them and will need to be happy for her to follow them around. A kind resident dog will be an important source of reassurance and companionship for her as she adjusts to her new life.

Although she spent some time in foster and was adopted for a short period, she had never lived in a home before this, so Holiday will still need to learn all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn to walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice wearing these around the home and garden, once her confidence with handling has grown a little more. She will then need to practice walking around the garden until she is confident enough to venture further.

Since arriving back with us, Holiday has started to make some more progress and will now take a treat from our hands as long as she has a doggy friend next to her for support. With time, love and patience she will start to leave her past behind her and will truly start to blossom. Holiday's journey won't be a short one, but it will be so worth it when you see her tail wag for the first time or when she first willingly accepts some fuss and attention. In the right home, she will thrive, so please don't keep her waiting too long.

name: Trixie
description:
I'll need an adult only home with adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs.

I am looking for a home where I can be the only dog & get all the love and attention.

I need an extra secure garden and home that can accommodate my needs.

I walk on a lead but will need my adopters to be extra secure.

I understand toilet training, but will need a reminder in a new home!

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home! Read below for more info!

Trixie is a very sweet lady who has come to us from a breeder in search of a new start. Although her tail is constantly wagging, she will shyly approach for a gentle fuss and tends to stay away and watch from a distance until she feels safe. Once she builds trust, she is affectionate and will enjoy a snuggle and a gentle fuss.

In foster, she shown herself to be a nervous girl in new environments who still needed encouragement to engage with new people. She would often hang back and observe, but once more secure she would come forward for interaction and enjoy fuss and attention from her fosterer.

Despite the fact that she is still a nervous girl, she also isn't keen on sharing her home with other dogs and so we feel she would be happiest as an only dog in her new home. Although she has been in foster with other dogs, she can be jealous when her fosterer is showing attention to other dogs and has reacted towards them on occasion. She is fine with socialising with other calm dogs, but can be reactive towards barking or yappy dogs ordogs that are in her face too much or too boisterous.For this reason, we feel she would be best suited to an adult only home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs. She has met cats fine, but due to her tendency to become jealous, we would not look to home her with cats.

In the garden, she has shown signs of digging and has previously tried to escape a foster home, so very secure boundaries are essential. Her new home will need to have 6ft minimum fencing height and her new adopters will need to keep her on lead in the garden until she gains confidence outside. She might enjoy having a sand pit to play in so she can enjoy digging in appropriate areas.

Trixie had been mostly clean in the house in her foster home, and seemed to be a star at toilet training. However, she may need some reminders in her new home as she settles in new surroundings.

She is walking on a lead and harness, but can still become startled and may try to back out if frightened. She needs experienced adopters, a secure garden (6ft+ fencing) as she has been digging in her foster garden, and additional safety measures indoors.

She will need a calm, secure, adult-only home and a gentle introduction to home life.

She has had a small lump removed from her left mammary gland and is recovering well.

Trixie has been given the Gift of Life by Tanya Player

Hello, my name is Trixie and I'm living at Many Tears whilst I wait for my forever home to find me.

My perfect home would be with lovely, gentle people, that enjoy a quiet life. I am easily worried by new sounds and loud noises and so I will need lots of time to adjust to my new home and environment. I love a squishy bed to lie on and one of those sofas I hear about sounds perfect to try.

I would be very happy in a secure garden where I won’t be bothered by other people, just my family, sitting with me and a few toys for little plays. Perhaps when I get used to my new people we could go for walks in quiet places together - but I will need time before I’m fully ready to do this.

I enjoy my food, so a good supply of tasty meals would make me very happy. I really don’t want much just a simple, safe and loving home.

Side note from my kennel mum:Trixie is a wonderful loving dog once she feels safe with you. She is a flight risk when startled - and she is easily startled!

If every day was a Trixie day, life would be lovely. Trixie is the sweetest and loveliest of dogs. Her favourite pastimes include tummy rubs and cuddles, and if there’s a home out there with a Trixie-sized spot on the sofa and a human to shower her with fusses, she would be in heaven.

When Trixie is happy, you know it, and she will bounce around you outside for a little play before parking herself next to you for more belly rubs. She loves sitting outside and just relaxing with you.

Trixie does also enjoy a walk (in very quiet areas); however, she can be very, very easily spooked and, if startled, will bolt and has done so previously. Any adopters would need to be very aware of this and work on building her confidence at home before considering outings. Adopters will also need to ensure a very secure setup for her at home, i.e. secure entrances and exits from the house.

Trixie prefers to have a human all to herself and, for this reason, she would like to be the only dog with a human who will be home most of the time.

Trixie truly is a gem of a girl with a heart of gold. A special and sweet lady, who longs for safe hands (and laps) to snuggle into. This super dog needs a little time and a lot of security,  give her that and you will have a bond for life.

Trixie is looking for a home that is quiet, gentle, patient and super secure on a practical level. Trixie is incredibly spooky and even if she trusts you, the slightest of frights in her environment and she will bolt. Because Trixie is a high flight risk she would be suited to a dog experienced home, ideally with knowledge of flighty and/or ex-breeding dogs.

It’s important that her new people have a secure plan for getting her out of the car on arrival home after adoption and are able to keep entrance and exits to the house escape safe. In return for your kindness Trixie will be the cutest of best friends. Trixie is looking to be the only dog and is suited to an adult home with no visiting children.

Trixie has been in foster with me for three weeks now and is settling into our routine fairly well.

When she first arrived, Trixie was very human-oriented and showed signs of jealousy towards other dogs, which led to a few altercations. She would often growl if another dog came close to me, as she wanted all the attention for herself. This is something we’ve been working on, but we still feel it is best if she is homed as an only dog in her new home.

From her interactions with my resident dogs, it’s clear that Trixie isn’t comfortable with small, yappy dogs. She does seem to prefer female human company, although she is continuing to build confidence more generally. She currently sleeps downstairs in an open, covered crate, which she uses as her safe space.

For the first couple of weeks, Trixie has slept downstairs quietly through the night with no accidents. Over the last few nights, she has been a little more unsettled and has had a couple of accidents, which seems to be linked to wanting more human attention.

Trixie is fed on dry Arden Grange and is currently fed separately, as she will try to eat other dogs’ food if given the chance. She was also caught eating poo, so I have started soaking her food in hot water and letting it cool, which she seems to prefer.

In her first week, Trixie did try digging in the garden and looking for ways to escape, but this behaviour has now settled. She clearly recognises me and gets very excited when she sees me, running over happily for fuss and attention.

She has been out on walks and does reasonably well when accompanied by another dog, but she is still quite flighty and easily startled. For now, she should only be walked in secure areas, as she will try to back out of her harness if she feels unsure and has demonstrated this once already.

Trixie can be complex at times, so she will need a calm, experienced adopter who understands nervous, ex-breeding dogs and can handle her with patience and care. It will be important to give her time to settle at home and build trust before introducing too many new experiences, especially.

Trixie absolutely craves human attention and is happiest curled up next to me on the sofa. As her confidence continues to grow and her jealousy is managed, she has all the makings of a very loyal and loving companion who simply wants to feel safe and adored.

Trixie is now in foster and is settling in well. She travelled well and was clean on arrival with no issues noted in the car or on entering the home.

Once in the foster home, Trixie has shown herself to be a very nervous little girl who is still unsure of new environments and needs encouragement to engage with people. She will often hang back and watch, but once she feels a bit more secure she will come forward and seek interaction. On these occasions she has chosen to snuggle close to me and will sit gazing and enjoying contact, although she does need to be gently encouraged each time as confidence doesn’t yet seem consistent.

It has quickly become apparent that Trixie is quite a complex girl in the home. She is very focused on attention and has already shown signs of jealousy when sharing human interaction. On one occasion, when another foster dog came onto the sofa, Trixie reacted strongly and became defensive. She can also be particular about other dogs in general and can be especially reactive to barking dogs, and has shown a clear dislike of a small dachshund in the home. For this reason, she will now be looking for a home as an only dog where she can get all of the attention for herself.

Outside of this, she is an active little girl and has already shown she is a determined digger, having previously managed to dig under fencing and patio areas. This will need careful management going forward with very secure boundaries required.

Overall, Trixie is settling in but is still very much finding her feet.

name: Carry
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & have a Grade 3 patella luxation in my right hind leg.

Carry is a sweet and gentle girl who came to us from a breeder looking for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very scared and unsure of people, but she has already made wonderful progress and is continuing to grow in confidence since moving into foster care.

Carry has settled well into life in a home and is taking all the sights and sounds of everyday living in her stride. She sleeps soundly with the other dogs in the lounge each night and has settled into a good routine, although she is quite happy to let her foster carer know when she thinks it's time to start the day! She has a great appetite, happily accepts treats from your hand, and has been generally clean in the house.

Carry is still nervous of being touched and will often run away if someone tries to fuss her. However, she is becoming much braver and will now happily approach to sniff hands. If she is relaxing on a dog bed or in a smaller space where she feels safe, she is beginning to tolerate gentle fusses. She is trying so hard to be brave, and it has been lovely to watch her confidence slowly grow.

Carry relies heavily on other dogs for reassurance and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her forever home. They will help guide her through new experiences and continue to build her confidence as she settles into family life. She has also started taking her first steps with lead training and recently allowed her foster carer to attach a lead to her collar and enjoy a little walk around the garden, with plenty of encouragement and a generous supply of squeezy cheese!

She has also discovered the joy of playing with soft toys and can often be found happily throwing them around and giving them a good shred. Seeing her playful side emerge has been a wonderful milestone and shows just how much she is beginning to relax.

Carry will be looking for a calm and understanding home with resident dog companions and patient adopters who are happy to let her progress entirely at her own pace. We feel she could live with older, dog-savvy children who understand that she will need time and space to build trust. As she is in a foster home, she is beginning to learn about home life. But her adopters will need to continue helping her with house training, lead walking, and all the other adventures that family life brings.

Carry is an adorable little girl who is trying so hard to overcome her fears. She brightens the day of everyone who meets her, and with continued patience, kindness, and reassurance, we know she will continue to blossom into a happy and trusting companion.

Our vets have noted that Carry has a Grade 3 patella luxation in her right hind leg. This is not causing her any issues at present and may improve with gentle exercise, but it will need to be monitored by her adopters and their veterinary team. Should treatment be required in the future, this condition would not be covered by insurance.

Carry has been given the Gift of Life by Wendy Bowen

Carry has begun to settle into life in a home, she is accepting of the sights and sounds of home life. She sleeps well with the others in the lounge, but let's me know when she thinks I ought to get up, about 6.30.

Carry eats well, accepts treats from my hand and is generally clean in the house.Carry will come up to me and sniff my hands but runs away if I try to fuss her. If she is sitting on a bed or in a smaller area, she is starting to tolerate gentle fuss. She is trying so hard to be brave. Today she did allow me to attach a lead to her collar and have a walk round the garden aided by squeezy cheese!! She is starting to play with soft toys, ripping them and tossing them about, so lovely to see.

Carry will need a home with a resident dog/s, older children and adopters who are happy to go at her pace. She is an adorable girl and deserves the best

I’m lucky enough to get to work with Carry twice a week whilst her kennel mum is off for the weekend, and every week I get to spend with her the more in confidence she grows!Carry is such a character, and everyday she shows you how much she is blossoming and how much she appreciates feeling safe & loved. She absolutely loves cuddling up to her kennel friends, and tearing it up in the yard and the kennel. Her one true love is toys, and as long as you have toys around you needn’t worry if she is happy or satisfied!!We recently took Carry out on a harness for the first time, and as a beginner we think she smashed it. She didn’t freak out, and simply followed the lead of her kennel mum & another dog by her side. We think with another few more goes she will be enjoying her small adventures in no time. Carry broke up the walk with a few stops for some squeezey cheese which she simply couldn’t say no to!Carry is such an adoring girl, and watching her flourish infront of our eyes is so beautiful to watch. A loving family, a resident dog, and lots of understanding is all she needs, and she’ll be ready to take on the world, day by day & little by little.

Carry is coming out of her shell more and more every day and is now a very happy and lively girl who always has a waggy tail. She’s discovered toys and is learning how to play with them which she’s really enjoying, and she’s also turning into a massive foodie which is always very helpful with nervous dogs. She is still hand shy and will run away if I go towards her, but she’s extremely curious and always likes to be close to me watching what I’m doing. She’s happy to approach me to give me lots of sniffs and to take treats from my hand, so we’re definitely moving in the right direction and I really don’t think it’s going to be long until she starts to accept gentle fusses.

Carry is the type of dog that can put a smile on your face even on the darkest of days, and she really is a joy to work with and be around. In a home environment where she has lots of time with her new parents, I think she’ll absolutely blossom. She probably will be nervous at first of course, so as long as her adopters are patient with her and work with her through her worries and fears, I think it will work out so well.

I haven’t started harness training with Carry yet as she hasn’t been on my section for that long, but I do feel as though she may be ready to start exploring it soon. So, over the next couple of weeks I’ll get one fitted to her and see how she does. I’ll keep you all updated!

Carry is a sweet, gentle girl who has come to us from a breeder and is currently very scared, timid, and unsure of humans. She will need plenty of time, patience, and TLC in her new home to help her learn to trust and build a loving bond with her family. Once she gets to know you, she will approach you for a fuss but she isn't comfortable being picked up at the moment as this is very new for her.

Carry will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She relies on other dogs for comfort and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home. A canine companion will provide her with reassurance and help guide her as she learns about home life, giving her someone to lean on as her confidence grows.

As Carry has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be understanding while she learns the basics, such as house training and walking on a lead. The big wide world may feel overwhelming for her at first, so starting with calm, gentle experiences, like exploring the garden will help her gradually gain confidence.

With love, patience, and understanding, Carry has all the potential to blossom into a happy and trusting companion.

Our vets have noted that Carry has a Grade 3 patella luxation in her right hind leg, this isn't causing her any issues at the moment and may improve with gentle exercise but it will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vets and should she need any treatment in the future it wouldn't be coverable by insurance.
