name: Siwan
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have a Grade 1 heart murmur, and have had 2 teeth removed.

24-07-26 Siwan has come to us from a breeder and is a gentle girl who just wants to please. She is easy to handle and isn't overly frightened, although she is clearly not used to human attention yet. She is still learning to trust people, but her curious nature is beginning to shine through.

Siwan takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need a home with at least one kind, confident resident dog that she can look to for reassurance as she settles into home life and continues to build her confidence.

As Siwan has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns about house training, lead walking, and all the routines that come with family life. With gentle guidance and encouragement, we are sure she will continue to grow in confidence.

Siwan is a kind, sweet-natured girl who has so much potential. All she needs is a loving home and someone willing to help her come out of her shell, and she will make a wonderful companion.

Siwan has arrived with a Grade 1 heart murmur that will need to be monitored in her new home. She has had 2 teeth removed at the time of her spay.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Flash
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with ex-breeding experience to understand me

I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a good sized, secure garden to explore.

I can walk on a lead but find this very overwhelming at the moment.

I have entropion in both eyes, which have been repaired by the vets.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle with a big personality, a sensitive soul, and an oversized puppy spirit. He first came to us after his previous owners could no longer give him the time and exercise he needed. Since then, we’ve watched him grow from a worried boy into a much more confident and affectionate companion, and he continues to make us proud every single day.

Flash is still very much a character, goofy, playful, and full of energy but beneath his bouncy exterior lies a gentle heart that just wants to love and be loved. He can be sensitive in new situations and still finds the world a little overwhelming at times, but with people he trusts, his sweet and loyal nature shines through. Once Flash bonds with you, he is yours for life.

Recently, he’s been showing us more of his loving side. On rainy days when we huddle together out of the downpour, he rolls over for belly rubs, brings his toys for attention, and happily drifts off to sleep during a cuddle. It’s in these quiet moments that his true personality comes out, affectionate, trusting, and eager to please.

Flash’s training is going from strength to strength. He’s mastered “touch” (booping his nose to your hand) and is now learning “place.” He still gets a little mouthy when he’s overexcited, but he’s come a long way since his arrival and continues to improve with patience and consistency. He’ll need his future family to have ex-breeding experience and to continue this gentle guidance in the home so he can keep building on all the progress he’s made.

Being an active breed, Flash loves his walks and enjoys exploring the world at his own pace. He’s happiest in calm, quiet areas where he can relax and take everything in without feeling rushed. He will need to be the only pet in the home, as he prefers human companionship over other animals, and he’s not a fan of pigeons or seagulls either!

Flash has had successful surgery for entropion in both eyes, he received care for mild dermatitis around both eyes, but this has since cleared. He is currently being treated for sore and sensitive ears.

What Flash truly needs now is a calm, understanding, adult-only home with ex-breeding experience and with someone who’s around most of the time, someone who can offer him patience, structure, and all the love he deserves. With time and trust, Flash will repay his person a hundred times over with loyalty, affection, and that special spark that makes him so unforgettable.

Please don’t overlook this beautiful boy. Flash has come so far and is ready to start the next chapter of his life he’s just waiting for that one person to believe in him and bring him home.

Flash will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Flash has officially been waiting for a home for a whole year. After a first few months of (a lot of) patience and training, it's then blossomed into the most incredible remaining months where we’ve really seen Flash’s true heart and soul. This dog is phenomenal in more ways than one, and it’s so sad he’s now become part of the MT furniture, and that the rescue has now become his home.

So for Flash’s 1 year anniversary, I took him off site to the nearby country park for a lovely stroll, followed by a visit to McD’s for some chicken nuggets.

Flash was suuuuuuch a good boy on his walk. He took in all the new smells, and took the new environment in his stride. He was even approached by 3 off lead small dogs, and didn’t react at all. He trotted along the park, with the world at his feet and it was the most amazing thing to see.

He is an absolute darling in the car, so we made a swift visit to McD’s for a box of 20 nuggets to eat together in our on site flat.

It was so nice to see Flash in a home like environment, he jumped straight on the sofa, and wandered around inspecting every room. We sat on the floor together eating our nuggets, and he eventually rested on the raised bed and had a little snooze.

It was heartbreaking putting him back in his kennel, when he seemed so at peace and settled in the flat. I just wish there was someone out there who could see him for everything he is and more!!!

Our beautiful, bonkers Flash has learnt a new trick and we thought we would share.

Flash has also been enjoying the sunshine with lots of walks and plays in the yards this week.

Flash continues to work hard on growing his calmness around new people and he is doing ok. He has now been 10 months here at the rescue and has an increasing fan base amongst the staff but he of course longs for a home and people of his own.

When I first started working with him, I was apprehensive. He was a much larger dog than I was used to working with, and he would mouth you til his hearts content. Not because he is a nasty dog, or means any harm whatsoever, but simply because he has come from a home (just out of puppyhood) and he has become extremely anxious and unsettled being in a kennel environment. On top of that, he has been taught 0 manners which definitely didn’t help with the matter!!! I struggled to bond with him, I struggled to understand why he wouldn’t listen when being told, and why all he wanted to do was treat my arm like a toy…

However I found myself thinking, what has Flash been through in his life that was ever HIS fault? He didn’t ask to spend so much of his life in kennels. He never asked to be put in situations where his anxiety gets the better of him, it was never his decision to not be trained to behave normally. So I decided to buck up my ideas and realise he’s not as scary as he seems, and he’s probably just as anxious being around me as I was him. And from that moment on, our relationship has blossomed…

This boy is truly a superstar in every sense of the word. He is SUCH a goofball, and can have you in fits of laughter within seconds of being with him. His personality is infectious, and as soon as he is comfortable with you and realises you are no threat to him, he shines like the star he is. It’s gutting that Flash doesn’t allow every staff member to see all sides of him. The side that shows his softness, his sweetness, his kindness. But that just makes me so much more grateful that he feels comfortable enough around me to do so.

You can see from his pictures, Flash is muzzle trained. Not because he is an aggressive dog, not because he is a violent dog, it’s simply due to his anxiousness. On one hand, Flash is a super intelligent Poodle but on the other hand, he doesn’t really show it. His anxiety gets the better of him, and he puts himself in uncomfortable positions with new people & then panics whilst he’s in it. It is SUPER important that whoever adopts Flash’s main priority is keeping him safe, and keeping him from making decisions that he feels uncertain about. He wants to make friends with everyone, but also decides halfway through some interactions that he’s not to keen on the thought too!

Among (of course) all of the other precious angels I look after the rescue, Flash is one of the reasons I get excited to go to work. You shouldn’t really have favourites, but Flash does take the cake. I cherish every single moment I get with him. Our lovely strolls up the country lanes, our snuggles in the back of his kennel after a long day, our zoomies down our big play yard. Every single moment & memory I look forward to recreating every single day. Nothing tops being around this dog, nothing else matters when you’re with Flash.

If I was in a position to take him home & work with him through his quirks, I absolutely would, in heartbeat in fact. There is just something so special about him, and I truly envy whoever is fortunate to adopt this incredible young man. And for as long as Flash remains in kennels, I will advocate for him, make him feel safe, comfortable and most of all loved.

Flash has completely changed my mind about Poodles. I am absolutely in love with him. He might not be the sharpest boy in the bunch, but he more than makes up for it with his goofy charm and endless silliness.We are still working on his mouthing when he becomes overexcited. Progress is steady, and every small step forward feels like a real achievement. Flash loves his freedom. We take daily trips to the big yard where he runs around like the happiest whirlwind you have ever seen. He would really benefit from visits to private dog fields where he can safely zoom and explore to his heart’s content.Meeting new people can still be a little tricky for him, but we have a careful plan in place to help him do so safely and comfortably. For those of us who know Flash well, he shows a side many would not expect. Beneath his anxiousness and the need for a muzzle at times is the sweetest, softest boy who adores snuggles and head tickles.He loves to stay close, gently resting his head in your lap until he drifts off to sleep. At the end of each day, we share a quiet moment together, curled up side by side until his eyes close and he is peacefully dreaming.Flash truly is a special boy who deserves a very special home. He needs someone who can offer love, patience, and understanding. In return, he will give unwavering loyalty and companionship for life.

Flash is an absolute character, this boy is full of life and once he knows you he adores you but his introductions to new people always need to be slow as this sensitive boy can be easily overwhelmed.

Flash works well within a routine, he has an abundance of energy and a super inquisitive nature which can sometimes lead to him becoming quite lively, he will often revert to ‘mouthing’ and jumping up when he is uncomfortable or unsure.

Flash has a super inquisitive nature and loves to observe what’s going on at a distance. This boy can also be an absolute cuddle monster and adores a snuggle with his favourite people, and will fall asleep next to us when we have the opportunity to sit quietly with him. One of flash’s unique traits is his love of a pamper session! I have never known a dog who enjoys a bath and hairdryer the way he does and he becomes quite docile under the hair dryer whilst having a gentle brush.

Flash’s ideal home would be a quiet an experienced dog owning home (adults only) with humans that have the patience and time to help grow his confidence and who also understand the need to grow calmness in him. Flash has had a few dog friends at the rescue but his high spirted nature can be a bit much for some dogs and he does not seem to like male dogs, for this reason a home where he is the only pooch would suit him best.

Flash walks well on lead but can become very excited when he sees other dogs, walks in quiet areas would be perfect for him, he loves to be outdoors and often just enjoys sitting in the yard with me watching birds, but he will equally enjoy time spent just hanging out with his humans at home. Flash really is a wonderfully, lovable, giant puppy, looking for kind and understanding humans to provide him with the security and love he deserves.

Flash has had a brilliant few weeks. He celebrated his second Birthday and was treated with his first snow day, which he loved frolicking about in. Unfortunately, he did have to spend his birthday in kennels, but I made sure it was still a very special day for him. We hopped in the car, and I took him for a little walk before heading to the pet shop to pick out some birthday treats. He chose a dinosaur toy and a knuckle bone, which he thoroughly enjoyed. I also bought him some special birthday biscuits to keep him going through the week.

After that, I truly spoiled him, and we decided to go to Burger King for a burger! Flash was quite confused at first, but once he had a taste, he couldn’t get enough.

Flash truly is a special boy and will need a special home to match. He can be very wary of strangers and doesn’t always show clear signs if he’s uncomfortable. For this reason, he is muzzled when out on walks, which I make sure to do whenever we go out.

Flash will need an adult-only home with no visiting children. He cannot live with cats or any small animals

The stunning Flash had a little pamper today, which he absolutely loved. He was as good as gold whilst in the bath and sat very contentedly on the grooming table looking out the window enjoying the warmth of the blowers. I have never known a dog to enjoy bath time as much as he does, he becomes quite sleepy and cuddley, it’s the cutest thing.

After his wash and blow dry he got to open some Christmas treats out in the yard sent in from the lovely folks out there that support Many Tears, Flash particular enjoyed the food presents.

Flash really is the most wonderful boy once you get to know him, and we see improvement every day in his sometimes lively and skittish nature. This fantastic boy will make the most awesome and loyal of friend with the person or couple that are prepared to put the time and love into him he so deserves.

Today, Flash and I went on a little adventure to the local pet shop, finishing off with a much-needed pupcup! He was an absolute angel in the car—he hopped right in, buckled up, and sat calmly for the whole journey. I watched him in the mirror as he gazed out at the world passing by. When we arrived, we popped his muzzle on as a precaution since he can sometimes be wary of strangers. Flash wandered around the shop, taking in all the sights and smells, until he discovered the pick-and-mix treats—which of course we had to get. After choosing his goodies, he rummaged through the plushies and picked out a squeaky monkey to take home.

As we headed toward the till, another dog suddenly rushed around a corner and startled Flash, causing him to react. I managed to whisk him away with a distraction, but he became very on edge and tucked himself into me for comfort. A lovely lady then came around the opposite corner and, despite having seen his reaction, kindly stopped to say hello. She happened to be a previous Many Tears adopter, and her own pup is doing wonderfully. She chose to ignore Flash at first to give him space, and once he settled, he allowed her to gently stroke his head. After wishing us well, we carried on with our day.

We sat outside Costa in the sunshine, and Flash absolutely loved his pupcup, so much so that he managed to get it all over his nose.

I’m incredibly proud of Flash today. It was his first outing since arriving in kennels, and I could really see how scared he can be underneath it all, and how much he relies on his human for reassurance. Flash needs someone devoted, patient, and willing to put time into training and working through his reactivity toward other dogs. He truly is a special boy.

Another bleak day at the rescue with the rain pouring down non-stop, but it meant I got to spend some more quality time with the dogsI’ve never been one for poodles but Flash really has stolen my heartToday I really did see his loving and caring side as we cuddled away from the downpour. He rolled around, brought me his toys and chews before receiving belly rubs and head scratches until he fell asleep

If you’ve been to the rescue I’m usually walking Flash around the reception area in order for him to build his relationship with humans and other dogs but it was nice to just have some one on one time with him today, once you’ve created a bond with this boy he is yours for life.Flash’s’ training is still continuing and has managed to learn ‘touch’ where he boops his nose to the designated hand and is in the midst of learning ‘place’.

In a home will still need some training in order for him to thrive.

Flash is still a little mouthy when he gets super excited but is doing much better to when he first arrived with us.

It's been almost 4 months since Flash arrived here and I feel he has been very much overlooked. Deep down he’s a big cuddle bug and thrives on attention.

I tried spending most of my time with him today as kennel life is very stressful for him. We visited the big yard multiple times, went for a stroll and even met 2 dogs on a walk and greeted them with such kindness. Might I say he walks beautifully alongside you!

We met some new people in the reception area, which can sometimes make Flash a little uneasy but he did fantastically and even accepted some treats. For this he is muzzle trained as he can be mouthy when he’s a little too excited!

The last task of the day was to be groomed. I never thought I would see this boy sit still for more than a few seconds, but he amazed me and hopped up onto the grooming table ready to be pampered! And he now looks so good! Flash really doesn’t mind being groomed which will be helpful for the future.

I absolutely adore this beautiful boy. Flash is best described as an oversized puppy at heart. He has a playful, goofy nature but sometimes forgets his size, which can make him a little overexcited and mouthy, especially if he’s unsure or feeling frustrated.

Flash can be a sensitive soul who is often scared of his own shadow and needs plenty of reassurance and gentle confidence-building when faced with new experiences (like the umbrella he discovered today!). Because of this, kennel life is very tough for him, and I truly believe he will thrive so much more in a loving home.

Once Flash trusts you, he shows his affectionate side. He adores snuggling in for a cuddle and loves being pampered.

Flash’s ideal home would be an adult-only household where he can be the only dog. He isn’t aggressive with other dogs but can become boisterous and overwhelming. A quiet location with a secure, good-sized garden would be perfect, ideally with adopters who enjoy long walks and hikes.

He walks beautifully on the lead, enjoys all weathers, and has the stamina to go for hours. While he may sometimes react to new situations or get excitable around other dogs, his confidence and manners are improving every day. Flash will need adopters who are home most of the time or able to include him in their daily lives, as he finds being left alone difficult and may struggle with separation anxiety.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle who has come to us from a home as his owners no longer had time for him and couldn't offer him the exercise he requires. Although he has lived in a home before, Flash is a worried boy who finds new experiences and people quite daunting. Because of this, Flash is looking for an experienced, adult only home with adopters who have plenty of time, patience, and love to give. He needs adopters who won’t give up on him and who will allow him to settle in at his own pace.Initially, Flash can be wary of new people and unsure of their intentions, but once you’ve gained his trust, he begins to show his affectionate and loyal nature. He forms strong bonds with those he feels safe around and shows a deep need for companionship. He does not cope well with being left alone and has shown signs of separation anxiety, getting very worried and anxious when left on his own. He will need an adopter who is able to be with him all of the time and who will work on this with him, slowly building up any time he is left. We are told he was crate trained in his previous home, which may help with this process.Flash is particularly sensitive to loud or sudden noises, which can cause him to panic. He feels safest in quiet, familiar surroundings and finds walks outside of the rescue grounds very difficult at the moment. When taken beyond his comfort zone, he becomes overwhelmed and spins in circles in an attempt to return to safety. While he can walk on a lead, his adopters will need to help him grow in confidence very gradually and may need to begin with simply enjoying time in the garden or short walks in peaceful areas.Flash would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as he can be grumbly when meeting other dogs. This is something his adopters will need to work on with him with patience and positive reinforcement. Because of this, he must only be allowed off lead in secure areas with no other dogs present. He also cannot live with cats or small animals and we are told he isn't a fan of pigeons or seagulls.Flash will be looking for a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and where his adopters will help him settle into a consistent routine so he can feel safe and secure. We are told that he is house trained but he may need some reminders of this in his new homeAlthough he is currently worried about going for walks, he is an active breed who will need to be kept both mentally and physically stimulated. We have been told that he has previously done some agility and scent work, so once his confidence grows this is something he may like to explore again in the future. His previous owners also said he enjoyed being groomed and bathed, though we haven’t yet introduced this at the rescue.This beautiful boy has so much potential in the right hands. If you have the time, experience, and understanding to give Flash the security and stability he needs, he will reward you with trust, loyalty, and love. Please don’t overlook him, he’s waiting for that one special person to believe in him.Flash has an entropion in both eyes, which has been repaired by our vets but does have some dermatitis around his eyes.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Ureka
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

18-07-26 Ureka has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home with adopters who can help her learn that the world isn't such a scary place.

Ureka is a very worried little girl who has found the transition into rescue life incredibly overwhelming. She is struggling to settle into kennel life at the moment and can spin in her kennel when she is feeling anxious. To help her, she has spent time visiting one of our quieter offices with another dog for company. Although she didn't show any signs of spinning while she was there, she still found it difficult to settle.

Although Ureka is finding things very overwhelming right now, we believe that in the right home she will thrive. She will need experienced adopters who understand the needs of very scared ex-breeding dogs and who are prepared to let her settle entirely at her own pace, without any expectations. She will be looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home where she can begin to feel safe and secure. She will also need at least one other kind and confident resident dog who can show her the ropes and help her build confidence as she adjusts to her new life.

As Ureka has never lived in a home before, everything will be completely new to her. She will need patient and understanding adopters who can gently guide her through all the things most dogs take for granted, including housetraining, household routines and learning that people can be trusted. She is beginning to learn to walk on a lead and harness and is doing well, but she will need plenty more time and practice to help her gain confidence.

Ureka's journey won't be a quick one, but for someone willing to give her the time, understanding and TLC she needs, watching her slowly discover the joys of home life will be incredibly rewarding. She deserves the chance to leave her worries behind and finally experience the happy, secure life every dog should have.

Ureka has been given the Gift of Life by Victoria Henstock

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Yoshi
description:
I will need an understanding home, that will allow me to come out of my shell.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and no cats please!

I can be a little nervous, and will need a secure garden to learn about the outdoors.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

18-07-26 Yoshi is a sweet little lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is friendly but understandably nervous and is looking for a patient, understanding family who can help her come out of her shell at her own pace.

Yoshi loves to snuggle up with her kennel friends and takes a lot of comfort from being around other dogs. Because of this, she will need a home with at least one kind, confident resident dog who can help her feel safe as she continues to build her confidence and learn to trust but she cannot live with cats!

She can be a little worried when exploring the play yard and new environments, so her adopters will need to be patient and allow her to take things at her own speed. She has never lived in a home before so will need to learn all about life in a home, including house training, so her new family should be prepared to support her through this with kindness and consistency.

Yoshi is a tiny, gentle, inquisitive little lady with so much potential. With time, patience, and the reassurance of a canine companion, we're sure she will blossom into a wonderful, loving companion.

Yoshi has been given the Gift of Life by Will Bithell

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Derby
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 22 teeth extracted and will need some mammary lumps removed.

29-07-26 Please meet Derby. She has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving forever home where she can begin to enjoy the life she has always deserved.

Derby is a shy little girl with the most gentle nature. Although she can be a little unsure at first, she will quietly come over to say hello and is easy to handle. She has a lovely, sweet temperament and is already showing that, with a little patience and reassurance, she is keen to learn that people can be kind.

Derby is looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need patient adopters who understand that she has never experienced life in a home before and will need time to adjust to all the new sights, sounds and routines that come with family life.

A kind and confident resident dog will be essential for Derby, as she will take comfort from having a canine friend to help guide her and build her confidence. She could also live with sensible, dog-savvy older teenagers aged 16 years and over who will give her the space and understanding she needs while she settles.

Derby has never lived in a home before, so she will need help with house training and learning all about home life. She will also need to learn to walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice around the home and garden before venturing further.

Derby is a truly lovely little girl and with love and TLC, we think she will truly blossom.

She has had a dental and had 22 teeth removed, so will need a soft food diet moving forwards. She has an undershot jaw, but this doesn't bother her. Our vets have noted that she has a few mammary lumps, which will be removed.

Derby has been given the Gift of Life by Faith Harrison

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Grape
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I’ve learnt how to walk on lead but its still a bit scary for me.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training.

Grape came into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was a very worried little girl who clearly hadn't experienced much human interaction and found the world an overwhelming place. Despite her fears, she always tried so hard to be brave, gently accepting strokes while she learned that people could be kind.

Size wise Grape weighs approximately 14.5 kg. She's a lovely medium-sized girl, around the size of a cocker spaniel.

Fast forward a few months, and Grape has come on in leaps and bounds. She still has a sensitive soul, but each day we see more of the happy, playful little girl she was always destined to be.

When Grape first arrived, her coat was dirty and badly matted, so her first groom was more of a fresh start than a pamper. Now that her beautiful curls have grown back, she recently enjoyed a proper makeover to show off what an adorable little teddy bear she really is. The bath was a little scary for her, but she coped brilliantly, and by the end she was a gorgeous fluffy princess, looking every bit as special as she is.

One of Grape's biggest achievements has been her growing confidence. She is now walking on a lead and is doing really well, although she isn't quite 100% confident yet, particularly with people she doesn't know well. With someone she trusts, she is making fantastic progress and continues to improve every day.

She absolutely adores other dogs and gets on wonderfully with every dog she meets. Their company gives her confidence, and because of this shewill need a kind, confident resident dogin her new home to help guide and reassure her as she continues to settle into family life. We recently caught Grape playing for the very first time, doing joyful little bounces around a tennis ball. It may seem like a small thing, but for Grape it was a huge milestone and another step away from the life she once knew.

Although she's still a little nervous about human fuss, she now greets us every morning with a waggy tail and the sweetest smile. She's also a complete sucker for treats, making winning her over much easier! She is still learning about life in a home, so her new family will need to continue her house training, build her confidence, and help her discover all the joys of being a much-loved pet. A calm, patient home with adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs would suit her perfectly.

When Grape arrived she was a little overweight, but with a healthy diet and gentle exercise she has been making great progress. She has also been through quite a lot medically since arriving with us. She has been spayed, had two teeth extracted, undergone a hernia repair, and had a small cyst removed during her spay. Her hormonal alopecia should continue to improve following her spay, and she has also completed treatment for an ear infection.

We truly cannot understand why Grape has been overlooked for so long. She has blossomed into such a sweet, gentle little dog, and while she will need a family willing to continue building her confidence, the rewards of watching her flourish will be immeasurable.

Grape has been given the Gift of Life Wendy Stewart

Sweet, sensitive Grape has now been with us for around three months, and we honestly can't understand why she hasn't had floods of interest. She is such a lovely little dog who has come on in leaps and bounds since arriving at the rescue.

When Grape first came to us, her coat was dirty and badly matted, so her first groom was more of a fresh start than a pamper. Now that her beautiful curls have grown back, we thought she deserved a proper makeover to show everyone what an adorable little teddy bear she really is. The bath was a little scary for her, but she coped so well, and she was an absolute star with the dryer (apart from preferring us not to fuss around her head too much!). By the end, she was transformed into a gorgeous, fluffy little princess, ready to strut around the rescue.

It's not just her appearance that's blossomed. Grape has grown so much in confidence over the last few weeks. She is now walking on a lead and is doing really well, although she's still not 100% confident, especially with people she doesn't know well. With someone she trusts, she is making fantastic progress and continues to improve every day.

One of the loveliest things about Grape is how much she adores other dogs. She delights in every dog she meets and loves having canine friends around her. We even caught her playing for the very first time, doing playful little bounces around a tennis ball. It might seem like an ordinary moment, but for Grape it was a huge milestone and another step further away from the life she once knew.

She can still be a little nervous about human fuss, but every morning she greets us with a waggy tail and the sweetest smile. Each day she lets her guard down a little more, and we're seeing more of the happy, playful girl she was always meant to be. She's also very partial to treats, which definitely helps when making new friends!

Grape would make a wonderful addition to almost any family that's happy to give her a little patience and understanding while she continues to build her confidence. We truly cannot understand why this gorgeous little girl has been overlooked for so long.

Grape is still a nervous girlie and is taking longer to trust humans, given we know nothing of her past this is understandable.

I am trying to show her that all I want to do is help her and show her love, while also respecting her space and going slowly with her, which is what her adopters may have to do depending on where’s she’s at.

She will allow a gentle fuss when she’s in her bed but will not willingly come up and ask for one yet. I think maybe in a calm home she will start to feel more comfortable, kennel life isn’t for everyone, and learn to trust humans.

She is a beautiful girl and I hope she starts to trust soon so we can see that amazing and sweet personality that I’m sure is hiding in her somewhere just bursting to come out.

Grape has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a scared girl who is quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and clearly isn't used to much human interaction, so finds this quite worrying at the moment. Despite her fears she will let you gently stroke her and is trying so hard to be brave.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace and would benefit from adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs. She gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Grape has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Everything will be new to her, so a calm and consistent routine will be important.

Grape has arrived a little overweight, but with a good diet and gentle exercise, she should soon start to shed the excess. She has some hormonal alopecia, but this should start to grow back now she has been spayed. She has had 2 teeth extracted as well as a hernia repair and our vets have noted she has a small cyst, which was removed at the time of her spay. She is also being treated for a ear infection.

Grape is a very worried little girl at the moment, but with time, patience, and the support of another dog, she has the potential to slowly gain confidence and begin to show more of her true character.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

07-07-26 Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him.

Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

Archie has settled back into rescue life well and is currently sharing his kennel with a lovely female dog, who he gets on very well with. He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet.

Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

name: Toast
description:
I would like a quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe. I live with a cat in my foster home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in (6ft+)

I'm harness training currently but need to build my confidence around lead walking.

I will need to learn about house training and lead walking

Toast is a delicate little girl who came to us from a breeder and has been slowly finding her confidence in the world. When she first arrived, she was very nervous and overwhelmed by everything around her, often running to hide in her bed.

Since arriving in foster, it has become clear that Toast is an extremely nervous girl and remains very unsure of new situations. She does not enjoy handling and can panic when she feels pressured, so she will need careful, gentle management and time to feel safe.

Toast is currently living with a cat in her foster home and can live with a dog-savvy cat who respects her space.

She will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand nervous ex-breeding dogs and can support her without expectation or pressure. A calm, predictable environment will be essential for her ongoing confidence building.

She has come on in some areas, but handling still needs to be approached very carefully. While she has previously shown some progress with being picked up and having a harness fitted, this must always be done with patience and awareness of her limits, as she can become overwhelmed.

Toast is currently working on her harness training, and does allow her foster mummy to put one on her now, but she is not comfortable on a lead just yet and will need continued support and encouragement to build confidence. She is still learning about house training, and seems to be clean in the home when her foster mummy is around but can have a few accidents when she is left alone. With time and patience, she will begin to pick this up and understand the rules of house training.

She need a kind, confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and provide reassurance as she adjusts to home life.

Toast arrived with a low-grade luxating patella on her left side, which may improve with gentle exercise. She has also been treated for mucky ears, right-sided otitis, hot spots, and dermatitis, all of which are improving with care. Her general health will need to continue to be monitored in her new home, with any future treatment provided as needed.

Behind her shy beginnings is a sensitive little dog who is still learning to trust the world around her. With patience, understanding, and the right experienced home, Toast will continue to take small steps forward at her own pace.

Toast has arrived in Foster and continues to be a very frightened little girl and can panic easily if anyone tries to pick her up, so she really doesn’t cope well with handling at this stage. Once she is settled in her bed, she is a little more comfortable and will allow gentle strokes and will accept quiet reassurance and talking.

She is extremely nervous overall and will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand how to support a dog like her at her own pace, without pressure. She is also currently living with a cat in her foster home.

I can't believe toast has been here so long that she was due another haircut with me!She has come on tremendously for handling and as long as you're gentle she is content with being picked up, as well as having a harness put on. She is on the journey of learning to walk on a lead and it shouldn't be long before she achieves it.

I've worked with Toast for a while now and I have been able to see how much she's grown over time, especially when it comes to being groomed. The bath is still not her favourite place to be, but she tolerates it, and I think she quite enjoys the warm air of the dryer. She ends up with such a cute haircut because she is so well behaved when it comes to the styling.

This small dog has such a big and beautiful personality and I believe in the right home with another confidence dog she will flourish tremendously.

Toast was such a nervous girl when she came in and she has come on really far since then. I had the pleasure of giving her a much needed groom and although she was nervous she took to it like a champ. She will need grooming upkeep in her forever home to look after her evergrowing locks and I think with a few more pampers she will feel so much more comfortable with it.

She's currently having harness training so she can be more comfortable with the sensation and has gotten much better at being picked up and handled although she can still be a bit jumpy at times but once she's in your arms she's quite calm. She still has a ways to go but I'm so proud of her progress so far and can't wait for when she flourishes with her forever family.

Toast is a delicate little girl who has come to us from a breeder to start her journey towards a brighter future. Right now, the world feels like a very big and scary place to her, and her first instinct is to run and hide in her bed. However, once in your arms, she is easy to handle and accepts gentle reassurance with quiet trust.

Toast will need a calm and understanding home with patient adopters who can give her all the time she needs to find her feet. A kind and confident resident dog will be essential to help guide her, show her that the world can be safe, and give her the courage to explore new experiences.

As she has never lived inside a home before, everything will be new to her, from walking on a lead to learning about house training and family life. Gentle encouragement and plenty of love will help her begin to understand how wonderful it feels to be part of a home.

Toast arrived with a low-grade (Grade 1) luxating patella on the left side, which may improve with gentle exercise. She is also being treated for mucky ears and right-sided otitis as well as dermatitis.

Toast may be shy now, but behind those worried eyes is a sweet girl who just needs the right people to help her shine. With kindness, patience, and a little guidance, she will blossom into a loving and loyal companion.

name: Nuzzle
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like a home with a dog my size or larger. I'm fine with cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have a Grade 1-2 heart murmur and have had 2 teeth extracted.

Nuzzle is a truly gentle, special little girl who has already come so far on her journey. She originally came to us from a breeder and, after a short adoption, sadly found her way back to the rescue as it was not the right fit for her. While in the home, she did make progress, but she was fearful of the man in the household and reacted out of fear on two occasions, showing that she needs very understanding, experienced adopters. She is now in a foster home where one of her fosterers is male and has settled in beautifully, which shows great progress for her.

When Nuzzle first arrived with us, she was an extremely nervous and flighty soul, spending most of her time hiding at the back of her kennel, too scared to join in or even accept touch. The world felt overwhelming, being in the yard, meeting people, or simply being handled was terrifying for her, and she lived in a constant state of panic and flight.

Since then, the transformation in Nuzzle has been truly heart‑warming. With patience, kindness, routine, and consistency, she has slowly begun to blossom. She now approaches her carers for gentle fusses and, when she feels safe, will even ask for more. She enjoys being groomed and is walking nicely on the lead.

She shared her kennel well with other dogs of a similar size and is now in a foster home where she is getting along well with the other dogs in the home. Nuzzle thrives when she has another kind, confident dog by her side and will need a resident dog, her size or larger, in her new home for emotional support and confidence-building. She can bond quite closely with her doggy friends and can get quite protective of them, so may prefer to be homed with just one other resident dog who can be her bestie. She is in foster with cats and is fine with them so could potentially live with a dog savvy cat.

Nuzzle is not a dog for busy or noisy environments and will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and are prepared to be patient, gentle, and consistent, allowing her to progress at her own pace.

Despite her fears, Nuzzle is a sweetheart who adores comfort, routine, and affection. She enjoys cosy beds, soft fuss, tasty treats, and the safety of familiar people and dogs. She is house trained and really enjoys the comfort of home life.

From a medical point of view, Nuzzle has a Grade 1–2 heart murmur which does not currently require treatment but should be monitored by a vet. She has had two teeth removed when she was spayed, and she also has a fatty lump on her side which currently requires no action.

Nuzzle has already achieved so much and continues to surprise everyone with her courage and gentle nature. She has incredible potential and, in the right home with the right support, she will continue to grow in confidence and trust. She is a quiet, affectionate companion who simply wants a safe, loving place where she can feel secure and cherished.

With the right family who will celebrate every small step and understand her past, Nuzzle will flourish beautifully and become a deeply rewarding companion.

Today I've had a very busy day. I'm so tired that, as I'm typing this, I'm falling asleep.

I've been for a walk with my foster brother, and it wasn't our usual walk, so I had lots of new smells and sights to check out. Afterwards, we both went to my foster brother's groomer, and I had another groom. I was so good and looked beautiful afterwards (as always!).

Then we visited Foster Nanny, where I had a treat and got to test out her sofa.

Nuzzle recently went out with her foster parents to visit some friends and was such a good girl. She happily accepted treats from everyone, enjoyed playing in the garden, and had a lovely time with their little dog, Beau. She was a little nervous when their friends' sister and her husband arrived, but after a little time she found the confidence to let them give her a gentle fuss.

Nuzzle is such a lovely little girl who continues to make fantastic progress in foster care. She has become much more confident with her foster dad and now happily jumps up onto the sofa for cuddles with both him and his wife. She is house trained and is walking very nicely on the lead in quiet areas while she continues to build her confidence.

Today was my first grooming day with my foster brother. As my foster brother was due to be groomed my new foster parents thought they would treat me to one too and I was so brave and good. Although I wasn't very keen on the dryer and I'm still not very keen on being picked up, I did so well. Now everyone says I look so beautiful and fluffy!

Little Nuzzle has been with us for week now and it brings me to one question, and that question is why has this little darling not got a forever home already?She really is a little star from day one she has been nothing but a pleasure to foster. Her toilet training is 100% (only one accident on the first day she came), she gets on well with all the other dogs here and also gets on well with our cats. She's had 4 other dogs visit and was fine with them also.She sleeps well throughout the night, eats well, loves treats and will take them out of your hand. She walks on a lead with encouragement in quiet areas. She will allow you to fuss her but can be a little hand shy when putting on her harness and lead so does need vocal encouragement.Nuzzle is looking for preferably an adult only home with at least one other fur baby to help her continue with living her best life. Potential adopters must also be aware of her grooming needs.

Nuzzle is desperately missing her home comforts and I think she would love nothing more than to be back in a warm, cosy house. The weather at the rescue has been SO bad over the past couple of months and even though her kennel is set up like a palace because she’s so good, it’s still not the same as a home. She ADORES being snuggled up in bed and it’s definitely her happy place. I can only imagine how grateful she’ll be once she’s back on a sofa. We can dream!!!

This sweet girl completely has my heart and is breaking it at the same time. I cannot emphasise enough how easy she is to look after at the rescue. She quite literally doesn’t put a paw out of place in any aspect. She keeps her kennel and herself sparkling clean, she runs to and from the yard and back to her kennel perfectly every time, she shares everything including food and toys with her friends, and she’s easy to bath and groom. From the perspective of a kennel mum, she’s pretty perfect.

Her best friend got adopted a couple of weeks ago and she has been a little quieter since, but she now has a new kennel friend that she cuddles with a lot and has taken a shine to. I would so love for her to find her forever brother or sister soon because it would make her so happy to have a constant soulmate in her life.

Nuzzle has been back at the rescue for just over a month now and I have to say it’s been an absolute pleasure to look after her. She was on my section the first time she was here over a year ago and it’s been so lovely to see the difference in her. She was a very, very frightened girl back then and extremely panicky all the time. She was basically living in flight mode and it was so hard to have to watch. When she arrived back last month I was SO surprised when she approached me to ask for a little fuss on the first day. That is definitely not the same dog I knew!!

For the first couple of weeks I left her to decompress and settle back into my routine, and thankfully she did this pretty quickly. Since then, we’ve been doing lots of harness practice and she’s doing SO well. She’s been so much of a good influence that she’s even helped her best friend Denise learn how to walk too - so now they go out together on little strolls up the road and back. She’s still not perfect and won’t be up for going for big hikes anytime soon, but she’s getting better every day.

Her favourite thing in the world is being snuggled up in the back of her kennel under a heat lamp. She has a huge donut bed which she shares with Denise and you’ll find her tucked in for the majority of the day. They often enjoy a dental stick each while in the donut bed too, and it’s so sweet to watch!!

Nuzzle has SO much potential and I am so certain that in the right home with adopters who know what they’re doing with ex-breeders, she will thrive. She’s come such a long way and I know she has more to give, so please give her a chance soon.

Nuzzle is a truly gentle, special little girl who has already come so far on her journey. She originally came to us from a breeder and was adopted for a short period of time but has unfortunately found her way back to us as it was not the right fit for her. While in the home, Nuzzle did progress in some ways but was fearful of the man in the home and acted out of fear on two separate occasions without warning.

When she first arrived with us from a breeder, she was an extremely nervous and flighty soul, spending most of her time in the back of her kennel, too scared to join in or even accept touch. The world felt overwhelming, and every new experience, being in the yard, meeting people, or even being touched, was terrifying.

But since, returning, oh how far she has come! With patience, kindness, and the comfort, Nuzzle has slowly begun to blossom. She now approaches her kennel mummy for gentle fusses and, when she’s ready, will even ask for more. She’s learning to walk on a harness, enjoys being groomed, and moves confidently to and from the yard as part of her daily routine. She shares her kennel with a few other dogs of a similar size, and she gets along beautifully with them, sharing food, curling up together in bed, and finding reassurance in their company.

Nuzzle thrives when she has another kind, confident dog by her side, and in the right home, she will continue to grow in confidence and trust. She still relies on her canine friends for comfort, so she will need a resident dog of a similar size or larger. She also needs a calm, quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and are prepared to be patient, gentle, and consistent as she navigates life at her own pace.

Despite her challenges, Nuzzle is a sweetheart who adores comfort and love. She has shown that she can be fully housetrained in the home, but may need a few reminders in her new environment. She enjoys cosy beds, soft fuss, and tasty treats, and has a bright, promising future if given the right support. She does have a Grade 1–2 heart murmur, which does not currently need treatment but should be monitored by a vet, and she had two teeth removed when she was spayed. She also has a fatty lump on her side which requires no action currently.

Nuzzle has already achieved so much and continues to surprise us with her courage and gentle nature. She is a quiet, affectionate companion who just wants a safe place to feel loved and secure. With the right family who will celebrate every little step she takes, Nuzzle will flourish beautifully.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Kira
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Kira is a super sweet and gentle lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has now spent a week in foster care and has made lovely progress. Her first day was understandably overwhelming, and she spent hours pacing around the garden, too frightened to come into the house. However, with patience and reassurance, she has already started to settle into her new routine.

Kira has grown in confidence over the past week and now happily follows her foster carer around the house, enjoying being nearby. She is curious about what is going on around her and is no longer fazed by everyday household noises. Although she is still a little shy, she will happily sniff an outstretched hand, gently take treats, and accept a little fuss as people pass by, even if she doesn't actively seek attention just yet. It seems that chicken is certainly the way to Kira's heart!

Kira has a healthy appetite and would happily help herself to the resident dogs' meals if given the opportunity! She enjoys the company of the other dogs and has even started joining in with their excited races up the garden whenever they spot a squirrel, although she's still learning exactly how the game works. She hasn't shown much interest in toys yet and hasn't quite discovered the sofa, but we are sure these milestones will come in time as her confidence continues to grow.

She has been wonderfully clean in the house from the very beginning, helped by having easy access to the garden, and she sleeps soundly through the night. However, she may some reminders of this in her new home. She is also happy wearing a harness, and her foster carers will soon begin introducing lead walking once she is ready.

Kira is looking for a calm, adult-only home where she can continue to blossom at her own pace. She will need plenty of time, reassurance, and TLC as she learns that life can be full of comfort, companionship, and love. Her coat is also beginning to grow back nicely where she had alopecia, and she is looking healthier every day.

In the right home, we believe this gentle little girl has every chance of becoming a wonderful and devoted companion. With kindness, patience, and plenty of tasty chicken treats, Kira's future is looking brighter every day.

Kira has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

After a week in Foster Kira has made good progress. She found her first day here overwhelming and spent hours pacing the garden too frightened to come into the house.

A week later what a difference she now shadows her Foster Carer, is curious but not phased by household noises. Kira has a good appetite but given the chance will move in on the resident dogs food bowls.

She sleeps through the night and has been clean in the house from the start, helped by the back door always being open. Chicken is the way to win over the heart of this gentle little girl. She happily wears her harness and we will start lead training in the coming days. Kira will sniff a hand, take treats and accept a little fuss in passing but does not seek attention.

She has started joining in on squirrel alert racing up the garden with my girls but doesn’t understand the rules of the game. She has not shown any interest in toys and has not jumped up onto the sofa yet, Kira is not using a crate.

Kira’s coat is starting to grow back where she has alopecia.

Kira is a super sweet and gentle lady who has come to us from a breeder. At the moment, she is feeling quite unsure of her surroundings and will often stand completely still when approached, as she is still learning to feel safe and confident.However, after spending some time with her, Kira begins to relax and will even give a little tail wag, showing that beneath her shy exterior is a lovely girl who wants to trust. With patience, kindness, and understanding, we are confident that she will continue to come out of her shell.Kira is looking for a calm, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace without any pressure. As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns all the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. To begin with, gentle garden explorations may be a great way for her to build confidence and start experiencing the world around her.Kira will need plenty of time, reassurance, and TLC as she learns that life can be full of comfort, companionship, and love. In the right home, we believe this sweet girl has every chance of blossoming into a wonderful and devoted companion.

name: Chewwie
description:
I’d like a quiet home filled with love and kindness!

I would like a home with another dog medium size or larger. I am fine with cats.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 2 teeth removed!

Chewwie originally came to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He was lucky enough to be adopted, but sadly, despite being very loved, it became clear that the home wasn't quite the right match for him and he has now returned to our care to begin his search once again. Chewwie was very worried of the adult sons in the home and also wasn't a great match with the smaller resident dog.

Chewwie is a sensitive boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and can find unfamiliar situations overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but remained worried around the adult sons in the household. For this reason, he is looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Since returning to our care, however, Chewwie has been an absolute pleasure. From the day he came back, he has been nothing but gentle, loving and affectionate with everyone here. Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, we have seen a completely different side to him in kennels. He happily bounces over to greet us, is always looking for a fuss, and simply loves being around people. His affectionate nature shines through every day, and he has reminded us just what a special boy he is.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to family life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts of home, especially curling up in his cosy beds. He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and gradually build up any time spent alone as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be medium-sized or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog-savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has learnt to walk nicely on a lead and now really enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will benefit from ongoing encouragement as his confidence continues to grow.

Once Chewwie knows you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate companion with a wonderfully cheeky personality. He loves playing with other dogs and is especially fond of his kennel friend. He's also a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the paddling pool, making the most of every opportunity for fun. Like many mischievous youngsters, he has also been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially enjoys hard toys, while softer toys and enrichment items should be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. His return to rescue has shown us just how affectionate, gentle and resilient he is, and we know that in the right home he will continue to flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, fun-loving and wonderfully cheeky companion who will fill their days with smiles.

When Chewwie first arrived, he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. Following his return to the rescue, he began limping on the same leg and holding it up. X-rays at a local veterinary practice showed no abnormalities or injuries, so it is thought to be a soft tissue injury which should continue to improve. His adopters and their own vet should continue to monitor this as a precaution.

Chewwie has been given the Gift of Life by Paula Elliot

Chewwie is an absolute angel. From the day he arrived on my section, he's been nothing but gentle, loving, affectionate, and just a truly special soul.

Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, I honestly haven't seen that side of him. With me, he's all about cuddles and attention. He'll happily bounce over to say hello and is always looking for affection. He's also got a cheeky side that keeps me smiling. If you leave your folder, phone, or radio lying around for even a second, don't be surprised if Chewwie decides it's his now!

He's a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the pool with his kennel friend. Watching him let loose, have fun, and just be a dog is one of my favourite things. He also loves heading down to the big yard where he can have a good sniff, stretch his legs, and enjoy himself.

Chewwie really is such an amazing dog, and I feel so lucky to know him. Looking after him has been an absolute privilege.

Once Chewwie gets to know you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate boy who adores a fuss and cuddle. He has a wonderfully cheeky personality and loves to play with other dogs. He is also a bit of a mischievous boy and has been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as we are told he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially loves hard toys, but softer toys and enrichment items will need to be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.
