name: Snowy
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a laid back dog who is slightly larger than me in my new home.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 1 tooth extracted and am being treated for a ear infection.

Snowy is a very sweet little lady who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was quite worried and overwhelmed, but was trying so hard to be brave! She is still feeling quite timid, but once she gets to know she really enjoys having a fuss and is happy to be handled. She is an inquisitive and loving girl and once she's in a home we don’t think it will take long to come out of her shell and show her true personality.

Snowy would love to find a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and where she can settle in at her own pace and realise what it means to be a loved family member. We would consider homing her with gentle dog savvy older teenagers.

She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs, so she will need at least one kind, calm and confident resident dog in her new home to help her feel safe and settled. We have found that she is best suited to living with laid back dogs who are slightly larger than her. She can become a little jealous when other dogs are receiving attention and is more laid back with dogs who are a little bigger than her.

As Snowy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns about home life and house training. She has started to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and while this is still very for her, she is doing so well.

With her sweet nature and growing confidence, we are sure it won’t take her long to settle into family life and flourish in a loving home.

Snowy has had 1 tooth removed at the time of her spay and has prevously been treated for an ear infection.

Snowy has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

This week Snowy has met a few new friends and has been out for her first walk! She took it all in her stride. We were very impressed with how well she has done.

She is a timid lady but really enjoys having a fuss when she gets to know you. She would love a home where she has at least one confident resident dog to help her to settle in. She is currently sharing her kennel with a laid back Scottie dog and gets along well with her, although she ideally needs a friend who is larger than her, she can be quite shy if they are too much larger than her.

She really is a sweetheart who is just looking for her chance at a new and happy life.

Snowy is a wonderful lady who has come to us from a breeder. She is happy to be handled and will shyly approach for fuss and attention, showing that she is trying so hard to be brave and really wants to make friends. Snowy is an inquisitive and loving girl and once she's in a home we don’t think it will take long to come out of her shell and show her true personality.Snowy would love to find and calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and where she can settle in at her own pace and realise what it means to be a loved family member. We would consider homing her with gentle dog savvy older teenagers.She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs, so she will need at least one kind, calm and confident resident dog in her new home to help her feel safe and settled. We have found that she is best suited to living with laid back dogs who are slightly larger than her. She can become a little jealous when other dogs are receiving attention and is more laid back with dogs who are a little bigger than her.As Snowy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns about house training and walking on a lead. With her sweet nature and growing confidence, we are sure it won’t take her long to settle into family life and flourish in a loving home.Snowy has had 1 tooth removed at the time of her spay and is being treated for infected ears.

name: Nelly
description:
I will need an adult only home with breed-experience.

I’d like to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on the lead but I am strong, so I will need continued training!

I have lived in a home, but may need a few reminders as I settle in.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

Nelly, also known as 'Nellyphant' amongst the kennel staff, is a beautiful girl with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. Nelly came into our care after experiencing a difficult past, having spent much of her life confined to a very small room and sadly being passed between several homes. Despite everything she has been through, her love for people has never faded. She absolutely adores human company and greets everyone she meets like they are her new best friend.

Nelly is a typical fun-loving Bulldog girl who is full of character. She loves attention, affection and being involved in everything her people are doing. She enjoys a good play session, especially when there is a ball involved! Tennis balls, footballs, honestly, anything she can throw around will make her happy. She is even learning that dropping the ball means the fun can start all over again. Once playtime is finished, she is just as happy settling down for a well-earned rest.

Sadly, the instability Nelly has experienced has left her feeling worried when she is left alone. She can become distressed when separated and will need a home where she is not left for long periods. Her adopters will need to build up time apart gradually, using patience and consistency to help her understand that her people will always return.

Nelly is currently learning about other dogs and is not yet comfortable around them. She is doing brilliantly with her muzzle training, which allows her to enjoy her walks safely while she learns that other dogs are not something to worry about. She can enjoy walking alongside calm, quiet dogs, but she may react if she feels overwhelmed, especially with larger dogs or if another dog barks at her first. Her new family will need to continue her muzzle training on walks and support her with positive, patient guidance.

Nelly can already walk on a lead, although she is a strong and enthusiastic girl who can pull when excited. She will need adopters who are confident handling her and who are happy to continue her lead training. She loves getting out for walks, having zoomies and exploring, but she is equally happy being a cuddle-loving couch potato afterwards.

Nelly has come from a home before, so she may already understand some household routines, but she may need gentle reminders as she settles into a new environment. She will need an adult-only home with breed-experienced adopters who understand her bouncy nature and can provide the boundaries, consistency and love she needs. She will need to be the only dog in the home, with no visiting dogs and no cats. She will also need an extra-secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft+.

Nelly is wonderful at the vets and loves the attention she receives there. She enjoys spending time with the staff, soaking up the fuss and showing everyone what a friendly and affectionate girl she is.

Nelly is a resilient, loving dog who has been through more than she should have, yet she continues to greet the world with excitement and affection. She is ready for a family who will spoil her, make her feel safe and show her just how wonderful life can be. For lovers of Bulldog breeds, Nelly’s silly personality and loving nature are sure to bring endless joy.

*Nelly has been measured by our local Dog Licensing Officer and confirmed that she is not considered a banned breed.

Nelly, AKA 'Nellyphant', plays football and she’s amazing at it! She also absolutely loves a herding ball. In fact, Nelly would play with any ball or toy for hours if she had her way, and we have to remind her to take breaks and relax for a bit.

Nelly has an exuberant nature, and no day is bad when Nelly's about. Nelly is now muzzle trained and proudly trots along the lanes near the rescue, donning her bright pink muzzle.

Nelly really is a delightful, confident, and human-loving dog, and as much as she likes to play, she will settle down and chill, often contentedly hanging out with the office staff at the rescue whilst they're busy working away.

Nelly's ideal home would have no other dogs and adult humans who have plenty of time to play and hang out with her, as well as knowledge and experience of bull breeds.

This super lady really does deserve to find a lovely home of her own soon.

Nelly, also known as Hippo amongst the kennel staff, is a beautiful girl with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. Nelly came into our care after experiencing a difficult past, having spent much of her life confined to a very small room and sadly being passed between several homes. Despite everything she has been through, her love for people has never faded. She absolutely adores human company and greets everyone she meets like they are her new best friend.

name: Dutch
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is being trained to wear a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

name: Swanny
description:
I could live with dog savvy teenagers who respect my space.

I can be an only dog or live with a larger male dog. I cannot live with cats.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I do my best to keep my kennel clean, but may need help in a home!

Swanny is a truly lovely little lady who has come to us from a breeder and has been quietly stealing hearts ever since. With her unmistakable Beagle nose, Swanny loves to explore her surroundings and see what’s going on around her. While she can still have a slightly shy side, her confidence has blossomed beautifully during her time with us, and her sweet, gentle nature really shines through. She has become very people orientated and now absolutely loves some fuss and attention!

Over the past few weeks, Swanny has made wonderful progress. She is now walking beautifully on the lead and thoroughly enjoys heading out for walks or having a run around our big yard, where she shows her playful and inquisitive side. She also does her best to keep her kennel clean during the day, which suggests that house training in a home environment should be very straightforward with a little routine and patience.

Swanny has made friends with some larger male dogs here at the rescue and loves to go on play dates in our play yard with them. She can be quite picky with which male dogs she likes and can also be too enthusiastic and doesn't always read other dogs' signals, so she would only be suited to living with a calm, larger male dog who is very tolerant of her. Slow, sensible introductions would be essential. Thanks to her growing confidence, we now feel that Swanny could also live as an only dog in the right, understanding home where she can continue to thrive at her own pace or she can live with a larger, calm male dog. She cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Swanny has never lived in a home before, she will need kind and patient adopters who can help her learn the routines of family life. She could share her home with dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in. With gentle guidance, consistency, and love, she is sure to settle quickly and become a devoted and affectionate companion. An active family who enjoy getting out and about would be ideal, as Swanny loves having both her mind and body kept busy.

Swanny has cataracts in both eyes, which do not appear to bother her at all. She has had an umbilical hernia repaired at the time of her spay, along with two teeth extractions. She also has one fractured pre-molar, which our vets have advised leaving for now, though it may need monitoring in the future. Swanny also has a travel document in place.

Swanny is an absolute delight to care for here at the rescue, and we truly believe that whoever opens their heart and home to her will be gaining a very special little dog who has so much love to give.

Swanny is the perfect dog, suitable to be an only dog. She would thrive in a home with owners who love cuddles and walking. She's the right balance of cuddly and active and an absolute pleasure to work with! She's been enjoying her enrichment toys with her treats and adores anyone who she comes in contact with!

She's honestly perfect and I can't understand how she hasn't found a beagle loving home yet!

Over the last couple of months, we’ve introduced Swanny to many larger male dogs at the rescue in attempt to find her an ideal playmate. Swanny is an absolutely comical girl, and no matter the size of the male dog, she will not hold back!!

Swanny’s main buddy is our Standard Poodle Flash, and every single day they have play dates. She is incredibly tolerant with his exuberant and playful nature, but also gives it as good as she gets. They have such a good balance between them, and once Swanny has had enough she will just take herself away from playing and have a good sniff around our big play yard, or steal some fusses off the first human in sight!

She has also had a play date with Charlie (a Great Dane X Mastiff) and his size did not phase her one bit, he was probably 3-4x bigger than her, but Swanny’s playfulness definitely trumped his size!!!

Swanny is not only an absolute delight to look after, but just being in her presence would make your entire day. She is as sweet as anything, she is kind, gentle, and loving. She is not built for kennels, she is build for sofa snuggles, big adventures, and endless love.

How Swanny has not been adopted yet is a mystery to me .

Perhaps it's her demeanor when meeting new people? Swanny can be a little shy at first but soon makes a connection and there's nothing wrong with being cautious.

Swanny walks beautifully on a lead and loves to sniff and smell the grass.

As Swanny does have enough confidence, she can live as the only dog in the house or equally she would be happy living with a larger male dog.

I would say, to see the true Swanny, you need to meet her, walk her and give her a little time to show affection. It really is rewarding when it happens.

Beagles are really pretty dogs and Swanny is no exception, so if you would like a beautiful beagle in your life, Swanny is ready to be the one.

Swanny is the sweetest angel, and it truly is a privilege to care for her five days a week. She has the most gentle and loving nature.

Swanny can be a little nervous when meeting new people, which is completely understandable, but with a bit of patience and kindness, she soon begins to show her true self.

Once you’ve built that special bond with Swanny, she becomes the most loyal companion you could ever ask for. She loves to  be close to you and will happily follow you around like you’re shadow!

Like a true beagle, Swanny absolutely loves her walks. The moment she’s outside, her nose is straight to the ground, exploring every scent along her way. Watching her take in the world through her nose is such a lovely reminder of how much joy the simple things can bring.

Swanny really is the most perfect dog in her own unique way. With the right family who can give her patience, reassurance, and lots of love, she will truly flourish.

She has so much to offer and would make the most wonderful addition to a caring and understanding home.

Swanny is such a sweet girl who is blossoming in confidence every single day!

Swanny has made so much progress over the last few weeks, I now believe she can be an only dog in the right circumstances.

Swanny does get on with larger male dogs absolutely fine, but prefers dogs who aren’t in the her face and give her the space she needs.

During her time here so far swanny has had a few disagreements with the male dogs she has shared kennels with when they get to much in her space.

Swanny is now walking beautifully on lead, and enjoys spending time going out for walks, or running freely down our big yard!

Swanny also tries to keep her kennel clean during the days, so house training should be a breeze!

Swanny is honestly a delight to look after here at the rescue, whoever welcomes her into their family are going to be very lucky people!

Swanny is a fabulous little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She’s an inquisitive girl with the unmistakable nose of a Beagle, always eager to explore and see what’s going on around her. Swanny can be confident when she chooses, but she still has a shy side, and with the gentle encouragement of her kennel friends, she’s starting to show her sweet, sociable nature.

She will need a confident, larger male resident dog in her new home to help her settle, guide her, and teach her about life in a home. Once she’s comfortable, Swanny would absolutely love an active family who can take her on plenty of adventures and keep her mind and body engaged.

Swanny is an absolute gem and, as she has never lived in a home before, will need patient adopters to help her learn house training, walking on a lead, and all the routines of home life. With kindness, consistency, and love, we believe she will settle quickly and become a devoted, loving companion.

Swanny has come to us with cataracts in both eyes, that does not seem to bother her. She has had an umbilical hernia repaired at the time of her spay as well as 2 teeth extracted. She also has one fractured pre-molar which our vets have advised to leave, but this may need to be looked at in the future.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Lady
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need another kind resident dog in my new home. I haven't met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 1 tooth extracted and am ready to find my forever home!

Lady has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a sweet and gentle girl who was a little worried to find herself here when she first arrived, but did start to soon become very inquisitive and was trying so hard to be brave. She has since moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in well and learning all about home life for the first time ever.

Lady is looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle at her own pace and build her confidence, she would benefit from adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs. Her confidence is starting to grow and she will now allow her fosterer to gently stroke her and seems to enjoy this.

She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her feel secure as she settles in. She can guard her food bowl from other dogs, so she will need to be feed separately in her new home and will need adopters who are confident managing this, but she hasn't shown any signs of guarding treats.

Lady had never lived in a home before moving to foster, she is starting to learn all about home life and house training and is toileting on newspaper at the moment, so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to learn. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice first around the home and garden before venturing further.

With time, kindness and encouragement, we believe Lady will blossom into a wonderful companion. Lady is a truly sweet girl, and we can’t wait to see her thrive in a loving home.

She has had one tooth extracted at the time of her spay.

Lady has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

Lady has now been in her foster home for just over a week and is settling in well. She is a gentle, sweet girl who will now stand for gentle strokes and, after just a few days, was comfortable enough to allow her foster carer to clean and trim around her eyes. She is also doing well with her house training and will use newspapers when indoors.

Lady won't take long to settle into a forever home, as long as she's given the time and space to get to know her new family and surroundings. Once she feels safe, her lovely personality really begins to shine.

Lady has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a sweet and gentle girl who is a little worried to find herself here, but she has been easy to handle and is already becoming a very inquisitive little girl! It's clear that she is trying so hard to be brave and really wants to come and say hello, so we don't think it will take her too long to come out of her shell in her new home.

Lady is looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle at her own pace and build her confidence, she would benefit from adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs. We would consider homing her with gentle dog savvy older teenagers.

Lady has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient and understanding adopters who can help her learn all about home life. She will need support with the basics such as house training, learning to walk on a lead, and discovering that the world isn’t such a scary place. With time, kindness and encouragement, we believe Lady will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Lady is a truly sweet girl, and we can’t wait to see her thrive in a loving home.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Pop
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who love cuddles, and are active!

I will need to be the only pet in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I would like a secure garden where I can have plenty of play time!

I am very active and will need a home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I may have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

30-07-26 Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to "Pop", so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is a wonderful little girl who is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate, sweet nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise as well as mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is doing well with her lead walking and enjoys getting out and about, but she will need owners who are committed to continuing her training and helping her build confidence.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Whilst she can walk past some dogs, she is worried by them and can become reactive on lead, making the wrong choices when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and willing to continue working on her doggy social skills using positive, reward-based training. We have already started muzzle training with Pop to help build her confidence, with the hope that, in time, she may be able to enjoy controlled walks alongside calm canine companions.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine.

She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle and ongoing training she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

name: Tinkerbell
description:
I need an adult-only home with ex-breeder experience that can show me love.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe but I haven’t met cats yet so I'm not sure

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Tinkerbell has come to us from a breeder and has never lived in a home before, so she is understandably unsure and very sensitive to touch. She can go into panic mode if handled too quickly and may try to nip out of fear, as she is simply terrified and trying to protect herself. The initial handling is what scares her most, so patience and slow, gentle introductions are essential.

Recently, Tinkerbell has made wonderful progress and is beginning to show us just how much potential she has. While she is still worried by touch and may move away if approached, she is becoming much more comfortable around the people she knows. She will now approach her kennel mummy to sniff fingers, gently take treats, offer little kisses, and happily relax nearby. Recently, she has even started jumping up onto the bench beside her favourite carer at lunchtime, eagerly hoping for a tasty treat. It has become their own little routine and is a lovely sign of the trust she is beginning to build.

Tinkerbell has also made fantastic progress with handling. Although being picked up can still worry her initially, once she feels secure she settles well. One particularly special moment came when she chose to stay sitting on her kennel mummy's lap for several minutes while being gently stroked, despite not being held in place. For a dog who once found human touch so frightening, this was a huge milestone and shows just how far she has come.

She has also continued her harness training and is now happy wearing a harness with a lead trailing behind her, which many worried dogs find frightening. She is still nervous when gentle lead pressure is introduced, so this will need to continue at her own pace with patient, positive training. With dogs as frightened as Tinkerbell, building confidence is far more important than rushing the end result.

Tinkerbell will need a very experienced, adult-only home with people who understand extremely worried ex-breeding dogs. She will also need a kind and confident resident dog to guide her and help her feel safe. Her adopters will need to appreciate that she may never be a dog who constantly seeks cuddles, but with time, patience and kindness, she can form an incredibly special bond.

As she has never experienced home life, Tinkerbell will need support with house training and all the usual household routines. Calm garden time and gentle introductions to the world will help her confidence continue to grow.

Tinkerbell will also need regular grooming to keep her coat comfortable. She initially found grooming very stressful, but she is making lovely progress through gentle, positive handling and regular visits to our grooming room. Her adopters should be prepared to continue this patiently and work with an experienced, understanding groomer.

Tinkerbell is a truly special little girl who has already overcome so much. The progress she has made since arriving with us is incredible, and we truly believe she is ready for someone to take a chance on her. In the right home, with patience, understanding and love, she has every opportunity to continue blossoming into a wonderful companion.

In the past month I’ve seen more progress in Tinkerbell than ever, and it makes me sooooo happy and proud!!! A little while ago, out of nowhere, she jumped up onto the bench next to me and then quickly jumped back down. It was as if she was thinking “oh gosh, what did I just do!?” … but then she kept doing it again, and again. And now it’s like a little ritual that we have! I eat my lunch with her kennel in the yard nearly every day and because she’s so foodie, she jumps up next to me and waits to see what I have to share. It may or may not be the favourite part of my days!

Another big step for Tinkerbell is that we’ve moved forward with her harness training. I’ve started attaching a lead to it when she’s in the play yard so it trails behind her. A lot of scared dogs get freaked out by this, but it doesn’t seem to bother Tinks at all. I have attempted to pick the lead up twice to essentially ‘walk’ her, and she did panic at the tension, so I’m going to have to ease into it slowly. With dogs as frightened as Tinks, harness training is a huge step, so in my opinion it doesn’t matter how long it takes to get there. What matters is how we get there … slowly, gently, kindly.The last “win” in the past month came a couple of weeks ago. I picked her up in the back of the kennel to put her harness on (which she is not a fan of), and I put her down on my lap to make it easier for me to clip it up. For the first time ever, she just stayed put. She stayed sitting on my lap for about 2 or 3 minutes while I gently stroked her, not holding her in any way - she chose to stay. This made me SO happy and it was such a lovely moment to share with her.Tinks may still be against human touch, but the progress she’s made since her arrival is quite incredible. She really needs someone to take a chance on her now. She deserves it so much.

This week at the rescue we’ve had a big heatwave which resulted in a lot of our dogs needing to be shaved, including my beautiful Tinkerbell as she started to struggle having quite a thick coat. She has the most beautiful fur and she keeps herself so clean and dry, but it had to come off for her comfort. She was taken into the vets to be sedated again, but only because the weather has been so warm.. it would have been too hot to put her through the stress of shaving her all off with no sedation. I have been taking her into the grooming room regularly to brush her and trim the hair around her eyes, and she does definitely get better and better each time, so this is a good sign!! The next time she’s due a shave, I will try again without taking her into the vets to see how she does.

Even though Tinks is still a nervous girl, especially around people she doesn’t know, she is still progressing slowly and steadily. She’s still very reliant on other dogs and tends to copy them a lot of the time, so this has been good for her learning to trust me. She’s watched so many other dogs come up to me for a fuss, take treats from me, and just be comfortable in general being around me, and she is following suit.. just at her own pace. And that’s okay!

She is SUCH a sweet girl who has clearly been through a lot, and it’s not her fault she has such a strong guard up. I absolutely adore working with her and I understand and accept her for who she is. Seeing her get excited over toys and treats, and greeting me with a waggy tail in the mornings really makes me smile, and it gives me hope for her future. She deserves adopters who will love and cherish her the way she always should have been, regardless of if the feelings are mutual.. but I do think she is capable of loving and trusting.. she just needs to find herself with the right people.

Over the last few weeks, our lovely Tinks has reached a huge milestone. After seeing how well she has been progressing with her handling, we felt it was time to take the next step — harness training.

For a dog who finds handling so worrying, we knew there was a strong chance she might not accept wearing a harness. But unless we try, we’ll never know.

Tinks’ other kennel mummy and I took her into the grooming room, where we carefully introduced and fitted her harness. As expected, she was a little unsure and understandably a bit overwhelmed, but she made us both incredibly proud with how she coped. The next step was returning her to her kennel to see how she would manage wearing it throughout the day. Many of our more worried dogs will freeze or refuse to move in this situation, but not our Tinks. She carried on with her day as normal, moving around comfortably with the harness on.

To some, this might not seem like a huge achievement, but for Tinkerbell, it is a massive step in the right direction. Over the coming weeks, we will continue to build on this by practicing daily, with the hope that we can eventually begin introducing a lead in the yard.

With a dog like Tinkerbell, progress takes time, patience, and understanding. Thankfully, she has all of that in abundance, and we will never give up on her.

Tinkerbell has settled into my routine at the rescue beautifully now, so I’m finally starting to see glimpses of the real her. Her guard is definitely still up, but it has dropped slightly and I can tell she’s a lot more comfortable being around me than she used to be. She still won’t allow me to touch her and will bolt away if I go towards her, but she’s approaching me to sniff my fingers, sometimes give me kisses, and taking treats from me every single day now. She also feels content enough to lay near me when I’m sat in the yard eating my lunch, often with her back towards me which I guess is a sign that she does trust me!

One thing she has improved massively with is being picked up. I mentioned in my last update I still had to use a thick blanket and she would still sometimes try to bite (just not as often), but that’s even better again now. This week I was able to pick her up with no blanket, which is HUGE for Tinks!!

Because of how much better she had gotten, I thought I would attempt a full groom - going into it with absolutely no expectations. She allowed me to shave her back, but that’s as far as we could get. She started to get more and more stressed and I really didn’t want to push her and ruin the work we’ve done, so I took her into the vets so she could be sedated to complete the groom. So, she’s now shaved (minus her INCREDIBLE eyelashes), and I think she looks absolutely beautiful. Now that we’ve started fresh with her coat, I’m going to start taking her into the grooming room just once a week or so, and gently brush her etc to get her more used to it all.

Tinkerbell has made slow and steady progress since she’s been on my section and I’m so proud of how brave she’s trying to be. I can tell she wants to come out of her shell a bit more and join in with the rest of the dogs, but she’s not there just quite yet. Something big did happen last week though!! During dinner time I was hand feeding one of her friends, and Tinks came over and started licking the food off my hand for the first time!!!! I was absolutely over the moon and so happy that she felt comfortable enough to do that. Since then she’s done it nearly every day and has also started to take treats from me too if they’re yummy enough. I know this probably won’t sound like a lot to most people, but for a dog like Tinberbell it’s huge. For me, taking food from my hand is usually the first step in earning trust with my scared dogs, so I think we’re heading in the right direction.

We have also made a small amount of progress with Tinkerbell’s fear of being picked up. She still doesn’t like it - at all - but she’s not panicking as much any more and definitely doesn’t try to bite me as much as she did before. I still have to use a thick blanket and be very slow and calm with her, but I think she is starting to slowly realise that I’m not going to hurt her. I trimmed her fringe again a few days ago as her hair seems to grow quite quickly, so I took this opportunity to stroke her head gently for a little while once I was done. She actually started to close her eyes after a minute or so and I think she may have been enjoying it, or at least I hope she was.I adore this little lady and I’m going to do everything I can to show her what love and kindness is. I just hope a special someone will come along and feel the same way about her soon.

Tinkerbell has recently been moved to my section, as she struggles a great deal with being touched and handled by us humans. At present, she goes into complete panic mode whenever I go to pick her up, and she will try to bite to protect herself. This doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog at all; she’s literally just so scared she will do anything she can to stop it happening. Once I have her comfortably in my arms, she will actually settle really well and will allow me to do things such as give her a gentle fuss and trim the hair on her face. I think the initial picking up is what scares her the most so this is what we’ll work on slowly together.

Tinkerbell is going to need a very experienced home with people who have had terrified dogs before. She’s going to need a lot of work and TLC put into her, and also a lot of understanding. Her adopters will need to accept the fact that she may never be a normal dog, and she may never be a dog who wants fusses or cuddles, but love her anyway. She’s a very special girl, and she needs a home equally as special to help her and give her what she needs.

I’m going to work as closely as I can with her over the next couple of weeks, and hopefully I can earn her trust and prove to her that she doesn’t need to be afraid of me. I’ll keep you all updated!

Tinkerbell has come to us from a breeder and can be a little unsure at first. She is touch-sensitive and may need time to feel comfortable, but once she calms down, she begins to show her gentle, sweet side. Tinkerbell will need an adult-only home that can handle her sassy personality and provide the patience she needs to settle in at her own pace.

She will also need a kind and confident resident dog to guide her and take her under their wing as she adjusts. Tinkerbell is looking for someone to teach her about trust, companionship, and the joys of home life.

As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be gentle and understanding while she learns about house training and walking on a lead. Starting with a few gentle garden sniffs will be perfect for her confidence as she begins to explore her new world.

Tinkerbell is a little gem who, with time and love, will grow into a devoted and affectionate companion.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gala
description:
I need a quiet adult-only home with no visiting kids to keep me stress-free.

I need at least one resident dog to help me feel safe, preferably a female my size.

I’m frightened and will need a secure garden to learn about being outside.

I enjoy secure enclosed areas where I can run around, but the lead still worries me.

I’m learning to walk on the lead, it's scary for me but I am toilet trained!

I’m fully vaccinated and spayed, ready for my forever home!

Gala is an extremely sweet but incredibly sensitive girl who originally came to us from a breeder. Sadly, she has already been adopted twice and returned both times, as the homes simply weren’t the right fit for her. Because of this, Gala is now searching for a very special forever home with people who truly understand her needs and are committed to giving her the time, patience, and stability she has never had.

When she first arrived, she was an extremely scared, flighty, and shut-down girl who wanted nothing to do with us humans. Since then, Gala has made some lovely, if small, steps forward. She will now allow a gentle stroke while she is on the sofa, usually for around a minute before she chooses to move away. This is huge progress for her and shows just how brave she is becoming.

On one occasion, she even chose to jump up onto the sofa and sit beside someone. Although she ran off as soon as there was a slight movement, it was still a big milestone and a really positive sign of her growing confidence.

That said, Gala is still a very worried girl who carries a lot of fear, and she has a long way to go. She is still frightened of interaction and will run away when approached. However, once she has settled into one of her beds, she will stay still to be gently picked up or have her lead put on.

She remains very nervous of the harness and lead. While she settles a little once it is on, the process of putting it on is still very scary for her. This will need to be built up slowly and gently to avoid overwhelming her or setting her back. She does know how to walk on a lead, but finds it quite daunting, and the outside world is still very overwhelming. She will need time and patience, starting in a secure garden to help build her confidence before any bigger adventures.

Gala takes great comfort from other dogs and truly thrives in their company. She loves to snuggle up with them and will be happiest in a home with other female dogs — the more, the better if possible. She has already shown that she forms particularly strong bonds, often choosing a favourite companion and looking to them for guidance. A kind, confident, and playful female dog of a similar size would be ideal for her, as she finds reassurance and happiness with other dogs while humans are still a source of uncertainty.

She also has a lovely playful side beginning to emerge, and she enjoys carrying around and playing with cuddly toys, which seem to bring her comfort and contentment.

Gala cannot live with cats and will need a calm, child-free home, including no visiting children, where she can feel safe and secure.

Gala has never truly known security, so what she needs most now is patience, kindness, and someone who will never give up on her. There won’t be any overnight miracles, and she may never become a confident, outgoing dog, but with the right person by her side, we know she can continue to grow in confidence, heal from her past, and finally understand what it means to feel safe and loved.

Gala has visited the vets regarding a small mass of inguinal fat. This is not causing her any harm and is currently being left alone, but it may need monitoring in the future.

Gala has made a few small improvements over the past month. She will now allow us to give her a short stroke while she’s on the sofa, usually for about a minute before she moves away. This is massive progress for her and shows how brave she’s becoming.

On one occasion, she even jumped up onto the sofa and sat beside me. As soon as I moved slightly, she ran off, but it was still a big step forward and she did so well.

She is still very scared of the harness. Once it’s on, she settles a little, but the process of putting the lead on frightens her. It’s going to be a very slow process, as we don’t want to push her too far and risk setting her back.

She also loves carrying around and playing with a cuddly toy, which seems to make her feel more content and happy.

Gala is still happiest when surrounded by other female dogs — the more, the better if possible. She has chosen a favourite and looks to her for guidance. A confident, playful female companion would be ideal for her, as she finds comfort in other dogs while humans are still a source of fear.

Gala has been back in foster for a few weeks and she seems to be happy and loves being with her dog friends. She settles very quickly and will happily sleep on a comfy chair. But she is still a very worried girl, as although looking settled, If one of us gets up, she'll be up and running to hide out of our  way. We have found routine is the best thing for her, she is more confident with this.

She very quickly learns what to do and does get animated when certain times arrive, such as breakfast and dinner - as long as she doesn't need to be too near a human. She will definitely need a very stable home without changes and without expectation. At the moment she will interact with us from a distance ok but doesn't get close. If you approach slowly she will stay put and you can stroke her or pick her up but she's not comfortable with it and would much rather escape from you...

On the positive side, she has started to show signs of enjoying a tummy rub, she will lift her leg for more to show she's liking it - almost like her doggy instincts are getting the better of her, this is the only time she happily excepts touching that she seems to enjoy.

Putting her harness on she shakes with fear when she sees her harness and it needs putting on very very slowly. She then is happy to walk in her own surroundings on a lead, but is so scared of being outside in the big world on it and will try to escape.

However she does love being taken to a secure field where she can run around playing with her furry friends. She loves all our other dogs and interacts very well with them all. Plus she is house trained.

Her new home must be one who gives her patience and time and expects nothing in return, this could be for a long time. She needs a very stable quiet home without too many changes happening and a good routine She wouldn't react well to things like doggy day care or holidays. She needs some very gentle persuasion to gain trust on humans but without expectations so she is not pushed too far and regressed.

Gala has been back at the rescue with me for just about two months now. I also looked after her when she was at the rescue originally, around a year and a half ago. Seeing her arrive back was hard for me, but it was nice to see how much progress she’s made during her time away. When I knew her all that time ago, she was an extremely scared, flighty, and shut-down girl who wanted nothing to do with us humans. It’s very clear she has gained confidence since then and has (sort of) learnt that she can trust us humans, so it is lovely to see the difference in her. Having said that, she does still carry a lot of worry and fear, and she still has a long way to go. Steps have been made in the right direction, so hopefully she can continue learning and growing, and eventually try to put her past behind her.Gala’s biggest love is food, so this is the main thing I’ve been using to get her comfortable around me. She has learnt how to ‘sit’ and also how to give the best puppy dog eyes that I can never say no to! She waits patiently for her turn for a treat, and takes them nice and gently too.Gala does still have quite a big fear of human hands and won’t approach me for a fuss, but she is good when it comes to things such as being groomed. When I need to pick her up, she’ll usually jump into one of her beds and then stay still for me to scoop her. She knows how to walk on a harness, but the outside world is another one of her fears, so this is something that needs to be taken slowly with her. I doubt very much she’ll be up for big adventures any time soon and will need a lot of practice in the garden and very quiet areas for a good while, so this is something her future adopters will need to take into consideration.After a life full of uncertainty and confusion, her next home HAS to be the right one for her. She really needs adopters who will love her regardless of her worries and work with her through them. Most importantly of all, she can’t be given up on again. She deserves to know where she’s going to wake up in the morning and not have to worry about being passed from pillar to post. She deserves love, trust, and commitment … and not a smidge less.

Sadly, Gala has returned to the kennels after her recent adoption. Although her new family cared deeply for her, it turned out not to be the right match. This decision was made with everyone's best interests at heart, and she’s now back with us while we look for her perfect forever home. Gala is a wonderful dog who just needs the right environment to truly thrive, and we’re hopeful that her special someone is out there waiting for her.

Gala is still in foster and gradually making progress. She is still extremely hand-shy but has started to come up and let her nose touch your hand before running off! She will then come back wanting to do it again and wagging her tail (huge progress!).Gala is looking for a forever home to offer her patience and lots of time to help her get over her fears. She is fully house trained and very happy to follow our other dogs around copying what they do. She is an escape artist on a harness as she is still nervous walking on a lead, but we have found taking her to a secure dog run field is amazing for her and she absolutely loves her freedom running around. Gala is ideally looking for some playmates in her new home as she does love to run and play with other dogs.

Gala is doing brilliantly in her foster home. She loves the company of other dogs and loves to play with them but is still very hand-shy with us humans and very wary.Gala would love a home with one or more furry friends who love playing, but what she also needs is a home which would help her understand to not be frightened anymore and people who will understand it's going to take time and patience until you get any affection or love back from her.Gala has big trust issues and needs a selfless home to get her over this hurdle she is facing.

Gala has sadly returned to the kennels through no fault of her own after a six month adoption. Her adopter made the difficult decision to bring her back due to a change in their personal circumstances, and she was much loved during her time with them. She’s now back with us and receiving lots of care and attention while we help her find another loving home. Gala is a lovely dog who truly deserves her second chance.

Gala came to us from a breeder a few months ago. We are told she is a Poodle cross Cavalier cross Bichon and she is the cutest little girl but is very overwhelmed and nervous so does need an experienced home who have had scared ex-breeding dogs before.Sadly Gala was returned after a short adoption due to a change in her adopters circumstances but was lucky enough to go to a foster home. She will need a calm and quiet home and is very scared of children so will need an adult only home with no visiting children. She will need a secure garden as she is so worried she can be a flight risk.Gala will need a home with at least one other kind and confident resident dog to be her friend and help her to settle in. She is house trained, but may need some reminders in her new home and walking on a lead is a little scary for her, so she will need more practice with this. She LOVES food and that's the way to her heart, she will take a treat from our hand, but other than that she is very hand shy and will run away if we go to stroke or approach her.This little lady just needs to find her perfect home for she can learn that people can offer her kindness and love. She is a sweet girl who with time, love and kindness will soon start to blossom.

Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Lollipop
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I've been introduced to a harness but I'm not ready for lead walking yet!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a grade 2 luxating patella and have had 7 teeth extracted. Read below for more

02-06-26 Lollipop is a lovely Bichon Frise who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is an inquisitive and funny little girl who is already showing glimpses of her playful personality. Lollipop will happily come over to lick our fingers before darting away again, as if she's still deciding whether people are quite as interesting as her kennel friends.

She definitely prefers the company of other dogs at the moment, but she is happy to follow their lead and takes great comfort from having them around. As Lollipop gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends, she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had 7 teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

Lollipop has been given the Gift of Life by Jodie Stanley

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Cuba
description:
I will need a loving and understanding adult-only home!

I'd prefer to be the only dog. I can't live with cats.

I am still unsure about the world, so a secure garden would be ideal.

I walk well on lead but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home. Read below for more!

Cuba is a very sensitive and shy boy who is still finding the world quite overwhelming, but who is making lovely progress as his confidence slowly grows. Cuba arrived with very little life experience and can be easily worried by new situations, so he needs a calm, gentle approach and plenty of time to build trust.

As he gets to know people, Cuba is becoming increasingly sociable. He may need a couple of meetings to feel comfortable, but once he trusts you, he will happily approach with his tail wagging and enjoy quiet, gentle fuss. He particularly loves relaxing in his bed with trusted company nearby and finds calm strokes very reassuring, often drifting off to sleep while being gently fussed. As his confidence grows, his playful side is beginning to shine. He adores playing with toys, cuddling, giving kisses, and will happily bounce around like a lunatic when he’s feeling safe and excited.

Cuba has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to him. He will need experienced, adult-only adopters who understand nervous dogs and are happy to let him settle at his own pace. Patient guidance will be needed as he learns all about home life, including house training and walking on a harness and lead. He has recently started harness training and is beginning to enjoy it, but this will still need to be continued slowly and positively, starting with gentle practice in the garden. Once out and about, Cuba enjoys taking in the world at his own pace and loves sniffing everything in sight on his walks.

Cuba would prefer to be the only dog in the home, so his adopters will need to be around enough to keep him company and provide reassurance as he settles.

He will need a home without cats or small furries as he does have a prey drive.

He is quite fond of using his voice and enjoys a good grumble rather than barking, which is very much part of his character. Beneath his worried exterior, Cuba is a sweet, gentle boy who has already formed strong bonds with familiar staff and is learning that not all people are bad.

Cuba will need a calm and understanding home where his boundaries are respected and he can have his own safe space. With kindness, patience, and the right support, he has the potential to continue blossoming into a truly rewarding companion.

Cuba has had a bilateral entropion repair.

Cubawill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Cuba has had quite a busy few weeks at the rescue and has had to put his big boy pants on!! I’ve started taking him into our on site cabin which is similar to being in a home environment. It’s got a sofa, bed, TV etc … so I thought it would be a good idea to start taking him in there to help desensitise him to new things.

Obviously he’s never been in a home before, so everything was completely brand new for him. The first time he was very nervous and really didn’t know what to do at all. He was holding himself low to the floor and hunched, but he was walking around doing little sniffs of things. I was sat on the sofa and he did come over to me a couple of times for reassurance which did help a little, but after about only 5 minutes I took him back to his kennel as I didn’t want to overdo it.

The second time he was still nervous again, but after a little while he did start to drop his guard and became quite curious. He kept coming over to me for a fuss and a treat, so that was a really good sign being brave enough to eat in there. He was fascinated by the TV and didn’t quite know what to think of it. He was a bit scared of it I think, but equally as intrigued. I’m going to keep taking him into the cabin once a week or so just to ease him into it slowly, and then hopefully that will help his transition to home life when he does get adopted.

Cuba has been with me for over 3 months now and I literally love him more and more every day. I’m lucky to have a very close relationship with him and he loves me and trusts me completely, so I see a side to him that not many other people get to see.

He absolutely oozes charisma and character, and he makes me laugh and smile every time we’re together. He’s fiercely loyal, super affectionate, and SO comical. He gives the best of everything. He loves running around the yard with me and playing with toys, but loves a big sit down snuggle equally as much. So much so, he now likes to sprawl across my whole lap and fall into a deep sleep on me (snores and all)! His kennel is filled with plush toys that he loves to carry around in his mouth and sleep with, and he’s SO gentle with them. Isn’t he just the sweetest boy!?

He does still find a lot of things quite challenging, but I do feel as though we’re still making steady progress, and you can’t rush certain things. He’s still very easily spooked by loud noises, cars passing, people trying to approach him etc, so on walks especially I do have to make sure I’m paying complete attention to him. Most of the time he does recover quickly with a bit of reassurance from me, but then sometimes it will ruin his whole walk and he’ll immediately want to turn around and go back to the safety of his kennel. That’s okay though - I always allow it and take him back to make sure he knows he always has a safe place as and when he needs it.

We’ve briefly mentioned in a previous update that Cuba doesn’t like other dogs that much, but I hope this won’t put you off him as he’s not reactive to other dogs out on walks or anything like that - he simply just doesn’t like to share his space with them. I don’t think he was socialised with others apart from his old kennel friend before he came to us, so I think it’s understandable.

If you have the time and the patience to put the work in with Cuba, I can promise you 10 times over that adopting him will be the best decision of your life. Once he settles, he will truly be your best friend and the love of your life. That’s how I feel about him and I’m just his kennel mum!! He is utterly special and he deserves someone equally as special, who will love him as much as he will love them. He has such a big heart and he really does deserve the world and more.

Cuba has come on leaps and bounds over the past few weeks, and I feel so lucky to have been appointed as his “Kennel Auntie,” spending two days a week with this incredibly handsome boy.

Although Cuba can still be wary of strangers, the bond he forms once he trusts you is truly something special. Knowing him from when he first arrived, you honestly wouldn’t recognise him now. He used to hide away at the back of his kennel, wishing we would go away, now he demands to be the centre of attention and absolutely smothers you in kisses. While he may take a little time to warm up to new people, once he feels safe, his affectionate nature shines through.

Cuba has taken some big steps (quite literally!) and is absolutely smashing his harness training. His progress has been incredible, and his confidence grows more each day. He happily trots along on walks, tail wagging, taking in all the exciting new smells he’s never experienced before. Watching him discover so many “firsts” is truly magical.

We’ve found that Cuba isn’t too fussed about other dogs (aside from his kennel friend Chippy), so he would be best suited to a home where he can be the only dog. This will allow him to soak up all the love and attention he thrives on.

I cherish every moment I get to spend with Cuba. He is the sweetest, soppiest boy. He is so full of love, yet not enough people get to see this side of him. He adores playing with toys, cuddling, bouncing around like a lunatic, giving kisses, and sniffing everything in sight on his walks. But most of all, he loves his people.

There isn’t a moment with Cuba where you won’t feel loved. He makes every second count and whoever is lucky enough to adopt him should do the same. He truly is a special boy, and you wouldn’t want to miss out on him.

Cuba has been on my section for a few weeks now and I am just head over heels in love with him. I knew he was a nervous and sensitive boy so I have taken things slow with him and left him be to suss me out and get used to my routine, but it really didn’t take long for him to become quite attached to me. Within a few days he started to trust me, and now I would say he actually trusts me completely. So much so, I’ve been able to start harness training with him, put medication in his eyes after his surgery, and he’s given me his belly a couple of times for fusses!!!

I still haven’t taken him outside of the secure yard on his harness yet, but I do think he’s ready so I’m going to try it really soon. His biggest fear was having any tension on the lead - he would get really spooked by it and panic - but I think we’re just about over that now and he’s gotten used to it.With Cuba, once he gets to know you and forms a bond with you he is an extremely affectionate, happy, and playful boy, but he is still standoffish with people he doesn’t know and he doesn’t trust them to touch him or handle him. This is something his future adopters will need to take into consideration and prepare for. He’ll just need to be given some time, patience and gentleness to begin with. I am certain he’ll come around, but it will need to be in his own time as he can’t be pushed.

Cuba is hilarious and so goofy, and he will make such a great addition to someone’s home in time, but it does need to be the right home to ensure he’s set up for only success. I adore him very much and I just know his future parents will too, so please keep him in mind if you think you could be a good match for him!

Cuba is making lovely progress and is becoming increasingly sociable as his confidence grows. He is still finding walking on a harness quite scary and will need a patient home willing to help him continue this training at his own pace.

Cuba may need a couple of meetings to feel comfortable, but once he knows you, he will happily approach with his tail wagging and enjoy a gentle fuss. He particularly loves relaxing in his bed with trusted company nearby, quietly enjoying being stroked as he drifts off to sleep.

At heart, he is a very sweet and gentle boy who is learning to trust and has already formed strong bonds with familiar staff. He is simply a scared boy who needs a fresh start in a calm, understanding and respectful home where he can continue to blossom.

Cuba is a very nervous and shy boy who is finding the world quite overwhelming at the moment. He needs a slow, gentle approach and plenty of time to build trust, but once he feels safe with someone, he will allow calm, gentle fuss while settled in his bed, which he finds very reassuring. Underneath his worried exterior, Cuba is simply a big, scared baby who needs kindness, patience, and understanding to help him feel secure.

Cuba will need an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand nervous dogs and are happy to let him settle at his own pace. He has never lived in a home before, so everything will be completely new to him. His adopters will need to be patient and supportive as he learns about home life, including house training and how to walk on a harness and lead. Gentle practice in the garden will be an important starting point before he is ready to venture further afield.

Cuba will also need at least one kind, confident resident dog in the home. He gains comfort and confidence from other dogs and will benefit greatly from having a calm canine role model to help guide him and show him that the world is a safe place. He is not suitable to be an only dog.

Cuba is currently learning to walk on a harness, but this is something he finds very challenging and will require a great deal of time, patience, and dedication. He is also quite fond of using his voice and enjoys a good grumble rather than barking, which is very much part of his character.

Cuba will need a calm, quiet home where he can have his own safe space and plenty of downtime alongside gentle interaction. With love, reassurance, and understanding adopters, he will slowly begin to realise that not all people are bad and that he is finally safe. In the right home, with the right support, Cuba has the potential to blossom into a deeply rewarding companion.
