name: Gabriel
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I cannot live with cats.

I may be shy now, but once I have settled I would love a nice garden I can play in!

I love going for walks, and would love an active home!

I know some tricks & walk well on the lead but will need help with housetraining.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

Gabriel originally came to us from a breeder, and for him the world felt like a very frightening place. He was worried of people, the new environments, and unfamiliar experiences left him feeling overwhelmed, and even something as simple as having a lead put on was a huge challenge. He needed time, patience, and gentle encouragement to begin to feel safe.

Gabriel was adopted for a short period, but unfortunately it was not the right fit for him, and he was returned after displaying unwanted behaviours in the home and unfortunately making the wrong choices when he felt uncomfortable in a situation, which did result in Gabriel biting. He will need a quiet adult-only home without resident or visiting children to ensure he can get the structure he is needing. Gabriel can struggle with visitors coming to the house so will need a home without too many visitors and the ability to put him in a different room when people do some over. He will need adopters who are willing to meet him multiple times to develop a bond with him!

Gabriel requires a highly structured, boundary-focused home with experienced owners who are confident, calm, and consistent. He is not a dog who should be allowed on the sofa or cuddling up with toys and we would not want him to be set up for failure. Instead, he needs clear rules, his own space, and guidance that helps him feel secure and understand what is expected of him. His adopters will need to understand that he has potential to guard high value items or sleeping spaces and will need to work with him. Respecting his boundaries is essential to his wellbeing and success.

He will need both physical and mental stimulation every single day, whatever the weather. Regular walks, enrichment, and brain games are a must to keep his active mind engaged and to help him remain balanced and settled.

Despite his difficult start, Gabriel has made remarkable progress. These days, he can’t wait for his walks and becomes visibly excited when he sees his lead come out. He now allows his harness to be put on and walks beautifully, thoroughly enjoying his outdoor adventures.

Gabriel is a very clever boy and a true foodie, which makes training both rewarding and enjoyable. He already knows cues such as “sit” and “paw” and loves learning new skills. He thrives with clear guidance, consistency, and ongoing training, and will do best with an experienced owner who enjoys working with dogs and building a strong, structured relationship.

Gabriel forms very strong bonds with his people and is deeply loyal once trust is established. Because of this, he has shown signs of separation anxiety and will need adopters who are home for the majority of the time. He is not suited to being left alone for long periods and will thrive best with someone who can make him a central part of their daily routine. While he is not a dog who seeks constant physical closeness, once a bond is formed he does enjoy affection and gentle fuss in his own way.

He could live as the only dog, enjoying one-to-one attention, or potentially alongside a calm, confident resident dog who respects his space. He will need a home with no cats or small furries.

Gabriel has worked incredibly hard to overcome his fears and has already come so far. He is now searching for a forever home that will offer him understanding, structure, commitment, and the chance to live a fulfilled life. For the right, experienced person, Gabriel will be a loyal and rewarding companion.

Gabrielwill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

This week we’ve had a heatwave which has meant alot of our rescue dogs have needed their ears checked incase they’ve had any mucky build up - Gabriel was one of the unlucky few that have needed some TLC in this area!!We’ve recently had a new meds person who has been visiting Gabriel to do his ear cleans & he has been an absolute angel. He’s even been given the nickname Angel GabrielIt’s just a testament to Gabriel that yes he can be unsure of new people, but once he knows you he truly is such a wonderful boy. He just needs someone to take that chance on him, show him the love he’s desperate to have & he’ll return it tenfold.Gabriel has been waiting such a long time now, and seeing a boy so full of love & hope is heartbreaking when we can’t reassure him that his time will come soon!!!

Today, I worked with Gabriel again for the first time in months. I was a little worried he’d have forgotten, however, it’s safe to say the bond previously made still remains.Gabriel is such an excited little boy. He lives for treats. He’s such a clever and obedient boy when the treats come out. Usually, he’s full of energy and excitement. Once the treats are out, he’s still and sits like the perfect little boy we know he can be.As he can be very busy, I’ve always thought it essential to take him out on walks, the longer the better. As mentioned in a previous update, he loves walks! Once you pull the lead out, you get a similar reaction to the treats.The longer the walk the better. Walks are so good for this gorgeous boy. They keep him stimulated and help shave off the pounds he gains from everyone giving him treats!On the whole, I was so happy to see my boy again. So happy, so loyal, keen to go on walks and he listened so well. I’m so proud of the progress he’s made since I last saw him!Gabriel still can be a challenge and, he does not like everyone. Once you’ve made that bond with him though, it stays. Don’t overlook this boy. He’s such a beautiful, intelligent and fun dog!

This boy has my heart, once you form that special bond with him I do believe it's for life. He is very loving and enjoys a cuddle and a fuss from people he feels comfortable around, as his adopter you'll hopefully get that bond through spending time with him and letting him go at his own pace.Gabriel, as most bockers do, lives for his food and treats, whenever I run him in from being in the yard I always leave a small treat in his bed or somewhere in the back for him to find, and he absolutely loves this he gets so excited knowing he'll get a treat and runs straight to the back of his kennel to find it.He loves his walks and his time in the big yard. He's the curious, adventurous type who just wants to investigate everything, a 10 minute stroll up the road can take us an extra 20-25 minutes to stroll back because he likes to explore, but I don't mind, seeing him happy makes me happy I'd never want to stop him from exploring the world.Gabriel would need an experienced, adult only home (view profile for explanation), he would need someone who is active and can provide him with mental and physical stimulation daily. He is a very smart boy and can pick things up quite quickly which is why, with the help from some treats I think he would pick up toilet training rather quickly.Please don't overlook this handsome guy just because he's not your small and fluffy type dog, Gabriel is a special boy with a lot of love to give, and for that right person/people he would become a true companion and best friend.

Gabriel, a stunning Bocker with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. This handsome boy is full of life and enthusiasm, always ready to embrace whatever the day brings. Gabriel thrives on affection and absolutely loves a good fuss and cuddle — he’s a real people-dog who enjoys being close to those he trusts.

Gabriel is a clever lad with so much potential. He’s already showing us just how intelligent he is as he responds to basic commands! With the right guidance and training , we know he’ll flourish and continue to grow in confidence, not that he lacks any confidence! He also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out on adventures.

Sadly, Gabriel has been returned to us, and we are now searching for the right forever home where he can truly settle and feel secure. Gabriel would be best suited as an only dog, in a calm and quiet home environment. We are looking for a home with minimal visitors and no children, as busy households can feel overwhelming for him.

Gabriel can display guarding behaviours, so he will need experienced owners who understand this and can manage the home environment appropriately to support him. With the right knowledge, structure, and patience, Gabriel will thrive and continue to build trust.

Gabriel has so much love to give to the right person. With understanding, consistency, and kindness, he will make an incredibly loyal and devoted time

Gabriel is a stunning Bocker who is full of life, love, and character! This gorgeous boy is bursting with energy and adores nothing more than a good fuss and a cwtch.He’s incredibly smart, and we just know it wouldn’t take long for him to be trained to a very high standard – he’s already showing us how bright he is every day. Gabriel also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out and about.Now all he needs is a forever family who can give him the love, attention, and adventures he deserves. With his brains, energy, and big heart, Gabriel is sure to make someone the most wonderful companion.

Gabriel has come to us from a breeder and has made incredible progress since arriving with us! When he first came, he was nervous around new people and worried about having a lead put on, which made walks and new kennel staff introductions a real challenge. Now, he gets excited for walk time and happily allows us to put on both his lead and harness with no issues.This handsome boy is a true foodie and loves learning new tricks. He already knows “sit” and “paw,” so with trust and patience, teaching him more tricks should be a fun and rewarding experience. Gabriel needs a confident, experienced, owner who will provide clear boundaries and structure, as he can be cheeky if he thinks he’s in charge as well as an adult-only home where he can continue to learn. Gabriel has the confidence to be an only dog in a home with can allow him the dedication and time he needs, or he can be homed with a resident companion that he can continue to learn and grow from, but will need a home with no cats or small furries.Once Gabriel knows and trusts you, he is affectionate, loyal, and loves nothing more than sharing his goofy charm. Underneath his shy moments, he is a beautiful boy with a heart full of love. He is looking for someone who will continue his training, set clear rules, and enjoy all the affection, loyalty, and joy he has to give.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Louise
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am not ready to learn about walking on a lead and harness yet.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and currently finds people and handling very frightening. Although she is still a very scared girl, she has already started to show us that, with patience and understanding, she is capable of making lovely progress.

Over the past month, Louise has grown in confidence every single day. While she is still terrified of being touched and picked up, she is no longer as shut down as she was when she first arrived. She is now more than happy to come over for treats and will happily sit close by while waiting for more. As she has begun to relax, her cheeky little personality has started to shine through. She likes to use her voice to let everyone know exactly how she's feeling, is very partial to chasing flies, and has quite a big personality packed into such a tiny dog. Watching her confidence slowly grow has been an absolute pleasure.

Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can help guide her as she settles into family life.

Although Louise takes great comfort from other dogs, she can show signs of resource guarding around food. For this reason, she will need to be fed separately from any resident dogs, and care should be taken when offering treats or other high-value food items. Her adopters will need experience managing this behaviour calmly and appropriately.

Louise is slowly becoming more comfortable with being handled, and gentle work has begun to help her get used to being picked up. While this is still very worrying for her and she can become wriggly and panic when lifted, she has never tried to bite during these sessions. We are confident this will continue to improve with time as she learns that she is safe and that nobody is going to hurt her.

Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns the basics, including house training. She is not yet ready to begin harness training or venture out into the outside world, so her future family will need to carefully plan how they will introduce these experiences when she feels ready. Everything must happen at Louise's pace to ensure she continues building confidence rather than becoming overwhelmed.

Louise is a sensitive little soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her flourish. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to surprise us with just how much she is growing in confidence. With experienced adopters, kind canine companions and lots of love, we truly believe Louise will continue to blossom into the wonderful little dog we know she can become.

Louise has been given the Gift of Life by Ann Winter

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

Louise has been on my section with me for about a month now, and I’ve definitely seen some positive changes in her. She’s still terrified of being touched and picked up, but her overall confidence is improving daily. She’s now more than happy to come and take treats from me and sit close to me while she’s waiting for more. She’s also nowhere near as shut down as she was when she first arrived and is now turning into quite a cheeky monkey. She does like to use her voice to express her feelings, and she’s also very partial to chasing flies! She’s actually got quite a big personality for such a little girl, and it’s a pleasure to see it emerging as the days go by.I’ve been working slowly on getting Louise used to being picked up, and while she’s definitely still very worried about it, she has calmed down slightly. She’s never tried to bite me, but she does sometimes have little panics and becomes very wriggly when she’s in my arms. I do think this is something that will improve over time. She just needs some more practice and to realise that we’re not hurting her. She obviously hasn’t been handled a lot in her life, so now it’s up to us to prove to her that it’s okay.I love working with Louise, and I can really see the potential in her. She just needs someone to give her a chance and work with her through all her worries and fears. She’s not ready for harness training or conquering the outside world yet, so that’s something her future adopters will need to take into consideration and make a plan for. I do believe she’ll progress faster in a kind home with adopters who have lots of time and patience to give her, so I really hope she won’t have to wait here for much longer.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and currently finds people and handling very frightening. At the moment, Louise feels safest keeping her distance and, if pushed beyond her comfort zone, may make the wrong decision and nip purely out of fear. She is a very scared girl who needs understanding, patience and time.Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience of helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing.Although Louise takes great comfort from other dogs, she can show signs of resource guarding around food. For this reason, she will need to be fed separately from other dogs, and care will need to be taken when giving treats or other high-value food items. Her adopters will need experience of managing this behaviour and the confidence to do so appropriately.Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns new skills such as house training. She is not yet ready to begin learning about lead walking or wearing a harness, as handling is still very worrying for her. These things will need to be introduced gradually and at her pace once she feels more comfortable and secure.Louise is a sensitive soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her build confidence. We will continue to work with her every day, helping her take small steps forward at a pace she is comfortable with. In the right home, with the support of canine friends and experienced adopters, we hope Louise will slowly learn that people can be kind and that life has so much to offer.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: River
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog at the moment. I can't live with cats.

I would like a secure garden in a quiet area.

I can walk well on a lead and would like an active home.

I need experienced adopters to work on my reactivity with me.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

River originally came into our care in 2020 from a breeder and was adopted into a loving home. Sadly, her family later found they were unable to continue meeting her needs, and River has now returned to us.

River is a highly intelligent, affectionate girl who forms very strong bonds with her people. According to her previous home, once she feels safe she is extremely loving, enjoys close contact and seeks reassurance from those she trusts. She loves cuddles, gentle scratches, and being near her humans, and is very in tune with their emotions, often offering comfort when someone is feeling down.

River is a clever and enthusiastic learner who already knows a wide range of cues and enjoys training, enrichment and mental stimulation. She loves her toys, especially balls and tug toys, enjoys scent games such as “find it”, and is very food-motivated, peanut butter is her absolute favourite! She settles well at home, enjoys routine and structure, and is clean and non-destructive.

River enjoys her walks and would suit an active home with access to quieter walking routes. She walks nicely on a halti and enjoys being out and about, but can find busy environments overwhelming and may be reactive to dogs, vans or motorbikes when anxious. She will need confident handling and continued training, and should remain on lead unless in a secure area.

Although affectionate and loving, River is a sensitive dog and can struggle with unfamiliar people, visitors and loud or sudden noises such as fireworks. When frightened she may bark or retreat. For this reason, River is looking for acalm, quiet, adult-only homewithvery few visitors, ideally in arural or semi-rural setting. Her adopters must beexperienced with reactive dogs, patient, and willing to work at her pace while respecting her boundaries.

We are advised that River can occasionally display guarding behaviours towards her trusted humans, such as growling if another person enters the room while she is settled. This will need calm, confident and experienced management.

River is currently looking for a home as anonly dog, although she has previously lived with another small dog and may be able to live with a calm companion following careful introductions.

River may not be suited to everyone, but for the right home she will be an incredibly loyal, affectionate and rewarding companion who has so much love to give.

A bit about River from her previous home:

Quiver, Trevor, Clever Trevor, Trev, Piggy, Pig, Squirrel, Egg Nog Dog

Riverwill need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Just wanted to share quick update for our wonderful River! Her kennel mum has been working on showing River that visiting the vets isn’t always a scary ordeal. Today, I popped in with her to see how it was going. I was SO impressed!

Although she was hesitant to come in, once in the vets she settled enough to have the biggest cuddles (River gives the BEST cuddles). We spent 5 minutes or so telling her how beautiful and amazing she is and made sure to head out before she got too worried.

River is honestly one of those special, once in a lifetime dogs. Once she bonds with you, she has this incredible ability to make you feel like the most important person in the world. She gives you her whole heart. Whoever adopts her will be so lucky to have her in their life!

Our gorgeous girl River is still on the search for a new home and family and hopefully her forever one. River is continuing to do very well here at the rescue and has progressed so much since being back with us.

Having lived in a home River knows a lot of commands and has been very well taught. She's clean in her kennel and isn't destructive at all. Although, she has lived in a home before she does still struggle at times with busy environments and people she doesn't know. When shes greeted by someone she doesn't know she will bark out of uncertainty but if you offer her a treat she tends to make friends with you pretty quickly. There were only a couple of people who could work with River initially when she came back to us due to her being so overwhelmed and worried but now half the rescue can work with her so shes made massive progress and I couldn't be any prouder of her.

She walks lovely on the lead and absolute loves going out for walks or down the big yard where she also loves to play fetch. We have been training River to understand that going to the vets isn't all that scary. We have been desensitising her by walking her up the vet steps and just sitting there for a moment praising her. Before, she wouldn't even go up the steps so for her to do this and sit there for a moment is massive for her. Our next step will be to open the vets door and go from there. River is such a special girl and when she trusts you she loves you with her whole heart and she genuinely does make you feel so loved. Being Rivers Kennel Mum is honestly the best and having all that love and affection from her is just utterly amazing.

River is continuing to do incredibly well here and is trusting more and more people she meets each day. It’s been lovely to see her confidence grow as she builds good relationships with other people. As part of her ongoing desensitisation, we’ve been walking River around the front of the rescue and gradually up towards the vets. This helps her learn that these environments are safe and nothing to worry about. Throughout this training we give her plenty of praise and tasty treats, and she is responding really well.

Considering everything she’s working through, she’s doing brilliantly. River is muzzle and Halti trained, as she can be reactive to certain dogs and can be strong when she first heads out on walks. We are working on her reactivity daily, and she is improving.

Her future adopters will need to continue with this training to help her keep progressing and feeling secure. River is an absolute darling. She has such a loving nature and truly makes you feel so loved when you spend time with her. With the right support and understanding, she would make a wonderful companion and a very special addition to the right home

River is a gentle girl who has previously lived in a home and is already kennel clean, giving her a great foundation for her next chapter. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but with time and patience, she soon shows her sweet, affectionate side. Once she trusts you, River forms a lovely bond and just wants to be close to her people. She’s looking for a kind, understanding home that will give her the reassurance and love she deserves.

Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Emrys
description:
I am looking for an adult only home with experienced adopters.

I could live with other dogs or be the only dog. I cannot be homed with cats.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Emrys is such a wonderful boy. He’s currently living in a foster home where has been for a year now and has absolutely flourished with them. He originally came to us from a farm so had very little in the way of training and socialising. This meant he could find new people worrying and during a short adoption of just a few months, he struggled to get used to a male visitor and would react towards him and redirected onto another person while stressed. He was returned to his foster home following this and hasn’t put a paw out of place since.

In foster, Emrys does very well, he absolutely adores his three collie best friends and we think he would thrive in a home with a resident dog to keep him company. We would consider an experienced home adopting him as an only dog however he loves having doggy friends so would need regular playdates. Unfortunately Emrys cannot live with cats. He is looking for a collie and rescue experienced home to help him thrive. He absolutely loves his walks and as he is such a clever lad, he will need brain games to wear out his mind too! If an active home is looking for a dog to join in on a sport like agility, we are sure he would do well!

Once Emrys trusts you, he is a wonderful companion and after an exciting walk where he gets to play with his friends, he does really enjoy a cuddle and a snooze on the couch. He is looking for a quiet, adult only home who understands collie behaviour, especially collies bred to work. When introduced to people with plenty of space to move away if he gets worried, he makes friends quickly. His amazing foster home have done so well in bringing out his silly, confident side and absolutely love his quirks. He is such a brilliant boy and has been waiting very patiently for his forever family.

Emrys has a fatty lump on the right flank that does not pose as an issue and is being monitored.

Emrys has been in foster with us for the past 10 months and has proven to be a confident, affectionate collie. He loves his walks just as much as he enjoys relaxing on the sofa afterwards.

He gets along well with both dogs and people, is clean in the house, and travels happily in the car. During his time with us, Emrys has shown no signs of reactivity and has greeted all visitors kindly.

He is a truly lovely dog and would make a fantastic, loyal companion.

Emrys has been in foster with us for seven months now, and he’s a real character. He gets on well with all dogs and, since being back with us, has shown no reactive or guarding behaviours. In the right home, he will truly thrive and make a wonderful companion.

Emrys can occasionally feel nervous around new people, and when this happens he takes himself off to his safe space, which is in the garden. From there, he’ll assess the situation at his own pace before coming back inside when he’s ready to meet someone new. It’s important that he’s given the time and space to do this calmly.

Once he knows you, Emrys is an absolute joy to be around. He loves his walks and secure field runs, is calm and settled in the evenings, and is incredibly affectionate.

With his wicked personality and loving nature, Emrys will make a fantastic companion for the right person.

Emrys has been back in foster for 11 weeks now and has settled in beautifully with no problems at all. He gets on very well with the three resident dogs as well as visiting dogs, and he is friendly with visitors and strangers outside the home. Emrys is totally house clean, travels well in the car, and is very treat-orientated, which makes him easy to train. After his walks, he loves nothing more than relaxing with his foster family.

Emrys has settled back in beautifully with his foster family and hasn’t shown any issues at all. He loves racing around the garden with the resident dogs and is starting to enjoy playing with toys and bringing a ball back.

He’s now completely house trained, walks very nicely on the lead, and is happy to travel in the car.

Emrys is such a lovable boy and is coming along wonderfully. He’ll make a fantastic companion for the right home.

Emrys is a striking, high-energy Collie who came to us from a farm where his owner could no longer give him the time he needed. After arriving he quickly found himself in foster, where he received plenty of exercise, mental stimulation, and affection, everything a clever Collie thrives on.He was adopted for a short time, but sadly returned to us after displaying behaviours in the home that hadn’t been seen while in foster. His adopters told us that Emrys exhibited some guarding tendencies and could react negatively when he felt backed into a corner or overwhelmed. Because of this, he’s looking for a calm, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand the needs of a sensitive, intelligent dog and can support him with firm but kind guidance.Emrys will need a secure garden with space to run, and a home that can provide him with plenty of structured physical and mental activity to keep him happy and settled. He’s a bright boy who’s eager to please and loves learning. With patience, consistency, and the right support, Emrys has every potential to thrive.Emrys is now back with his original foster where he has shown many lovely qualities, he is clean in the house, travels well in the car, walks nicely on the lead, and is affectionate with those he trusts. He’s also food-motivated and already learning basic commands. We believe that Emrys thrives on activity and as he has not displayed these behaviours in foster it may be because he is provided with so much stimulation and exercises. His adopters will need to keep this in mind, and ideally be very active and willing to provide him with different games and activities to keep his mind busy.Emrys could live with another confident resident dog or be the only dog in the right home. He cannot live with cats, and due to his sensitivity, he will need a home without children or visiting children.This boy has so much potential and is just waiting for the right people to help him blossom.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Criss Cross
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I'd prefer to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can now walk on a lead and harness and enjoy my walks.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Criss Cross, a big-hearted, sensitive lad who has come to us from a breeder and is slowly learning to find his confidence in the world. When Criss Cross arrived as a worried soul, needing extra patience, understanding, and gentle care. He had very little formal handling in his past, and early on could be grumbly or anxious when unsure. He required slow, careful introductions to people, places, and experiences while he started to understand his new surroundings.

While Criss Cross can still be a little shy when meeting new people, once he feels comfortable his affectionate side really shines through. He actively seeks out fuss and cuddles and has become quite the cuddle bug, often trying to return kisses to the people he trusts. He is learning his manners well and responds nicely to calm, consistent guidance.

Criss Cross is growing in confidence with his harness training and now enjoys daily walks beyond the rescue. He has even started greeting some people on his walks for a hello and perhaps a treat or a fuss. He can still feel a little unsure if people are behind him, but gentle encouragement and reassurance help him relax and continue exploring the world around him.

He has also started learning about kennel cleanliness, with staff helping him practice good toilet habits to make the transition into a home life easier for him in the future. When enjoying some quiet time on his own, Criss Cross loves exploring his toy collection, especially anything involving treats or food puzzles.

Criss Cross would prefer to be the only dog in the home so he can fully relax and enjoy all the attention for himself.

He will need a calm, adult-only home with experienced adopters who can continue helping him build confidence at his own pace. He also appreciates having a quiet space at mealtimes where he feels safe and secure. Criss Cross will need a home without cats as he is overly interested in them.

Criss Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet-natured gentle giant with so much love to give. With patience, understanding, endless bum scratches and plenty of tasty treats, he has every chance to flourish into the loyal and devoted companion he is meant to be.

Criss Crosswill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Criss Cross is such a sweetheart! He is loyal to his friend Crumble, his kennel mums and dads. He’s still greeting everyone on walks with a bit of caution but once he’s recognised you, you’re considered family.

He’s going on occasional independent walks to gain his confidence but he is always looking for Crumble to keep him company. He’s very cautious of new things however day by day his confidence is growing and with his trust in his kennel mums he always runs back to check they’re okay, showing you just how brave he is and continues to be, so when the right home finds him….they will have to earn his trust and give him the patience and love he truly deserves.

This distinguished gent is progressing so well, every day!

He has started to get in the practice of being kennel clean, one of his kennel mums likes to come in a little early to help him practice this so when he finds his forever home it might be a little less stressful learning toilet training skills properly.

Criss Cross is even getting more adventurous greeting people on his daily walks now just to  say hello and maybe scoring a treat or fuss, and even recognising some of the staff when they visit him.

He is protective of Crumble and always looks to see her catching up on their daily walks, and enjoys playing with her or being near watching over her. But when he has his solo kennel time, he has been exploring his personal toy collection, anything with a treat in it and he’s happy. This cuddle bug deserves a home with endless bum scratches and scrumptious treats

This handsome guy is progressing every day! And showing his kennel mums just how much of a sweetheart he is. He is an affectionate goofball once he’s comfortable with you. He enjoys playing with his chow friend Crumble and he loves getting love from her and his kennel mums. He loves to jump up to have his harness put on, refusing to stand still because he gets so excited to go out and explore with Crumble.

Criss Cross will now even allow some of his part time kennel mums and dads to give him attention too. He is still very cautious of new people but is slowly meeting new people and remembering them!

With some time his new family will find out just how special Criss Cross is!

Criss Cross has made incredible progress over the last few days. He used to hide and grumble when people approached his kennel, but this has changed massively!

Now, Criss Cross comes up to the kennel door and wags his tail, getting very excited to see people. Spending time with this handsome boy brings me so much joy; I often find myself straying from my section just to sneak in five minutes of cuddles.

Criss Cross is still looking for a quiet, gentle home and someone who will take things slow while he gets to know them.

Criss-Cross has grown into an incredibly sociable and interactive boy, although he can still be a little shy when first meeting new people. Once he feels comfortable, he actively seeks out attention and loves a cuddle, often trying to give kisses in return. Criss-Cross is a big lad and is still learning his manners; when he’s excited he can occasionally use his size to try and barge past, but he responds well to clear, firm verbal guidance.

He will need a quiet area to enjoy his meals, as this helps him feel more secure. Criss-Cross is doing very well with his harness training and has already ventured out of the rescue for walks, managing a good distance down the road. He can still feel a little unsure if people are walking behind him, and one of his endearing little quirks is that he finds reassurance if you turn and face him while walking backwards. Criss-Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet and gentle giant who will thrive in an active, patient and understanding home.

Criss Cross is a very worried soul who has come to us from a breeder, and is needing extra patience, understanding, and tender care. He appears to have had very little formal handling in his past and can be grumbly or anxious when he feels uncomfortable. He requires slow, careful introductions and time to begin to understand the world around him.

Criss Cross would thrive in an adult-only home with experienced owners who can provide the reassurance and consistency he needs to start building trust. He is still learning the basics of house training and walking on a lead, so his adopters will need to be patient and gentle as he gradually discovers confidence. He will need an understanding and kind resident dog in the home he can look to as he continues to learn and trust.

This sweet, sensitive boy is not yet ready for the full bustle of the world, but with time, quiet encouragement, and safe garden sniffing adventures, he will slowly open up and reveal the loyal companion he can be. Criss Cross will need a calm, loving home where his cautious nature is respected and nurtured and where he can finally feel safe and truly belong.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Primrose
description:
I am looking for an incredibly special, adult only home.

I need at least one other dog in my new home who is happy to share their bed.

I need a very secure garden in my new home.

I am not ready to learn about walking on a lead and harness yet.

I am in a foster home and am currently using puppy pads.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Primrose is a very scared little girl who has come to us from a breeder to start her new life. When she first arrived, she was completely shut down and was too fearful to even leave her bed, choosing to cuddle close to her kennel friends. She had clearly never experienced much in life before and the world around her felt overwhelming and frightening. She soon moved to a wonderful foster home, where she has spent the last several months settling in and adjusting to home life.

Primrose is a very special little dog who will need an equally special home. When she first arrived in foster, she was utterly petrified of people. For several weeks she would bury her head into her chest and hide under a cupboard just to avoid looking at her foster carer. Although she is still very fearful of humans, she has come a long way since then. She doesn’t interact with people or other dogs, but she does find enormous comfort in calm, affectionate little dogs who choose to cuddle into her.

In foster, Primrose has slowly begun to blossom in her own quiet way. She now chooses to sit in one of her three “safe places,” finding comfort in having spaces that feel secure and predictable. She has started to trust her foster family and looks to her fosterer for treats and is now even happy to be placed on the sofa next to her and on occasion has even rested her head on her lap, which is a huge step for Primrose.

At night, when the home is quiet and everyone is in bed, Primrose starts to come out of her shell and has even been seen on camera emptying the toy box and playing by herself, which is a lovely glimpse of the happy dog she may become once she feels truly safe.

Primrose is still incredibly frightened of anything beyond her safe spaces, but is now venturing outdoors into the garden. Her foster mum does have to put her outside, but when she does she is happy to explore it and runs around with excitement. She’s even played chase a couple of times with her foster brothers and sisters. Whilst incredibly nervous she is clearly coming out of her shell a little more now, and her foster mum says it’s wonderful to see this most gentle dog, finally learn it’s okay to be happy and have fun.

She is now happy to wear a harness, although she is not yet ready for walks. She is currently using puppy pads for her toileting.

Primrose will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will understand that she needs to be allowed to settle in and progress at her own pace, with no pressure or expectations.

She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog who will take her under their wing, cuddle up with her and offer her the reassurance she needs as she settles in to her new home. She seems to prefer smaller dogs and dogs around her size and is less comfortable around larger dogs.

Her adopters must be prepared to dedicate the time, patience, and kindness needed to help her continue building confidence. A quiet environment with no visiting young children is essential. Her fosterer will support the adopter through this process.

With patience, understanding, and love, Primrose has the potential to blossom fully and show the happy, affectionate dog she should have always had the chance to be. She just needs the right family to help her take the next steps.

Primrose has been given the Gift of Life by an Anonymous Supporter

Primrose is a very special little dog who will need a very special home.

She is an incredibly frightened ex-breeding dog whose past has clearly left her deeply traumatised. When she first arrived in foster five months ago, she was utterly petrified of people. For several weeks she would bury her head into her chest and hide under a cupboard just to avoid looking at her foster carer. Although she is still very fearful of humans, she has come a long way since then.

Primrose is probably the gentlest dog her foster carer has ever looked after, but also the most emotionally damaged. She is sweet, patient, and completely unassuming. She never causes any trouble, joins in with nothing, and asks for very little. She doesn’t interact with people or other dogs, but she does find enormous comfort in calm, affectionate little dogs who choose to cuddle into her. She seems to especially like small dogs and appears less comfortable around larger ones.

In foster, Primrose’s little canine housemates have gently helped her in their own way. They share her bed, steal her treats, pinch her food, take her spot on the sofa, and she accepts it all with quiet patience. If placed on the sofa or bed, she will happily snuggle down beside them. She does not actively seek dogs out for play or socialising, but she clearly takes comfort from being close to kind, cuddly companions.

Primrose spends most of her time in her safe places and will usually only move from one safe space to another if encouraged. She does not yet venture out confidently on her own. However, at night, when the house is quiet and her foster carer has gone to bed, Primrose becomes a different little soul. Caught on camera, she carefully empties every toy out of the toy box, and plays by herself. It is a lovely glimpse of the happy dog she may become once she feels truly safe.

Over the past month, Primrose has started to show small but meaningful signs of progress. She now looks to her foster carer for treats, especially when sitting together on the sofa, and she has rested her head on her a couple of times. These moments may seem tiny, but for Primrose they are huge steps forward.

Primrose is currently using puppy pads, as she is still too frightened to go outdoors of her own accord. When placed outside, she will usually tuck herself into a corner of the garden. More recently, if carried around the garden, she has started to show some interest in her surroundings. She is now happy to wear a harness, although she is not yet ready for walks.

Primrose will need an exceptionally kind, patient, and understanding adopter with experience of ex-breeding dogs or very fearful dogs. She must be allowed to go at her own pace, with no pressure and no expectations of quick progress. She needs a calm home with at least one small, affectionate dog who loves to cuddle, as canine companionship is essential for her confidence and comfort.

She also seems wary of men, particularly men with beards, and appears to feel safer with women.

Primrose is both the sweetest and the most broken little dog her foster carer has ever known. But after five months, she is slowly starting to come alive. She needs someone who can see the beauty in the smallest steps and who will cherish every tiny piece of trust she gives. For the right person, helping Primrose heal will be an extraordinary privilege.

Given the chance, Primrose will choose to sit on her own in one of her three “safe places” in her foster home. Whilst it is common for ex-breeding dogs that have never lived in a home before to not want to be near humans, Primrose unusually chooses not to be with the other dogs living in the house either.Whilst she has progressed significantly since going into care, we have decided that there is still a little way to go before we make her available for adoption.Primrose flees from one of her “safe places” to another keeping her body close to the ground. Her foster mum wants to see her walking upright as well as expose her to areas beyond her comfort zones, including outdoors which she currently fears, so she is better prepared for adoption.Whilst her progress is slow, she has still come along way from the early days when she would bury her head in her chest or hide behind or under furniture. She’s even played with a ball for about a minute, which her fosterer said was possibly the most moving experience she’s seen with a dog in years, suggesting there is a happy dog “inside” Primrose wanting to come out.She also uses a puppy pad if placed close to her bed. She eats well, is very gentle, and allows her quieter foster brothers and sisters to cuddle up to her. She also likes her tummy rubbed, is happy to be carried for short periods, and if put next to her foster mum, will lay down and sleep.Before Primrose will be made available for adoption we would like to see Primrose walking upright as well as walking outdoors which she still fears.Anyone applying to adopt Primrose will need experience with very frightened ex-breeding dogs that have never lived in a home. They will need to have at least one confident gentle dog,  ideally no larger than her, and a quiet home with no visiting young children. Importantly they will need to be prepared to dedicate the time it will take to help develop Primrose’s confidence, Her fosterer is happy to help guide the adopter going forwards.

Primrose is a very scared little girl and is unsure of her new surroundings. She hasn’t yet found the courage to leave her bed but she finds comfort in cuddling close to her kennel friends because that’s the only comfort she’s ever known.

Primrose needs a calm, adult only home with at least one gentle dog to guide her and give her the reassurance she needs and who will allow her to cuddle up to them for support and comfort if she wants to. She has never lived in a home, so everything will feel overwhelming at first. She will have no idea about house training and the garden may be as scary as being in the home at first so she will need adopters who have plenty of time and patience to help her.

Lead walking will be a new experience for her and should start in the garden before venturing into the outside world.

With endless patience, kindness and time, her new family will see Primrose slowly open up and blossom into the happy girl she was always meant to be.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Ivan
description:
Ivan is a one year old Greek Harehound, and unfortunately he is looking for a new home as soon as possible. He arrived in the UK in June 2025 at the age of five months old, and has been in a loving, supportive home since then.

But very sadly, the arrival of a baby has led to Ivan being relinquished back into our care. Our deadline to find Ivan a foster home is the middle of May, and if we’re unable to do so he will have to go into kennels.

Due to the significant life changes his family are going through, Ivan has not been given adequate attention or training over recent months.

With his family now functioning on reduced sleep, they have admitted that they no longer have the time for him and that he’s spending more and more time in his crate.

All of this change has resulted in his behaviour deteriorating as he’s found situations more overwhelming to deal with. We recognise that his environment is also not the most conducive to his needs, and this too plays a role in him needing a new home.

Ivan is looking for a semi-rural home where he has more space, a nice garden to run about in, and a family who understands hounds. He is currently living in London and is struggling with the suburban surroundings.

There are a lot of factors that he finds overwhelming and this is causing pent up frustration and anxiety. He would be much happier outside of the city where he can enjoy long walks in green spaces.

Ivan needs some time to reset, adjust to a new environment, and decompress. He is extremely food motivated, which really helps with training, and he has learnt a few tricks too.

He is also housetrained and crate trained, but does unfortunately struggle with the car which needs some continued desensitisation training.

In true hound fashion, Ivan is incredibly affectionate with his family, loves a snuggle on the sofa, and is happiest when chasing after a ball.

He’s an energetic boy and needs an active home, but he also responds well to mental stimulation and enrichment with his food, such as stuffed kongs and scatter feeding.

Ivan’s main struggles relate to reactivity and anxiety. Before leaving the shelter and in his initial UK foster home, Ivan was brilliant with other dogs and socialised with males and females of a variety of ages.

Unfortunately this hasn’t been the case since being adopted, and he is now very selective with other dogs. It is possible that in a calmer environment this may improve, and he has had good relationships with mature female dogs.

Although Ivan currently lives with a newborn and has been very adaptable to the new arrival, we’re looking for a home with older children simply to keep his environment a bit more predictable and relaxed.

Ivan is looking for a family that can give him the time, patience and training to settle in at his own pace.

We feel a change of environment will really be integral in supporting his onward progress, and we won’t be considering urban homes given his struggles in London.

We know how loving, sweet natured and friendly Ivan can be and we’re looking for a home where he can enjoy lots of adventures, a calm home atmosphere, and has the attention and understanding of a more experienced adopter.

name: Kevin
description:
Kevin is a one year old Pointer/Labrador mix who was brought into the shelter as a stray by the dog warden at the very beginning of the year.

He was quite shellshocked to start with and very overwhelmed by all the noise and comings and goings at the shelter, but within a week he had really found his feet, made some friends, and settled in well.

Kevin is a young dog at only around a year old, and is an active, hilarious and affectionate boy. He is also really beautiful (his pictures don’t do I’m justice!) but has so far been overlooked, most likely because he really does just blend in at the shelter.

It’s so much harder to get the black dogs noticed, and Kevin hasn’t been so lucky just yet.

During the past few months though, he’s taken the opportunity to make friends with lots of other dogs and due to his sociable, adaptable nature, he’s been integrated into lots of different groups.

He currently shares a kennel with a group of siblings (males and females) who have just about accepted him as one of their own! He loves to play and really gets along with other pups of a similar nature to him.

Kevin is still really only a puppy and has a bouncy, energetic nature, and is still learning every day.

He would really benefit from some basic training to work on some entry level commands and manners, and because he’s so keen to please we think he will respond really well.

He is food motivated, but also very play motivated too, and he absolutely loves to chase after a ball or run around with a toy in the yard!

The ideal home for Kevin would be an active, semi-rural home with a family who enjoy spending time outdoors, understand that a young dog needs training and direction, and are looking for a dog to really be a part of their everyday lives.

Kevin loves being with people, and can sometimes be whiney, so we think that he could potentially struggle with some separation anxiety in the early days.

Although Kevin is great with other dogs, as long as he has plenty of human company during the day we think that he would be happy enough living on his own.

He would still benefit from opportunities to socialise and interact with other dogs though, such as at day-care or on group walks. This will continue to help him grow into a balanced boy with good social skills.

Kevin is super loving and adores human affection, so we would love to see him find the outdoorsy family he deserves.

He will make an excellent companion on long walks and adventures, and he’s so ready to get out of the shelter and enjoy a new and exciting lease of life.

name: Charlie
description:
Charlie is a young, friendly, cross-breed, medium-sized dog, around 12 months old. He has beautiful, speckled markings and a gentle, eager-to-please nature.

He is breed, likely spaniel crossed with pointer, and weighs around 10 kg. He was found wandering alone but has made excellent progress in foster care and is ready for a committed home.

Charlie is friendly with other dogs and may bark when he first sees them, but his tail is wagging and he is keen to make friends.

He can be a little nervous when meeting new people for the first time, but he warms up quickly, especially if offered a small treat. He lives with two confident cats who tend to bully him.

He will chase if a cat runs, so a home with dog-savvy or confident cats is best. He is affectionate, enjoys human company and responds well to praise and reassurance.

He loves children and enjoys their company. He is still young and may occasionally mouth hands, but he is improving with consistent guidance.

He enjoys outings and behaves well in public places. He loves visiting Pets at Home and will sit politely for a sausage after breakfast at the garden centre.

He may occasionally bark in the garden, but he is learning to be quiet and will come when called. He settles quickly when asked to sit and given calm reassurance. Charlie has made good training progress.

He has good recall in an enclosed park and will come when called, and he is practising this in other environments which are more distracting. He is used to wearing a lead but still needs guidance to walk nicely and not pull on the shorter lead.

He is mostly clean in the home but may still have the occasional accident. He has learned sit, wait, down, get down and paw. He takes food gently and waits politely for his meals.

He enjoys playing with a ball, even if returning it is optional. Charlie would be best suited to a home with children aged five and over and a secure private garden.

He is better as an only dog, as he prefers one-to-one attention and forms strong bonds with his people. Dog-savvy cats are suitable. He needs an active home that enjoys walking, training and outdoor time.

He loves running in open secure fields and would suit a family who can offer regular exercise and enrichment.

name: Brandon
description:
Brandon has to be on the next flight. He’s 3 years old and when he arrived at the shelter last year he was emaciated. He was nothing but skin and bone.

Completely starved and mistreated. We suspect he was a hunters dog – made to go hungry to ‘make him a better hunter’. Brandon is a pointer and ready to find his forever home.

Unfortunately Brandon entered the shelter nearly a year ago. He has been well cared for and did initially put on some weight. But the stress of being caged up all day has got to him and he has lost weight again.

That’s why we need him in a home asap. He’s struggling. Perhaps he once knew a home and had a family. He can be fostered or adopted.

Brandon is friendly and curious of everyone he meets. He’s happy to be getting regular meals, but what he really needs now is a human to give him the life he deserves.

He enjoys any time he gets to spend with people. He’s super cuddly – true to the pointer breed.

He shares a space with both male and female dogs of similar size and can be homed as an only dog or with females and/or submissive male dogs.

After initial excitement to be out of his kennel, Brandon walks well on the lead. He is super (!) food oriented and will be a joy to train.

Overall, Brandon simply adores people and would also be ok with children aged 10+.

Brandon is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and will be castrated.

name: Barney
description:
Another day, another black dog. This boy is Barney & he is approx 2 years old. He is only medium sized cross-breed. He is currently in some private kennels in Cyprus after being found as a stray.

When he arrived, he lost quite a bit of weight through stress. He is also super clean in his kennel. Perhaps both signs that he was in a home and loved before?

Barney is only young, so he has energy to burn. He needs to get out of the kennel environment so he can live out what’s left of his youth. He cannot live with male dogs but is good with females. Equally he would be ok as an only dog.

Barney would suit most home situations – a single person, a couple, a family…

He relishes at any opportunity to engage with humans. Even at the vets he is just excited to be around people. Let’s find him his forever family so his life can start.

Due to the time he has spent in kennels, his vet fees are sponsored, so we are only asking for his travel costs to be covered.

Barney is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and will be castrated.

name: Loco
description:
It was sad to see that, after I last saw Loco 6 months ago, he still hasn’t been adopted and is still stressed. Loco is such a joy to be around. But he has that heartbreaking look in his eyes pleading you to help him.

Wondering what he’s done wrong. He’s very affectionate and a bit goofy at times.

Loco is medium sized and approx 2.5-3 years old and the shelter have been working on his leash training, sit, and down. This boy thrives on love and reassurance.

Any fosterer or adopter needs to be willing to put the work in to train him (he’s very food oriented) – as is standard for any rescue dog.

We don’t know about Loco’s background but we do know that the situation he has found himself in is very upsetting for him. This leads us to believe that he once knew not only a home but perhaps a proper family.

Any children should be 10+ due to Loco’s strength. Even though he is only medium sized, he is a strong boy.

If he is to be homed with another dog then they need to be female or a non-dominant male. He currently shares his kennel with a female.

Loco is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and will be castrated.

name: Floki (Flopy)
description:
Flopy (Floki del Valle de Duero) is a male two year old German Wirehaired Pointer. He is a wonderful boy; tall, strong and athletic with a slender, elegant body and beautiful honey coloured eyes.

Floki is a truly special dog looking for an active, loving home where he can thrive. He’s a joy to have around—affectionate and full of personality.

Loving and affectionate – he absolutely thrives on human attentionAbsolutely loves the great outdoors, he is very active and intelligent, he enjoys his exercise and training sessionsRecall training is going well, of course this will need continual work and reinforcementWalks quite well on the lead, especially after a good runExcellent in the house – usually calm, clean, and no food guarding

Floki is incredibly likeable and easy to live with. He enjoys being part of family life and settles well indoors. He may occasionally carry off socks or gloves, but never destroys anything—just his quirky charm!

He mixes well with dogs both at home and out on walks, although he may vocalise if barked at when on lead or react in stressful situations.

Floki, like most GWP, is an active dog who needs a home that can offer plenty of exercise and stimulation. He’s used to lots of exercise and training and enjoys being involved in activities, including group walks and training sessions.

He currently eats well but struggles to gain weight.

Floki is a gorgeous, affectionate, and fun companion who is an absolute pleasure to spend time with. If you’re looking for a loyal, active, intelligent and loving dog to join your life, Floki could be the perfect match.

Floki would love a rural home with lots of space and opportunity to stretch the legs

Floki was given up by his Spanish hunter because he was very keen on eating the catch, rather than returning it to his hunter!

If you are interested in giving wonderful Floki, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Flopy is currently in Hereford Essex.

name: Son
description:
Son, is a three year old male German Shorthaired Pointer. Son is a very handsome GSP, he is a spectacular dog, large and elegant in stature.

He is clearly a sensitive soul and was very fearful when he arrived at the shelter we work closely with in North Spain. He trembled and tried to move away in an extremely submissive manner.

However in the short time he has been at the shelter he is already improvement in his confidence.

Son loves the companionship of female dogs and they have helped his confidence no end. Son is still wary of other male dogs so he would fit most easily in a home with a female dog companion.

Son has a good appetite, is easy to handle as fear makes him so submissive. Son is looking for an understanding home with people and dogs that can bring out the wonderful dog hidden behind the anxious face.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Son a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Son is in Spain and is ready to travel to his forever home in the UK.

name: Enzo
description:
Enzo is a two year old male Jagd Terrier. Enzo is a really gorgeous boy. The Jagd Terrier is not often seen in the UK but might be most similar to the Fox Terrier.

Enzo is a looking for his forever home after being given up by a hunter as he was deemed unsuitable for hunting life. Now, he’s ready to leave that past behind and become a much-loved companion.

Weighing just 11 kg, Enzo may be small, but he has a big positive personality. He’s cheerful, playful, and constantly on the move, always sniffing, exploring, and enjoying everything around him.

His lively nature makes him a great match for someone with an active lifestyle who can keep up with his energy.

He is very sociable with other dogs, though confident and strong-willed. He has a brilliant, fun-loving nature, extremely affectionate and attached.

With people, Enzo is truly adorable. He is incredibly affectionate, deeply attached, and loves nothing more than being close to his humans.

He’ll happily follow you everywhere, always ready for cuddles and gentle attention, forming a strong and loyal bond.

Enzo is already very obedient when called within the safety of the shelter we closely with in North Spain, which shows great promise. However, he will need continued recall training before being allowed off lead in open areas to ensure his safety.

Enzo is looking for a home that can offer him plenty of activity, patience, and love. In return, he will give endless companionship, affection, and joy.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Enzo a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Enzo is in Spain and ready to travel to his forever home in the UK. Will that be with you?

name: Mona
description:
Mona is a 6 month old female Shepherd cross. She is currently living in a foster home in Leeds and is available for meets and greets with potential adopters.

Mona weighs 12kg now and is not expected to grow larger than 20-25kg. This sweet girl has been through a lot of hardship since she came into the world and would love to find a home and family to call her own.

She was born in a work yard in Sarajevo, Bosnia in the middle of winter, and has survived almost freezing to death, serious illness, and being chased by dog catchers.

Sadly, she lost half her tail before she was rescued, and she was in a lot of pain at the time. Fortunately, it doesn’t cause her any discomfort now and she loves to wag it!

Despite everything she’s been through, she is so very, sweet, loving and gentle. She is still a puppy and loves to play and run around! Mona lives in a foster home with other dogs, and she could live with another dog (or dogs) or as an only dog.

Mona is doing really well in her foster home and is learning what it’s like to feel safe, get regular meals and treats, as well as going on short walks discovering the outside world.

She loves her cuddles and will snuggle up next to you for reassurance and love. Mona has also discovered the joy of toys, and loves chasing her ball!

This clever girl is eager to learn and is very trainable. If she is given the time and patience she needs to settle into her new life, she will make the most loyal and devoted family member.

Mona has met cats, but unfortunately, she seems scared of them. This makes her go on the offensive, so she will need a cat free home.

She is good with children, but preferably over the age of 5, since being a puppy she can still be a bit mouthy at times, and perhaps a little clumsy.

Please get in touch if you think you can give Mona the loving home she needs and deserves.

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 6 month old female Shepherd cross. She is currently living in a foster home in Leeds and is available for meets and greets with potential adopters.

Lucy weighs 15kg now and is not expected to grow larger than 25-30kg. This sweet girl has been through a lot of hardship since she came into the world and would love to find a home and family to call her own.

She was born in a work yard in the middle of winter, and has survived almost freezing to death, serious illness, and being chased by dog catchers.

Despite everything she’s been through, she is so very sweet, loving and gentle. She is still a puppy and loves to play and run around! Lucy lives in a foster home with other dogs, and she could live with another dog (or dogs) or as an only dog.

Lucy would love a home with someone who enjoys being active. She’s doing really well in her foster home and is learning what it’s like to feel safe, get regular meals and treats, as well as going on short walks, discovering the outside world.

She is learning that cuddles are nice and will start to seek you out for snuggles when she’s feeling safe. Lucy has also discovered the joy of toys, and loves chasing her ball!

This clever girl is eager to learn and is highly trainable. If she is given the time and patience she needs to settle into her new life, she will make the most loyal and devoted family member.

Lucy has met cats, but unfortunately, she seems very scared of them. This makes her go on the offensive, so she will need a cat free home.

She is good with children, but preferably over the age of 5, since being a puppy she can still be a bit mouthy at times, and perhaps a little clumsy.

Please get in touch if you think you can give Lucy the loving home she needs and deserves.

name: Jordan
description:
He is yet another pointer found as a stray, likely discarded like rubbish by a hunter in Cyprus. He was found at the end of hunting season along with 2 other pointer boys.

He is so human oriented and loving that he doesn’t deserve to find himself in a shelter. We can only hope that his current scenario is better than his previous life.

Jordan happily shares his space with other dogs but what he truly loves is human affection and exciting walks. Once settled, it’s likely that he will be an active boy — he’s a pointer after all.

Jordan is a well rounded boy: good with dogs, friendly and loving with strangers and children, walks well on the leash, takes treats gently…there is nothing bad to say about him.

Due to his breed, it’s likely he will have medium-high energy levels once settled in a home. He will enjoy an active lifestyle but will also know how to chill and cuddle up under a blanket for the evening.

Jordan is not good with cats due to his prey drive so a home with no small furries is a must.

Jordan is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and castrated.

name: Chase
description:
Chase is a 9 month old male Labrador Retriever Cross.

Poor Chase entered the shelter when he was just a young pup. He is shy and is losing his puppyhood to a cage, seeing the same 4 walls day in day out.

He needs a nice home to help him settle so he can finish his puppyhood and make up for lost time. He will be medium sized when fully grown.

Chase has been cat tested and we think he would be OK living with cats with careful introductions (as you would with any dog).

Chase has been doing some leash training and is coming on well. But being out of his kennel is difficult for him as he is a shy boy in the shelter.

We just know that once he is in a home he will be able to be his true self and we really can’t wait to hear about his personality, we just need his family to notice him!

The good thing is, Chase loves his food so training should be enjoyable for both him and his new family.

Please give Chase a chance. It’s heartbreaking to see him still in the shelter.

If homed with children, they need to be older and patient and understand that Chase needs time to settle.

This boy is going to be the best companion for anyone lucky enough to adopt him.

Chase is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated.

name: Seth
description:
Seth is a young male English Pointer, approximately 10 months old, was found as a stray when he was just 6 months, and has been in a shelter in Cyprus ever since.

He is a typical pointer: super friendly, loving, cuddly, extremely human oriented, good with other dogs, and loves children and anyone he meets.

We suspect Seth may have been from an unwanted litter produced by a hunters dog. He was probably then dumped on the roadside to fend for himself away from everything he had ever known.

He was found with 2 other male pointers a few years older than him and has been happily living with them in a pack with some other female pointers aswell.

Seth will be a real treat to train and welcome into your home. Just as any pointer does, for those that are familiar with the breed, they make the most wonderful companions.

They don’t ask for much: a full belly, a warm sofa, a human to cuddle up with, and regular physical and mental stimulation. They go hard with their exercise but also enjoy their sofa time.

We really hope that Seth will get out of the shelter while he is still a pup.

Seth is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and will be castrated.

name: Rena
description:
Rena, 1 year old female mixed breed, friendly with everyone

Rena is such a sweet girl. If you are looking for a well rounded dog who is gentle and gets on with everyone, please consider Rena.

Rena is good with other dogs, strangers, people, and children. She has such a calming presence and you can tell she just wants to be loved. Not to mention she is also very pretty!

She walks well on the leash and is more interested in the people who are with her. She takes treats gently.

Although she is calm once out of her kennel, she does enjoy a good play with other dogs and has energy to burn.

Rena is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases.

name: Cody
description:
Cody – 3 year old male Jack Russell Terrier Cross. Whilst he might be small in size, he has the personality of dreams, never stops making everybody smile, and loves to make new friends.

Cody is a wonderful little dog with a heart full of love and a lot of character. Rescued from Romania as a puppy, he came to us with a traumatic injury to his tail, which required surgery.

He was quite a shy little pup but was adopted into a home fairly quickly.

Unfortunately, this was not the right environment for Cody and he never really settled, so a year later he was back at DC. He was adopted out again and, through no fault of his own, was returned within a few weeks as the resident dog did not like him.

Cody had been a perfect gentleman, so he came back yet again to live his best life with his Wonky friends.

Cody is a sweet and friendly dog once he’s settled but can be a little shy at first. Once he gets to know you, he’s an absolute bundle of fun!

He’s great with other dogs, loves to run around and play, and is always up for an adventure.

He’s also very curious and loves meeting new people while out on walks. Since being back in rescue, Cody’s behaviour has changed a lot and he is now a happy wee chappy with everyone he meets, including strangers.

We feel that much of his behaviour in his first home was due to his environment and that a quieter, relaxed home will bring out all of his positive attributes.

Cody has learned several commands, including Sit, Stay, Down, Watch, Come (his recall is good but could use reinforcement), and Leave It.

He is generally good on the lead and enjoys his walks, though he can be a bit stubborn at times.

Cody had shown some resource guarding in his first home but has been easily trained out of this with positive reinforcement techniques.

He should not be given bones or chew toys like yak chews, as he tends to guard them.

Cody is happy around humans on walks, even strangers, and loves to sniff them, but he’ll always do things in his own way and at his own pace.

He’s comfortable with being picked up and loves a cuddle. As Mother Wolf always says, “Never say never” for a new home, and although he is as happy as can be at the rescue, he deserves so much more and would love his own people and a home of his own.

We don’t think that Cody would like to live with small children, but older ones in a quiet home would be fine.

Cody is looking for a family who can give him the space and understanding he needs to feel safe and loved. Could that be you? If you think you’re the perfect match for Cody, we’d love to hear from you!

name: Lily
description:
Our extra special girl Lily is approximately six years old and a near perfect cross breed at the bottom end of medium sized. Lily weighs just fourteen kilos and measures fourteen inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found on the streets Lily has been in our Cyprus shelter for one month.

Our shelter manager reports that Lily is very timid and needs lots of reassurance. She is quiet, very sweet and walks beautifully on her lead. Which begs the question: what more does a girl have to do?

Lily is so attractive with her shining black coat and delicate features. Her gorgeous eyes are perfectly enhanced with her prize-winning ears and sublime expressions.
