He’s friendly with everyone he meets, including the volunteers’ children, although due to his enthusiasm and tendency to play physically, we’re looking for a home with older children or teenagers.

Affectionate and enjoys human contactGood with other dogs, though can be intense in his approachPlayful and highly activeConfident, with no obvious signs of trauma

Like many ex-hunting dogs, Cat hasn’t had the best start. As with many dogs from a similar background, food hasn’t always been guaranteed.

He’s therefore very food-motivated and will eat quickly and as much as he can, so he’ll need sensible feeding routines and management to keep him healthy and happy.

He also has a high prey drive, so he would not suitable for a home with birds or small furries.

On lead and recall are both coming along, but Cat would benefit from continued training. He travels reasonably well and handles routine situations like the vet without issue.

An active home that can meet his exercise needsOwners willing to continue basic training and provide structureEither as an only dog (with regular social contact) or with a calm femaleHe’s not a difficult dog at all (he is a fabulous, friendly and kind boy), but he’s not low-maintenance. He needs outlets for his energy and a home that understands the needs of a working breed.

Catarella is currently at our shelter in Cordoba in southern Spain but will be coming to a UK foster home soon.

All of our dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme and Brucella canis.

All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons to not do so, will be sterilised. Catarella is neutered.

Please note that we will advise medical results and treatments upon successful application.

Adoption contract and fee, homecheck and lifetime RBU (rescue back-up) apply as standard.

name: Frankie
description:
Our extra special boy Frankie is just under one year old and a rather dapper small cross breed with a strong beagle appearance.

Frankie weighs a humble eight kilos and measures ten inches from shoulder to paw. Having arrived at our Cyprus shelter as part of an unwanted litter, Frankie has been there most of life.

Frankie has a powerful facial expression which is nicely enhanced by his woeful puppy dog eyes. With the most appealing ears and a wonderful tri colour coat. Frankie’s appearance could best be described as a showstopper.

Our shelter manager describes Frankie as lively and bubbly with a great love for humans.

Recognising that he is fairly high energy, Frankie would be best suited to a family with a busy lifestyle including lots of walks and exercise.

Frankie’s nature is sublime, and his adopters will be overjoyed and truly blessed.

Frankie walks reasonably well on his lead but would benefit from more training. He enjoys his time in the car, and seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Eve
description:
Eve is a 2 year old female samoyed breed. She is medium to large size at around 17kg. She is currently in Croatia.

Eve is a playful dog. She loves people and likes to play with other dogs. She is very cuddly. She is not fully house trained but has learned to walk on a lead.

She needs a firm hand so that she doesn’t pull on the lead.

She is good with other dogs and can live with children who are over 8 years old. She has not been cat tested, but this can be arranged.

Eve is microchipped, rabies vaccinated, infectious diseases two times vaccinated.

Bordatella vaccine will be recieved before transport, castrated, Mediterranean diseases tested-negative Brucellosis tested negative, and Kennel cough nasel given before travel.

Adoption fee and home check applies, and full rescue backup is provided by Ninas Haven.

name: Bello
description:
Bello is a 2-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is described as a gentle little boy with a wonderful character, making him a lovely companion for the right home. His calm and kind nature suggests he would settle well into a caring environment.

He is suitable to live with other dogs, showing that he is social and comfortable around canine companions. However, he is not suitable to live with cats, so a cat-free home will be necessary.

This helps ensure that he can live happily without added stress or conflict.

Bello would do well in a home with older children, indicating that he is best suited to a household where interactions are more predictable and considerate.

His gentle personality makes him a good match for families or individuals who can provide patience and affection. He appears to be a well-balanced dog who enjoys companionship and attention.

His willingness to travel expands his chances of finding a suitable family.

Bello will be rehomed with a full adoption package, ensuring his health and wellbeing are prioritised. This includes being vaccinated, microchipped, blood tested, neutered, and having full RBU.

These preparations mean he is ready to transition smoothly into his new home.

A home check will be required as part of the adoption process, ensuring that Bello is placed in a safe and appropriate setting. Interested adopters are encouraged to make contact and express their interest.

He is ready to find a family who will appreciate his gentle nature and give him the care he deserves.

name: Mikey
description:
Mikey is an 12month old male Bodegero located in Spain.

This very handsome little lad is Mikey, a young Bodegero (Jack Russel type) boy about 18 months old, with a mainly white, smooth, short coat and black and brown markings on his head.

Mikey is super friendly and very loving and affectionate, he will be neutered tomorrow along with his vaccinations, passports and blood tests.

Mikey gets on well with other dogs and walks well on the lead. Poor boy was sadly found abandoned with 2 other dogs by a river bed.

We are looking for a home with or without another dog and children over 8 years old. Mikey hasn’t been tested for cats yet.Great with people and other dogs, a real character. Very good on lead healthy and has such wonderful, gentle nature.

name: Gray
description:
Gray is a 10 to 12 month old male Mastin cross located in Spain.

Gray is an adorable, big puppy boy Mastin Mix, with a fluffy, light cream, soft coat and impressive speckled facial markings. He is a gentle boy and loves affection and attention from the volunteers and enjoys being groomed.

Recently entering the shelter, they are still assessing him therefore there isnt much information about him yet apart from he’s super friendly with people and other dogs, he likes to join in play and chase toys and balls.

Poor boy is only approximately 10/12 months old, has never been on a lead and so the training already started. Gray is doing well, a bit overwhelmed and a bit nervous but he is gaining confidence every day.

It’s thought that he is a Mastine mix as he’s not overly massive, but still a big lad and is filling out nicely.

Gray loves to get out walking with the other dogs and is very sociable and loves his walks but is not cat tested yet. We really want a loving home for this fella with another friendly dog and children over 12 years.

Very friendly people and dogs. gentle nature, and is obedient, and a laid back boy.

name: Pablo
description:
Pablo is a 4 year old male Mastin cross located in Spain.

Pablo is an adorable, big boy, with a fluffy, light cream, soft coat, and black masked face. He is a gentle boy and loves affection and attention from the volunteers and enjoys being groomed.

Pablo is very sociable and loves his walks and other dogs as you can see in the video but is not yet cat tested (but he does like horses!) but they can do this if required.

Out on walks he likes to saunter along close by the handlers sides. He is a gentle giant, fine with children, this poor boy was already abandoned once before as a puppy near the Granada dog pound.

Pablo has a good nature and would equally be suited as an only dog or with other dogs. We think he would thrive in a loving home, with some much deserved TLC and a garden to plod around in.

A definitely brilliant all rounder, super social with everyone, so we really want a loving home for this fella because he has been abandoned twice now at such a young age and so he deserves a place of his own now and with some initial time to settle he will make a loyal, loving family pet.

We think children over 12 would fit with Pablo well.

Very friendly with most animals especially horses and other dogs of all sizes. Loves people and walks well on lead.

name: Rolo
description:
Rolo is a 5year male pointer located in Spain.

Rolo is a gorgeous, medium-sized, adorable Pointer boy, with an all black, sleek coat. Rolo is such a lovely dog, who hasn’t had a very nice life so far. He’s a typical Pointer: strong, energetic, friendly and affectionate.

He is not at all aggressive, but he is quite boisterous! Rolo is obliging on the lead, he pulls at first, because he is so happy to be out and free, but soon becomes more manageable.

We are working with more training on the lead.He is 65cm at the shoulder and about 27 kilos. He is a gentle boy and loves affection and attention from the people who visit him.

Poor Rolo belongs to an elderly man, who used to use him for hunting. However, the man can no longer get about, and he has left Rolo to live on his own, in a pen on a piece of land outside the village.

The man’s daughter-in-law feels very sorry for Rolo and she visits as often as she can (twice a week) to feed him and let him out of the pen for a run around, which he adores.

But poor boy spends 90% of his time alone. He is lonely and frustrated. He longs for human company and has so much to give to his new owner.

Rolo is not cat tested and hasn´t shared with other male dogs up to now, but he has a good nature and would equally be suited as an only dog or with another female.

We think he would thrive in a loving home, with some much deserved TLC and a garden to plod around in he will make a loyal, loving family pet. We think children over 10 would fit with Rolo well.

Energetic and great with people and dogs. Happiest when out walking and getting fuss.

name: Tim
description:
Handsome Tim is a sweet natured, friendly and affectionate chap. He enjoys going on sniffy adventures and is curious of the world around him.

He is social with other dogs but can be a little excitable for some, so will need an owner that will be able to continue with his training and socialisation and provide him with guidance where needed.

He loves to be with his people and is always up for meeting new friends! Tim is a happy and loving boy and will make a wonderful companion in the right home.

Tim can live in a flat as long as there is access to a private garden. He can live with sensible junior/secondary age children as long as they will give him space when needed.

He could potentially live with a calm, well adjusted, large breed dog, subject to a successful meet at Mayhew. Tim has been microchipped, neutered, will have received his first vaccination and is up to date with flea & worming treatment.

He has also been health checked and behaviourally assessed. Lastly, every dog adopted from us will go home with 4 weeks free pet insurance.

name: Tuna
description:
Tuna is a medium-large sized Griffon cross and she is 7 years old.

Tuna arrived in the UK from Spain on Saturday 28 March 2026. She is 7 years old (DOB 30/1/2019). Tuna is 57cm high, 97cm long, 22kg.

Tuna is in good health and has previously lived in a home in Spain. She had a lump removed from her leg before she travelled which was benign.

Tuna came to me as a foster on Sat 28th March and has been the perfect house guest. She settled in really quickly and is very calm in the house.

She gets on well with both my dog and x2 cats. She is clean in the house standing by the back door to go out and have a pee. We crated her the 1st night but now she is left out at night as just settles quietly on a bed and sleeps all night.

We have left her for short periods during the day (3 hours ) and again she just goes to sleep when we leave the house. She is good with her food, eating at a normal pace and is not food possessive, but is fed separately from my dog.

When given a treat she goes off somewhere quietly to eat it.

She is walked on a harness but is very strong and does pull and has a very strong hunting drive if a scent or sight of a deer or squirrel is seen where she barks and just wants to get to it.

When this happens I pop a figure of 8 halti on her and this gives much more control and enables her to calm down. But she is very strong and you will need to be well attached to her so she does not pull off from you.

On a road walk again she is walked on a halti and is very well behaved, not spooked by anything at all.

She has ZERO recall and is not receptive to her name at all when out so she must be kept on a lead otherwise she will be long gone.

We have not had the chance to go to a dog park yet but she does like a good coffee shop especially if there is a pupachino on offer.

We have met lots of dogs on our walks and to be honest she is indifferent to them not going out of her way to say hello or interact with them but is fine if they come up to her.

She absolutely loves being cuddled and will sit with her head on your knee wanting love and will paw you when you stop wanting more.

She really is a lovely, kind and gentle dog and will make someone a very special pet.

name: Odi
description:
Odi is a large sized Griffon cross and he is 6 years old.

Odi is 6 years old (DOB 12/8/2019) and we have been asked to rehome him. He arrived at his owners in Jersey when he was only 16 weeks old.

He has always lived in a home but he was given up as his owners could no longer walk him. He is now in foster care in Staffordshire looking for a new home.

Odi has only been with us a short time but we have seen his character come through. He is a very loving lad and likes to be wherever you are.

He is clean and obedient. He can do sit, and paw, and will lie down when asked. We have found that although he gets on with our pack we feel he would prefer one to one where he can get lots of attention.

He loves to be outside and go for walks, although we were told he was strong on the lead, it’s not something we have found. He has had a groom to make him more comfortable. He will make a wonderful companion.

Odi can live with other dogs but he is used to living as an only dog with undivided attention which we think he prefers. He was groomed on Friday but the last photo shows how hairy he will become.

name: Tina
description:
Tina is a 4-year-old female English Setter. She is described as a medium-sized dog who is both cheerful and full of life. Her background shows she was sadly given up when her hunter became ill and could no longer care for her and the others.

She shows no signs of fear in the shelter environment, which highlights her confident and well-balanced nature. Tina is very friendly with other dogs and currently shares her kennel with four others, all of whom she gets along with well.

This makes her a great candidate for a home with resident dogs.

With people, Tina is extremely affectionate and enjoys plenty of cuddles and attention. She is an energetic girl who loves to run and play in a secure outdoor space.

Her lively personality means she would thrive in a home that can match her energy and provide regular activity.

She is suitable to live with cats and children, making her a versatile choice for many family types. Tina’s loving and sociable nature means she would integrate well into a home that can offer companionship and care.

She is currently in Spain but can travel to the UK for the right home.

name: Jara
description:
Jara is a 7-year-old female English Setter. She is a medium-sized dog who was also given up when her hunter became unwell and could no longer look after her. Despite this, she has maintained a happy and confident personality.

She is very energetic and enjoys greeting people with enthusiasm, often seeking out cuddles and affection. Jara gets along well with the dogs she shares her kennel with, showing she is comfortable living alongside other dogs.

Her adaptable nature means she could fit into a variety of homes.

Jara is suitable to live with children, making her a good option for families. While her compatibility with cats is not confirmed, she can be tested for the right home.

This flexibility may open up more opportunities for potential adopters.

She is currently based in Spain and can travel to the UK. Jara would benefit from a home that can provide her with both physical activity and affection.

Her confident and friendly nature makes her a lovely companion.

name: Tala
description:
Tala is a 1-year-old female English Setter. She is a young and energetic medium-sized dog who was also given up when her hunter became unable to care for her.

Her age means she has plenty of energy and enthusiasm for life.

She is described as overflowing with energy and is incredibly happy and confident around people. Tala loves attention and would happily spend her time being cuddled and fussed over.

Her affectionate personality makes her very engaging and rewarding to be around.

Tala gets on very well with other dogs and enjoys their company. She responds when called in the shelter, although this may change in more stimulating environments like walks.

Her sociable nature makes her a good fit for homes with existing dogs.

She is suitable to live with children and can be cat tested if needed. Tala is currently in Spain and can travel to the UK.

She would thrive in an active home that can provide both training and plenty of exercise.

name: Terry
description:
Terry is a 10-year-old male English Setter. He is a medium-sized dog from the Basque Country who was sadly given up because he was no longer considered useful for hunting. Despite his age, Terry is incredibly active and full of energy.

He proves that age is just a number, as he is always on the move and eager to stay busy. Terry would love a home where he can enjoy regular walks and outdoor activity.

His energetic personality means he would suit adopters who can keep him mentally and physically engaged.

Terry is friendly with other dogs and affectionate with people. He enjoys human company and would benefit from a loving home where he can receive plenty of attention and care. His sociable nature makes him a pleasant and engaging companion.

It is noted that Terry eats very quickly, likely due to not always having reliable access to food in the past. In a new home, he would need to be fed separately from other dogs and may benefit from using a slow feeder bowl.

With time and stability, he can learn that food will always be available to him.

He is suitable to live with children and can be cat tested for the right home. Terry is currently in Spain and transport is available to the UK. He would thrive in a caring home that understands his needs and appreciates his lively personality.

name: Suzy
description:
Suzy is a 6 month old female Cane Corso who has come into rescue as her owner has sadly been paralyzed in an accident.

She is a friendly girl who loves cuddles and company and doesn’t like being on her own so will need a home with someone around.

Suzy is a large puppy who will need further training as her brain and body are still developing.

Although Suzy has been good with dogs on walks, she has never lived with another dog and isn’t sure about sharing her humans’ indoors.

So would need a calm male dog and space within the home so introductions can be built up slowly in that environment after successful introductions here at rescue.

Suzy is a big clumsy girl who would chase cats and has no experience of children so an adult home is required.

name: Kira
description:
Kira is a 1-year-old female English Setter. She is a medium-sized young dog who was given up because she was no longer wanted for hunting.

Although initially reserved, she quickly becomes affectionate and trusting once she gets to know people.

With people, Kira is described as docile, loving, and very happy to receive cuddles and fuss. Her gentle personality makes her a sweet and rewarding companion.

She would likely do well in a calm and patient home that can help build her confidence further.

Kira shares her kennel with four other dogs and gets along very well with them. They happily eat and play together, showing that she is social and comfortable around other dogs.

This makes her suitable for a home with resident dogs.

She is suitable to live with older children and can be cat tested for the right home. Kira is currently in Spain and transport is available to the UK.

She would benefit from a loving home where she can continue to blossom and enjoy plenty of affection.

name: Marvel
description:
Marvel is a 1 year old male Cross-Breed currently in Cyprus and can travel upon request.

Marvel was found by a man who did not know where to post or who to ask for help regarding this poor boy.

Due to his circumstances, Marvel was kept tied in the man’s yard for six months while he tried to seek help for him.

A lovely lady offered to help and took him to a private kennel, where she has been caring for him.

Marvel is now under our care, and we are trying to find him the best home he deserves after all he has suffered in his short life.

He is a very friendly, energetic, and playful boy, but also very cuddly. He is approximately 1 year old and is very friendly with people and other dogs.

He will be rehomed with an adoption package including vaccination, microchip, blood tests, neutering, and full RBU. A home check applies.

name: Adonis
description:
Adonis is a Labrador Retriever mix, around 6 years old, and one of the 27 dogs rescued last October from a heartbreaking hoarding situation — a place where fear and neglect shaped the start of his life.

When he first came to us, Adonis was completely shut down. He kept his distance, unsure of everything around him, and had no reason to trust the world or the people in it.

But slowly, with patience and gentle care, Adonis has begun to blossom… and what a transformation it has been.

Today, he is a completely different boy. Adonis now comes over for cuddles — something that once felt impossible — and it’s truly incredible to watch. Each time he chooses to come close, to lean in, to accept love, it feels like a small victory.

He is still a sensitive, slightly shy soul, especially in new or unfamiliar situations, but he is learning every day that he is safe. He walks beautifully on a lead, happily takes treats, and most importantly, he wants to connect.

Adonis is looking for a calm, quiet home where he can continue his journey at his own pace. A home that understands his past and will meet him with patience, kindness, and love will be exactly what he needs to keep growing in confidence.

He could be perfectly happy as an only dog, soaking up all the attention, or he could share his home with a calm, gentle, and well-balanced dog who will respect his space and help him feel secure.

Adonis may have started life with very little, but he has shown just how much love he has to give. Watching him open up is something truly special — and his future family will be incredibly lucky to be part of that journey.

All he needs now is a place to finally call home.

name: Peaches
description:
Peaches is a 1 year old female Cross-Breed.

Peaches is a very friendly, playful dog who can be excitable and a little nervous at times. She enjoys toys and interaction, and has a bright, outgoing personality.

• Excited when someone enters her kennel and likes to try to play.

• Accepts a collar and harness, though she can be a little resistance when putting on the harness. Once on the lead, she is very excitable, pulls, and can be strong. This will need ongoing help and training. She would benefit from dog training classes

• Has lived with and is friendly towards other dogs.

• Playful and sociable, enjoys interaction with other dogs.

• Toilet Training: Has only ever been in a kennel therefore will need to start toilet training from scratch and the new family need to be prepared to work through this and understand it can take time.

• Crate / Kennel Behaviour: Has been destructive on occasion — for example, she and her kennel mate pulled down a board between kennels.

• Separation: Shows no signs of separation anxiety; comfortable left alone overnight.

• Very active and excitable, particularly around new people and on walks.

Peaches is a friendly, playful, and social dog who enjoys interaction with people and other dogs.

She is best suited to a home with children aged 7 or older, and an adopter who can provide consistent training, mental stimulation, and regular exercise to manage her excitable nature.

While she can be slightly nervous, she has a loving personality and is eager to interact with her environment.

name: Margot
description:
Margot is a 1 year old female Cross-Breed.

Margot is a nervous and reserved dog initially, especially when meeting new people. When someone enters her kennel she will typically retreat to a safe space and avoid interaction at first.

Once she becomes familiar with the person, she shows that she is a very sweet-natured girl.

Margot is slightly unsure when having her harness put on, but she will tolerate it with gentle reassurance and patience.

Margot is very early in her lead-walking development. Walks slightly behind the handler.

Frequently checks in for reassurance. Can become spooked by loud noises or sudden movements. May spin on the lead when frightened.

However, her confidence is steadily improving with time and experience. Margot is not yet ready for off-site walks, so her exposure to external stimuli (traffic, busy environments, etc.) has been limited so far.

Margot does toilet in her kennel, so she will likely need continued toilet training in a home environment.

Margot’s carers say Margot is a very sweet kind natured little girl but does lack confidence and will need someone patient to build a bond with her. Margot enjoys 1-1 grooming sessions with the staff.

name: Kenny
description:
Kenny is a 3 year old male Cane Corso and is extra large in size, weighing 53 kilograms.

Kenny was visited at home by a Pawprints volunteer who conducted an in-person assessment. She described Kenny as “calm, loving and friendly” upon meeting him, and said he was “a Velcro dog who wanted to lean in for cuddles”.

Typically, Kenny is welcoming towards guests in the home and can be quite vocal about it. He will bark due to excitement and does not intend to be intimidating; he is simply thrilled to see new people.

Kenny currently lives with Willow, a 4 year old Staffordshire Bull Terrier Cross, who he has a good relationship with. Despite Kenny’s size, Willow is regarded as the “boss” of the pair. Kenny is indeed a gentle giant.

The pair have a very good relationship, often sleeping alongside each other and playing together, but they are not bonded and can be rehomed separately. He is socialised around other dogs, in particular a much smaller dog belonging to a family member.

He enjoys their company and is completely non-confrontational.

Kenny’s current family includes a 17 month old child whom he adores. She is very affectionate with Kenny and loves to share her toys with him. Kenny’s behaviour has always been appropriate around children and has not given any cause for concern.

Kenny accepts a collar, lead and harness. He typically loves his walks and was previously walked on a daily basis, with a weekly visit to a dog field so he could run off lead.

His owner reports that he is keen to engage with other dogs while out and about and will pull towards them in excitement, occasionally barking in greeting.

Unfortunately, Kenny is not getting any regular exercise at the moment.

Our volunteer took Kenny for a walk during the assessment and noted a bit of a stubborn streak when he was reluctant to leave the house without Willow. Therefore, it should be noted that he has the capability to hunker down and put the brakes on if things are not quite to his liking.

Kenny was very excitable and did pull quite a lot. This is understandable given the fact he had not been out for a number of weeks. The assessor felt he would need some reminder work on lead training, particularly as he is a very strong dog.

Kenny is fed once a day in the late afternoon or early evening, and he sleeps well overnight. He has recently been spending time in the garden before settling down for the night. He has previously eaten his own poo, so needs to be observed while in the garden. He has also, on occasion, chosen to defecate in the kitchen with the purpose of eating it.

Kenny is toilet trained but not crate trained and enjoys being close to his humans while indoors. He tends to swipe things, particularly from worktops, that he is not supposed to have and will try to eat them as soon as possible.

Kenny has attended training classes in the past and understands basic commands such as sit, off and here. He is also trained to sit nicely and wait for his meals.

Kenny has never shown any aggressive behaviour but has previously displayed food guarding issues. This was as a young puppy and is no longer problematic.

He still is not comfortable with being touched while he eats and may “give the side eye”, but he does not growl or show any other concerning behaviour.

Kenny is frightened of water. He does not like baths at home, hosepipes or swimming outdoors. He will happily go to the groomers to be washed there, and his owners describe him as “placid and happy to be handled”.

This is what our assessor had to say about Kenny:

“Kenny is a perfect dog for someone strong, with large breed experience. He seemed very trainable and well-natured. His current owners obviously have firm boundaries, which have made him into a lovely dog. As long as these are kept, he will be a wonderful family dog.”

name: Rusty
description:
Rusty is one of the 27 dogs rescued last October from a heartbreaking hoarding situation — a place where love, care, and basic safety were missing for far too long.

When he was found, Rusty was in terrible condition. He had been attacked and suffered from severe, open wounds that required urgent and prolonged veterinary care.

He spent weeks at the clinic, where his wounds were cleaned and treated every single day. While this was a difficult time for him physically, it became a turning point in his life.

Thanks to the patience, consistency, and kindness of our incredible vets, Rusty slowly began to learn that human hands can be gentle, and that he is finally safe.

Today, Rusty is still a shy boy — but he has already come such a long way. He now walks on a lead and will come over happily for treats, showing his growing trust and curiosity.

While he isn’t ready for cuddles just yet, he is quietly building confidence every day, and it’s truly beautiful to watch.

Rusty is looking for a special kind of home — one that understands that healing doesn’t happen overnight. He will need a calm, patient environment where he can continue to blossom at his own pace, without pressure or expectations.

A home with another calm, well-balanced dog would help him feel safe and show him the way.

A quieter setting is essential for Rusty — he wouldn’t cope well in a busy or chaotic home or city life. What he needs most is stability, kindness, and someone willing to give him the time he was never given before.

Rusty may not be the dog who runs straight into your arms, but he is the one who will quietly change your life in the most meaningful way. Watching him learn to trust, to feel safe, and to slowly open up is something truly special.

After everything he has been through, Rusty deserves nothing less than a forever home where he can finally just be a dog — safe, loved, and understood.

name: Fluffy
description:
Fluffy is a 20-month-old female Shih Tzu Cross. She is described as a sweet, playful, and happy young dog who still has plenty of puppy-like energy and behaviour.

Despite her young age, Fluffy has already experienced a difficult start in life, having had two litters before reaching 18 months old. She would now benefit from a calmer and quieter environment where she can finally enjoy being cared for herself.

She is friendly with people and enjoys human company. Fluffy is also good with other dogs and has experience socialising with them positively.

Her affectionate and cheerful nature makes her an enjoyable companion to have around the home. She appears eager to interact and bond with those around her.

Fluffy has previously lived with cats. However, it is noted that she may chase cats in the garden if they run, so careful introductions and supervision would still be sensible in a new home.

Inside the home environment, she has already shown that she can coexist with cats. Her playful instincts simply become more noticeable outdoors.

She is considered suitable for homes with children aged eight years and above. As Fluffy is still young and energetic, older children who understand how to behave calmly around dogs would likely suit her best.

A quieter household is preferred because she has come from a chaotic background with significant responsibilities at a very young age. She deserves stability, patience, and time to settle properly.

On walks, Fluffy can currently be a little chaotic on the lead, although work is already being done to improve this. She has been exercised using a long training line and enjoys running freely while showing a good recall response.

Continued positive reinforcement training will help her build confidence and improve her lead manners further. She appears intelligent and willing to learn.

Fluffy also enjoys her food and is happy eating both raw and cooked diets. Her enthusiasm for meals may make ongoing training easier, as food rewards can be used positively.

She is currently located in Billericay, Essex and can be met there for the right home. Fluffy is now looking for a loving family who can offer her the peaceful and caring future she deserves.

name: Cametito
description:
Hi… I’m Camelito a small size 4 year old cross breed boy.

I’m still learning how to be brave, but I think I’m finally ready to tell you my story.

I came from a place where there were 26 of us… all living in conditions no dog should ever experience. We were hoarded, handled badly, and taught that human hands were something to fear.

When I was rescued, I was absolutely terrified — the world felt huge and loud, and I didn’t know who I could trust.

But that was back in October… and since then, something amazing has been happening. I’ve been getting braver. Little by little. Day by day.

At first, I couldn’t even look at people without shaking. Now? I take treats from the volunteers with my tail gently wagging. I even walk up and ask for soft petting — just a little, but enough to show I’m trying.

And they tell me all the time how proud they are of me. I like hearing that… it makes me feel like maybe I really can become the confident boy everyone believes I can be.

I’m still scared of walking on the lead. It’s not the lead itself — it’s the fear of the unknown, the memories I’m trying to forget. But I’m working on it, and I’m trying so hard. I promise I’ll keep trying.

I’ve reached the point where the shelter can’t help me grow much more. I need something different now — a home. A real home. Somewhere calm and kind, with patient humans who understand that healing isn’t a straight line.

I’ll have good days and harder days… but I know I have so much potential. I know I can learn to trust completely with the right family by my side.

I’m not asking for perfection — just understanding. Just time. Just a chance.

If you’ve ever looked at a frightened dog and thought, “I wish I could show you the world isn’t such a scary place…”then maybe you’re the person I’ve been waiting for.

I’m ready to take the next step.I’m ready to try.I just need someone who believes in me.

If you think that might be you… I’m here, hoping you’ll notice me.

name: Takis
description:
Meet Takis a small size beagle cross boy.

Takis is around 4 years old and a true survivor. He was rescued during the devastating wildfires last July, but his story started long before that.

Most likely abandoned as a puppy, Takis grew up alone in the mountains, learning to survive the only way he could.

Food was never guaranteed — he relied on a small local tavern that only opened on weekends, and the occasional kindness of visitors staying in nearby holiday homes. It was a fragile existence, but it was all he knew.

The villages were destroyed, the land was left burnt and empty… and somehow, Takis survived. But survival wasn’t enough anymore. The tavern stopped opening, the visitors stopped coming, and suddenly there was nothing left for him.

Takis was so shy he wouldn’t let anyone come closer than a metre. It took patience, planning, and four weeks of effort — but eventually, we managed to trap him and bring him to safety.

He was diagnosed with leishmania. Thankfully, his organs were not affected, and after completing his treatment, he is now doing really well.

Today, Takis is still a shy and sensitive boy, but he has come such a long way. He enjoys being outside, walks nicely on a lead, and is even starting to play with other dogs — something we could have never imagined before.

Takis is looking for a very special home. A calm, quiet environment with people who understand that love doesn’t always look like cuddles at first.

He will need patience, kindness, and the freedom to build trust at his own pace — even if that means loving him from a little distance in the beginning.

Because one day, that distance will close.

And when it does, it will be something truly special.

Takis has survived everything life has thrown at him. Now he deserves more than survival — he deserves a home, safety, and love for the rest of his life.

No dog should spend their life in a shelter…especially not one like Takis

name: Snickers
description:
Meet Snickers a medium size labrador cross boy.

Snickers’ story is one of those that stays with you. He and his siblings were found in the middle of a busy highway… tiny 4-month-old puppies left to survive the unthinkable.

Sadly, not all of them made it — some were hit by cars, and one disappeared and was never found.

Four of them were rescued. Snickers was one of the lucky ones.

His siblings — Bueno, Mars, and Bounty — didn’t wait long before finding their forever homes. But Snickers is still here… still waiting.

He was always the shyest of the four, and while his journey has been slower, it has also been incredibly special to watch. Over the past 15 months, Snickers has made beautiful progress.

He now gets excited when he sees us, eagerly waiting for his lead so he can go out to the playground — his favourite place, especially when there are treats involved.

Snickers is still a sensitive boy. While he will allow touch, he doesn’t fully enjoy cuddles just yet — but that’s simply part of his journey. He is learning, growing, and gaining confidence every day.

He is great with other dogs and would benefit from a calm, understanding home that will continue to build his confidence at his own pace.

A family who sees beyond the shyness, and understands that trust takes time, will be the perfect match for him.

Snickers may not run straight into your arms… but once he lets you into his world, it will be something truly special.

After everything he has been through, he deserves his chance.

name: Ron
description:
Ron is a four year old male Brittany. Ron is a very handsome boy. Small in size with a robust frame and vibrant colours.Ron is exceptionally attached to people.

He would like to spend all day by your side! He loves cuddles and caresses and has a very good appetite too whihc will be great for training!

Ron is very sociable with female dogs and but a little wary of other males, he will soon be neutered and we will see if he settles down more then.

He is a very active dog, he loves to be out in the enclosure having a run.

Ron was handed in to the shelter we work closely with in North Spain by his hunter. Ron is one of the many unwanted Spanish gun dogs.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Ron a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Ron is in Spain and ready to travel to his forever home in the UK.

name: Peru
description:
Meet Peru a 5 year old medium size terrier cross boy.

Peru is one of the 27 dogs we rescued last October from a heartbreaking hoarding situation, and his little body tells a story no dog should ever have to live through.

He is covered in scars… countless reminders of the life he endured, likely from repeated attacks and a complete lack of protection. While his wounds have healed on the outside, it’s clear that inside, he is still learning how to feel safe.

And yet, despite everything, Peru is the gentlest soul.

He is a sweet, sensitive boy who just needs time to understand that the world is no longer a place he needs to fear. He has already made beautiful progress.

He will walk on a lead, even if it’s not his favourite thing, and once he reaches the playground, you can see a different side of him — a dog who wants to enjoy life, who finds small moments of happiness.

Peru finds comfort in other dogs and will often look to them for reassurance. Sometimes, he still needs a little help — we even carry him outside on harder days — but that only shows how much he is trying.

Peru is looking for a very special home. A quiet, calm environment with patient people who will give him the time and space he needs to heal. A home with another kind, friendly dog will make a world of difference for him.

He may carry scars from his past, but they do not define him.

With love, patience, and understanding, Peru has every chance to become the happy, secure dog he was always meant to be.

name: Vroula
description:
Vroula is one of the 27 dogs rescued from a hoarding case back in October, and her story is one of quiet progress and gentle bravery.

She is still a very shy girl, but slowly, step by step, she is learning that the world doesn’t have to be so scary. Handling her has become much easier, and although she still keeps her distance in the playground, we are starting to see little flashes of curiosity.

Every now and then, she will come a bit closer for a treat or even allow a gentle cuddle from the children — small moments that feel huge for a dog like Vroula.

She is more wary of men than women and will need time to build trust, patience truly is key with her.

She is not yet walking on a lead, so she currently needs to be carried, but even here we see improvement as she becomes more comfortable with each passing week.

Vroula will need a calm, quiet home with patient adopters who understand that trust cannot be rushed. A home without too much pressure, where she can go at her own pace and continue building confidence.

Another calm, confident dog could really help show her the way.

She may not be the dog who runs straight into your arms on day one… but with time, kindness, and love, Vroula will get there. And when she does, it will be something very special.

name: Obi
description:
Obi is a 5 year old male Chihuahua Cross.

Obi is a sensitive worried boy who will be looking for a kind patient home to build his confidence.

He is a fun active boy who loves his walks and playing and will looking for a new home who can match his energy levels.

Obi is looking for a calm quiet patient home where adopters will give him the space to bond and trust. He would like access to his own secure garden to help with confidence building.

He is housetrained, ok travelling, and may prefer a home with company. Obi can be worried by lots of noise and activity so would prefer a quiet home in a quiet area.

Obi can be worried when meeting new people and will require a calm quiet patient approach to making friends.

He will bond closely with those he trusts and becomes a cheeky affectionate boy! Obi may prefer an adult only home or a home where any children are older teenagers who would be happy to take a slow approach with him.

He may prefer a home with no young visiting children.

Obi has previously lived with other small dogs and has previously been described as social with other dogs. Obi can be worried by bigger dogs but is social with small dogs.

He may prefer to be the only dog in the home but could potentially live with a small confident female dog

Not suited to living with cats, birds or small animals as will chase.

Obi would like a home with an understanding of, and the time to, support him both behaviourally and emotionally. A home that understands he will need a gentle approach when making new friends.

Obi will require several meets to get to know someone.

name: Ayaz
description:
Ayaz, 5 years old medium size cross breed male.

Ayaz is one of the 27 dogs rescued from a hoarding case back in October, a group of dogs who had never known normal life, kindness, or what it means to feel safe.

He is a gentle, sensitive boy who has already made lovely progress. Ayaz walks nicely on a lead and really enjoys getting out, often getting excited when it’s time to go for a walk.

It’s a big step for a dog with his past, and he’s embracing it more and more.

He finds comfort in other dogs and will need a home with a confident canine companion to help him feel safe and continue learning about the world.

Ayaz is still unsure when it comes to human affection. He’s not quite ready for cuddles yet and prefers to keep a little distance, but we can see the soft, trusting boy underneath.

With time, patience, and a calm environment, he will get there.

Ayaz will need a quiet home with understanding adopters who won’t rush him. A home where he can build confidence at his own pace and continue to blossom.

He may not be the dog who runs into your arms right away… but with the right family, Ayaz has everything it takes to become a truly special companion

name: Jharna
description:
I’m a 9-year-old German Pointer, and somehow, after everything, I still believe in love.

I was found in the middle of nowhere by kind tourists who saw that I wasn’t okay. They took me to the vet, and that’s when my story came out… I had a microchip, but I had spent my life being used only for breeding.

Over and over again. And when I was no longer “useful,” it was easy to let me go.

But here’s the funny thing… I didn’t let any of that take away who I am.

Because I am still the most loving, gentle, people-obsessed girl you will ever meet. I will follow you around, lean into you, and soak up every bit of affection like I’ve been waiting for it my whole life… because I have.

I have a strong nose (typical Pointer ), and I love being outdoors. Walks, little adventures, exploring new smells… I’m always ready. And yes, I may be 9, but don’t let that fool you — I still have plenty of life, energy, and joy to share.

I can live with other dogs, or I can be your one and only queen… I’m not fussy, as long as I’m loved.

All I’ve ever really wanted is a home where I matter. Where I am more than just what I can give… but simply loved for who I am.

So… if you have a soft spot for a girl who’s been through a lot but still has the biggest heart… I’m right here, waiting for you.

name: Ivy
description:
Ivy is a 7-month-old female Cross-Breed. She is a gentle and affectionate young dog who enjoys spending time with people and thrives on companionship.

Ivy also loves being around other dogs and appears to gain confidence and comfort from canine company. After spending time in kennels, she is now ready to leave that environment behind and begin a new chapter in a loving home.

She is described as a sweet-natured girl who would suit a family willing to continue giving her care, patience, and affection. Ivy is looking for a warm and secure environment where she can settle properly and enjoy life as a cherished family companion.

Her friendly personality and affectionate nature suggest she bonds well with humans and enjoys attention from those around her. She is still young, which means she has plenty of time to continue learning and developing into a wonderful adult dog.

Ivy is suitable to live with other dogs, making her a good match for a multi-dog household. However, she is not suitable to live with cats, so any future home would need to be cat-free.

She can live with older children, indicating that she would likely do best in a calmer environment with children who understand how to interact respectfully with dogs.

Her gentle temperament makes her an appealing companion for adopters looking for a friendly and loving pet.

She will be vaccinated, microchipped, and blood tested before going to her new home. Ivy has not yet been neutered due to her young age, but this will likely need to be addressed when she is old enough.

Full rescue support will also be provided to help her settle into her adoptive home successfully. A home check will be required as part of the adoption process to ensure that she is placed in a safe and suitable environment.

Although Ivy is currently based in Cyprus, she is able to travel abroad for the right home. She is waiting for a family willing to offer her the stability, care, and kindness she deserves after kennel life.

With her affectionate personality and sociable nature, Ivy has the potential to become a loyal and loving companion. She would benefit greatly from a home where she can continue building confidence and enjoying regular companionship.

Ivy is now ready to begin her new life with a family committed to giving her the happy future she deserves.

name: Fern
description:
Fern is a 7-month-old female Cross-Breed. She is a sweet and friendly young dog who enjoys being around both people and other dogs.

Her affectionate and sociable personality makes her a lovely companion for a family willing to offer her a caring and secure home.

After spending time living in kennels, Fern is now hoping to leave that life behind and finally experience the comfort and stability of a forever home.

She is described as a happy and gentle girl who gets along well with those around her.

Fern appears to have a friendly temperament and enjoys companionship, which suggests she would thrive in a home where she can receive plenty of attention and affection.

Being a young dog, she still has lots of potential to continue learning and settling into family life. She would benefit from adopters who are patient and committed to helping her adjust to a new environment.

Fern is suitable to live with other dogs, so she could happily share her home with a canine companion. However, she is not suitable to live with cats, meaning she will need a cat-free household.

She is also suitable to live with older children, making her best suited to a calmer family setting with children who understand how to behave respectfully around dogs. Her gentle and friendly nature suggests she could become a loyal and loving family pet.

Before going to her new home, Fern will be vaccinated, microchipped, and blood tested. She has not yet been neutered due to her age, but this may need to be arranged once she is old enough.

Full rescue backup will be provided to support both Fern and her future adopters throughout the rehoming process. A home check will also apply to ensure she is placed in a safe and appropriate environment.

Fern is currently based in Cyprus but is able to travel abroad for the right home. She is searching for a family willing to give her the opportunity to enjoy a happy and secure future.

With her friendly personality and affectionate nature, Fern has all the qualities needed to become a wonderful companion. She deserves a home where she can leave kennel life behind and enjoy the love, comfort, and stability every dog should have.

Fern is now ready to begin the next chapter of her life with people who will truly care for her.

name: Vera
description:
Meet Vera, our very smiley 2-year-old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier cross.

She loves to meet new people and will quite happily take any affection you can give her. She has a lot of love to give.

She walks well on the lead and will happily sit for treats. She does like to be kept active and would enjoy going out for walks with you.

We would recommend that Vera be the only animal in the home, but could settle well into a home with older children.

name: Duchess
description:
Meet Duchess our 4 ½ year old, Female, German Shepherd Cross. Unfortunately we have not had any enquires for Duchess as yet, which we simply can’t understand why.

Duchess came to us in a state of neglect, she was very thin, and had what looked like untreated sores. Through the dedication of our team she is now a much happier healthier dog.

This loving smiley dog, loves attention, and will give plenty in return. She loves her toys, and once she has found her favourite one she will carry it with her everywhere.

She is an active dog, and would suit a home that has a similar lifestyle. She loves to go for a walk, and have play. She walks ok on the lead, she can be a bit excitable to start with, but soon settles down once she has her toy to hold.

She would suit a home where she is the only animal, but could settle well in a home with older children.

name: Lika
description:
Lika is a deaf young dog whose foster family writes , she is one of the sweetest-natured dogs they have ever met. She is full of life, always looking for her next adventure, and brings a constant sense of fun wherever she goes.

She is a happy, confident pup with no signs of trauma. Lika approaches the world with complete trust and enthusiasm and absolutely adores people. She gives the most wonderful cuddles and thrives on affection.

Because she is deaf, Lika doesn’t always pick up on signals from other dogs, and her play style can be very boisterous. She loves other dogs, but her unfiltered excitement can overwhelm them, especially smaller or more sensitive dogs.

She is responding well to hand signals and already knows some basic commands. Like any puppy, she can be selective at times, but she is very food-motivated, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding.

“Sit” for a treat is already spot on! Lika would suit an active home that enjoys the outdoors and can offer: Plenty of exercise Ongoing training using positive, reward-based methods. Mental stimulation and engagement.

Although it may sound surprising given her deafness, we feel that with a dedicated handler she could even enjoy activities like agility, where visual communication is key.

She is not destructive, but she does love to carry things around and enjoys her toys and chew bones. Lika has not been tested with cats.

We feel Lika would be happiest: As the only dog, or with a confident, well-balanced dog who can clearly set boundaries She would particularly suit someone with experience of high-energy breeds such as Border Collies.

Lika was found abandoned in the countryside with her 5 siblings and her mother. A friend of our volunteer asked for our help. A vet took 5 of the siblings and they are now in a private shelter. We took Lika. As yet, we have been unable to secure the mother.

name: Mocca
description:
I’m not the shyest dog you’ll meet, but right now… I am a very confused one.

When I was just a tiny puppy, I was found in Romania with my brother and sister. We didn’t have much—no warm beds, no full bowls, just each other. Then we were taken to a shelter.

That’s where the older, wiser dogs told us stories… stories about a magical place far away where dogs had families. Real families.

They said dogs slept in warm beds, never went hungry, and went on adventures—sniffing grass, chasing leaves, even watching squirrels.

They said you needed a “golden ticket” to get there. And somehow… we got one.

We came to the UK. And for a little while, I thought the stories were true. I had a home. I had people. I had hope.

But then… after just a few weeks… they decided they didn’t want me anymore.

They said I guarded my food and toys. And maybe I did. When you grow up with nothing, it’s hard to understand that things won’t be taken away. I held on too tightly… because I was scared of losing everything again.

The girls here are helping me every day, and I’m getting better. I’m starting to understand that food comes back, toys come back… that I don’t have to be afraid anymore.

I absolutely love humans. I’ve had some good training, I can walk nicely on the lead, and I’m good with other dogs too.

Every time a volunteer walks past my kennel, I get so excited. I think, “This is it. I’m going home.” But I always have to come back… and it breaks my heart a little more each time.

So I’m asking—please. Share my story far and wide. Someone out there must have space for me. I don’t need perfect… I just need a chance.

name: Mikey
description:
Mikey is a small to medium, 18 month old male bodeguero ratonero.

Introducing Mikey, a very handsome little Spanish Ratonero Bodeguero whose cheerful personality shines through every day.

Mikey is approximately 18 months old and weighs around 10kg, making him a small companion with a big heart. Several months ago, Mikey was found running frantically in the area, confused, lost, and hungry.

Thanks to the dedication of caring volunteers, Mikey has truly blossomed and is now a happy, confident little dog who brings joy wherever they go.

Mikey loves his daily walks with volunteers and enthusiastically plays with other kennel mates. Surrounded by ten other dogs of various ages, sizes, and both males and females, Mikey gets along well and enjoys being part of the group.

While he can be a little nervous when meeting new dogs, Mikey’s bravery soon shines through with proper introductions, quickly becoming a playful friend.

Recently neutered and fully vaccinated, Mikey’s blood tests are all clear, and they are ready to find their very own family. Mikey’s affectionate nature means they love curling up on a human lap for cuddles, and their enthusiasm is contagious.

Imagine Mikey curling up beside you after a long walk, bringing warmth and happiness to your home. Mikey is very good on the lead and harness and would adapt well to a variety of home environments, thriving with love and companionship.

If you’re looking for a loyal and delightful companion, Mikey could be the perfect match for your family. Mikey can also be cat tested if needed.

If you think this little lad is a good fit for your home – please make your initial enquiry with permission from every one in the household.

We would like you to tell us who makes up your home, what type of building it is, what the human work patterns are like and if you have a secured garden space.

Our process included a full application, deposit to reserve, video home check call and confirmation of adoption.

Our fees cover the adoption fee (neutering, vaccinations, worming and flea and tick treatments) The transport fee to travel to the UK including traces kennels, microchip, passport, health certificate, customs charges and import tax, ferry or Eurotunnel.

Thank you for considering giving Mikey the loving family they deserve. He is looking forward hearing from you soon- his paws are crossed.

name: Nala
description:
Nala is a 4 year old female Cross-Breed, D.O.B. 14/09/2021, who was rescued in Romania in September 2024 along with her 9 puppies. She is a sweet, gentle dog who is still learning to trust people.

She is naturally cautious and nervous around new people but is gradually opening up to her foster and showing her true nature.

Nala would benefit from a calm, quiet environment to help her feel safe and take things at her own pace. Ideally, she needs to live with another calm, confident resident dog or dogs who can help her gain trust in her surroundings.

Nala weighs approximately 20kg and stands 50cm tall from floor to withers. She is spayed, fully vaccinated, and enjoys the company of other dogs. She takes no notice of cats. Due to Nala’s shyness, we recommend a home without children.

Nala can be left for a few hours as long as she has the company of other dogs. She is happy to sleep downstairs in her basket at night.

Nala is currently in Cullompton, Devon. However, transport can be arranged for the right adopter.

Stray2Me is a UK registered charity (No. 1186687), with trustees and volunteers across the country.

Home check and adoption donation apply. Full rescue backup and support provided.

name: Bracken
description:
Meet Bracken – a sweet, soulful young 2 year old Breton boy who is patiently waiting for the family he can finally call his own. He is 48cm tall and weighs 14 kg.

Bracken is an ex-hunting dog with a gentle, affectionate nature. Despite his working background, he shows little sign of trauma (comparatively to other dogs) and has adapted beautifully to shelter life.

What he wants most in the world is simple: people to love, and to give him what a Breton needs: exercise and enrichment.

He is often found waiting at his kennel door – not desperate to leave, but hoping that whoever passes by might stop for a moment of attention and cuddles. Once you give him that connection, he completely blossoms.

Affectionate, calm, and people-focusedFriendly with other dogsGood with children (8+ due to size/energy)Active and enjoys his walks and exploringContent to play independently if no humans are available, but always prefers human company

An active family who enjoys daily walks and outdoor timePeople who are home often and want a close companionA stable, loving environment where he is included in family lifeAdopters who understand the needs of a Breton (a working breed with energy and intelligence) and who will provide appropriate enrichmentHe will be a wonderful match for someone looking for a loyal, affectionate companion rather than a very independent dog.

Bracken is fully ready to travel (please see below) and to start his new life.

Bracken is currently at our shelter in Cordoba in southern Spain but will be coming to a UK foster home soon.

All of our dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme and Brucella Canis.

All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons to not do so, will be sterilised. Bracken is neutered. Please note that we will advise medical results and treatments upon successful application.

Adoption contract and fee, homecheck and lifetime RBU (rescue back-up) apply as standard.

name: Remy
description:
Remy is the kind of dog who will fill your life with movement, joy, and endless energy.

He was found in a crowded municipal pound – one of many dogs, waiting, overlooked. Like so many Bretons, he was once a hunting dog… and when he was no longer useful, he was simply left behind. No goodbye. No second thought.

Despite everything, he is still full of love, life, and trust in humans.

This handsome young Breton is incredibly affectionate with people and fantastic with other dogs. He’s also great with children (8+), making him a wonderful companion for an active family.

While he enjoys cuddles and attention, Remy’s true passion is being outside – running, playing, exploring, and making the most of every moment. He is 50 cm tall and weighs 14 kg.

Remy is a lively, high-energy boy who thrives on activity. He will need a home that understands his needs and can provide plenty of daily exercise, stimulation, and enrichment.

Long walks, playtime with other dogs, and space to run will make him the happiest version of himself.

Very friendly with humans, dogs, and childrenYoung, active, and full of lifeLoves running and playing above all elseAffectionate, but not a couch potatoFood-motivated (he LOVES his meals!)Can be protective over food while eating, so must be fed separatelyRemy doesn’t show obvious signs of trauma – he’s simply a sensitive, energetic dog who experiences the world with enthusiasm. He’s not dominant or submissive with other dogs; he just happily does his own thing and joins in play when it suits him.

Remy would thrive in an active household that can match his energy and give him structure, exercise, and fun. A home with another playful dog would be a bonus, but is not essential. Most importantly, he needs adopters who understand that young working breeds like the Breton require both physical and mental stimulation.

With the right home, Remy will be an incredibly rewarding companion – loyal, loving, and full of personality.

All of our dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme and Brucella canis.

All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons to not do so, will be sterilised. Remy is neutered. Full medical information will be provided upon successful application.

Could you be the one to give Remy the life he’s been waiting for?

Adoption contract and fee, homecheck, and lifetime rescue back-up apply.

name: Meeka
description:
Meeka is a small sized (14kg), black and white female wadi dog who is currently in Oman. She was 1 year old in February 2026 and was rescued as a newborn puppy.

Her mum had been sadly shot and died so a local rescuer took in Meeka and her siblings and hand reared them. Meeka came into our care when she was 3 months old.

Meeka currently lives in a boarding facility and the volunteers walk and socialize with her every week. She is always very happy and excited to see them and enjoys going out for a walk.

She enjoys sniffing new smells, and having a dig in any mud she finds. She is wary of trucks and large vehicles that pass by though.

She gets along well with the other dogs in boarding, and although she has never lived with cats, she has shown no prey drive with the cats she has met.

She would love a home with people who have the time and energy for a young dog. She is healthy, fully vaccinated, microchipped, spayed and rabies titer tested so is ready to leave Oman now.

We will test her for Brucella before she leaves Oman.

name: Indie
description:
Indie is a 10 month old female German short haired pointer located in Spain.

Gorgeous puppy Indie is a beautiful looking German pointer girl. She’s very loving, friendly and affectionate. She gets on well with her kennel mates but really loves human company.

Indie stands at medium height and she’s approximately 10 months old. She weighs 16kg so she needs to put some weight on, but she lively and healthy and has a great personality.

Poor Indie arrived at the shelter via a local vet who found her abandoned with two other dogs, so unfortunately we don’t know much about her background except she’s not had much training so she is a blank canvas for a family wanting to train for obedience or agility, she would be brill at either!

Indie isn’t a couch potato and loves to be exploring and having fun, so for that reason we need to look for a home with other young dogs and older children over 12 years old.

Very friendly with people and dogs. She’s a lively girl and still learning to walk on the lead but improving daily. So much potential!

name: Cosmo
description:
Cosmo is a medium sized, mixed breed boy, around 1 year old.

Cosmo is currently in Cyprus and ready to travel.

Cosmo is growing up in the shelter and it’s not fair. He has been there since he was 6 months old and needs to get out asap so he can start living his life.

He arrived with his mum and siblings after they were confiscated from the owner.

Cosmo is a lovely, friendly boy and is patiently waiting for his chance at life. He should be enjoying life in a loving home, cared for and cherished, warm at night instead of sleeping in a concrete floor and looking at the same 4 walls of a kennel.

After some initial excitement, Cosmo is beginning to walk well on the leash. He is medium sized but strong so will need someone who can handle him. He’s great with other dogs, strangers, and children.

He’s far too young to spend his days in a shelter. He can live with a single person, a couple, or a family.

Cosmo is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and will be castrated.

name: Shadow
description:
Lovely girl Shadow is a 2 year old medium sized mixed breed who has recently been saved by us from the streets.

She has a soft black and white short coat, and she is a very loving, affectionate and playful girl with her pal Max, who sleeps in her kennel.

Shadow is good with all the other dogs once introduced, but can be a bit of a slow burner to begin with, until she knows she is safe.

Shadow walks very well on her lead and we think that she is suitable for a family with older children with or without another friendly dog.

Shadow is not cat tested but we can do that if required.

Shadow is ready to travel now for the right family.

Great with people and dogs. gentle nature, and is obedient, loving and a pretty girl

name: Eddie and Billy
description:
Eddie is a no-age-given male Cross-Breed. He and his brother Billy are bonded brothers who are looking for a new home together. They are currently being fostered in Hertfordshire after the tragic loss of their owner.

The boys each weigh 12kg and have very friendly personalities. They love being around people and enjoy spending time with other dogs. Their affectionate nature makes them enjoyable companions.

Eddie has short hair, while Billy has a longer and fluffier coat. Both dogs enjoy their walks and love having the opportunity to run around and do zoomies. They would benefit from a home where they can continue to enjoy an active lifestyle.

They are looking for an active family, couple, or individual who can offer them a permanent and loving home. As bonded brothers, they would need to remain together so they can continue to enjoy each other’s company.

Their close relationship is an important part of their lives.

The boys are neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped. They are being cared for by The Little Rescue while they wait for the right adopters to come forward. A home check and adoption fee will apply as part of the adoption process.

name: Buddy
description:
Buddy is a 7 year old, neutered, fully vaccinated dog weighing approximately 20kg. He was rescued from a Romanian kill shelter in April 2023 and has since shown himself to be a curious and gentle companion with a moderate energy level.

Buddy is already housetrained and walks well on a lead.

Prior to coming to foster in the UK, Buddy was a curious dog, happy to greet strangers, but sadly his foster placement didn’t work out and now Buddy is struggling in kennels.

He is a gentle dog who needs equally gentle, kind adopters who are willing to rebuild his trust in people. In Romania he was good with the other dogs that he shared a kennel with.

Buddy needs help to adapt to living in a home. He’d be happy as the only dog or with calm, kind doggy companions. We are looking for a rural or semi-rural home because, once settled and able to trust again, Buddy will be happy to go on long walks.

He also needs a garden because he enjoys being outdoors. Ideally any adopters will have previous experience of Romanian dogs, and live within an hour or so of the kennels for several meets & greets.

However, transport can be arranged for the right adopters.

Please note Buddy does not have a tail. We are unsure if he was born like this or if something happened before he was rescued.

Full rescue backup and support throughout the adoption process and for the lifetime of the dog.

name: Henry
description:
Meet Henry, a 4 year old male medium-sized Cross-Breed currently based in Basingstoke, UK. Born in May 2021, Henry has sadly been waiting since April 2022 to find his forever home, and honestly, it’s baffling because he is an absolute gem.

Henry is a lovely, friendly boy who adores people and truly enjoys companionship. He is great with other dogs and can also live happily with cats, making him a wonderfully versatile family companion.

Thanks to his gentle and sociable nature, he could also possibly live with children aged 10 years and over.

Henry is neutered and fully vaccinated and is more than ready to leave kennel life behind. He would love a home where he can finally settle, feel secure, and enjoy the love and attention he has been patiently waiting for.

An ideal home for Henry would be with a family or individual who can offer stability, affection, and regular walks. He has waited far too long for his chance and truly deserves a loving forever home to call his own.

A home check and adoption donation apply. Full rescue backup and support are provided throughout the adoption process and for the lifetime of the dog.

name: Damian
description:
Meet Damian, a young cross-breed dog with a gentle soul who is slowly learning to trust the world around him.

Damian is around 2 years old and was rescued from another shelter after being found wandering alone on a road, likely having been abandoned. His early life was not kind to him, and he arrived shy and fearful, unsure of people and new experiences.

Despite this, Damian is making steady progress. With patience and care from the team at Rescates Garatuxa in northern Spain, he is beginning to come out of his shell.

Recently, he took an important step forward by going for a walk outside on a harness with a volunteer – a big milestone for a dog like him.

We believe Damian did not receive proper nutrition or care as a puppy, which has affected his physical development. This is sadly not uncommon in hunting dogs.

What he needs now is a home that can offer him time, understanding, and gentle guidance as he continues to build confidence.

Damian is good with other dogs and would likely benefit from a calm, stable environment, possibly with another confident dog to help him feel secure. He would suit an experienced and patient adopter who understands that trust takes time.

He will be fully prepared for travel – vaccinated, microchipped, neutered, and with his passport ready – and can travel to the U.K. or across Europe to the right home.

If you can offer Damian the quiet, compassionate home he needs, you will see him slowly blossom into a loyal and loving companion.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Sky
description:
Meet Sky, a young 1 year old Griffon Niverna girl with the gentlest soul who is still learning that the world can be kind.

Sky came into our care in Galicia, northern Spain, along with her two siblings after a hunter no longer wanted them and threatened to kill them if no one stepped in.

Thankfully they were saved in time — but Sky is now the only one still waiting for her forever home.

She is around 1.5 years old and a Griffon Nivernais type. Sky is currently underweight at approximately 17kg (she should be closer to 20kg), and we are working on building her strength, confidence, and trust in humans again.

Despite everything she has been through, Sky is incredibly gentle. She is good with other dogs and children, and with time, patience, and kindness, she will truly blossom into a loyal and loving companion.

Sky would benefit from a calm, understanding home where she can continue to gain confidence at her own pace and finally feel safe. Must have a secure garden.

She is fully prepared for travel — vaccinated, microchipped, dewormed, and spayed — and can travel to the U.K. or across Europe to the right home.

If you can offer Sky the second chance she so desperately deserves, she will reward you with quiet loyalty and love.

As with all of our dogs, she comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Mary
description:
Mary is a 3.5 year old female German Shepherd Cross. Originally from Romania, Mary was found all alone when tiny and taken to a private shelter where she was very lonely.

Mary spent three years there before she came to foster with a vet in Newmarket, Suffolk.

Mary has blossomed; she loves life and all she wants to do is shake hands with you. She can be a bit nervous when she meets someone new, but once she knows there is nothing to worry about, she is fine.

She is so friendly, affectionate, and loves cuddles. Mary is kind and calm but also enjoys a good run in a safe area. She is good on the lead and weighs 26 kg.

Mary is just a very special girl. She is looking for a home with someone who has plenty of time for her and can offer her an active life.

She is good with dogs, cats, and hens. She loves the car and will hop in and out with no problem. No children are preferred so she can be the centre of your world.

Mary has a lopsided face, possibly born like that, but it cannot be confirmed. It makes her all the more endearing. She is in foster with a vet who has given her a clean bill of health.

Mary is spayed, vaccinated, microchipped, and has a passport. You will not find a nicer dog than Mary.

Adoption fee £500. A home check is required, and there is rescue backup. Please consider this absolutely delightful girl.

name: Perine
description:
Perine is an 11 month old female small cross-breed currently in the East Midlands.

She is spayed, iElisa negative and weighs approximately 9kg.

Perine is a confident and outgoing young dog who enjoys being involved in day-to-day activities. She is playful, inquisitive and affectionate with people once settled.

She is friendly with men and women and has been positive around children. Due to her excitable nature, she would be best suited to a home with older children.

Perine gets along well with other dogs and benefits from their presence. A calm resident dog would help support her development and confidence.

She can be vocal when greeting visitors but settles quickly and seeks interaction.

Perine is still in the early stages of training. She may mouth during play and will require continued training and guidance as she matures.

She is housetrained, sleeps well overnight and accepts a lead, although she will benefit from ongoing lead training to build consistency and confidence.

Perine is used to a quieter environment and may find busy or high-traffic areas overwhelming.

Perine would suit a home able to provide structure, routine and ongoing training. A secure garden and a patient, active household will support her continued development.

name: Paddy
description:
Paddy is a 9 year old male medium cross-breed currently in Scotland.

He is neutered and settled into home life following rescue from a shelter environment.

Paddy is affectionate, calm and people-focused once he has built trust. He forms strong bonds with his primary carers and enjoys close companionship, but can be wary of unfamiliar people. Slow and controlled introductions are recommended.

He prefers a quiet environment and can become overwhelmed in busy households or where there are frequent visitors.
