name: Bailey
description:
Bailey is approximately 4 years old. Medium sized male Cross-Breed.

Bailey is looking for an adult only home. He likes people and will jump to say hello when he first meets you.

He likes to fetch a toy and bring it to you as an invitation to play.

He can be nervous on walks and will lunge at passing traffic. This is something that will need further training.

Bailey is currently reactive towards cats and dogs, for this reason he would suit a home where he is the only pet to allow further training to be carried out on his reactivity.

He has met other dogs but must be supervised when he does.

Bailey is toilet trained and enjoys travelling in the car.

Bailey is not crate trained and has not been left alone at home.

name: Brutus
description:
Brutus is a male Cross-Breed approximately 7 years old of medium/large size available for foster/adoption.

Nervous boy Brutus is looking for a foster or forever home to call his own.

Brutus is a very nervous boy, He hasn’t worn a lead or collar. He is nervous of noises so he will need a quiet home.

Brutus is a sweet boy and once he trusts you he enjoys a stroke behind his ears.

In the home, Brutus will need work to build up his confidence and eventually relise the world isn’t a scary place)

name: Arun
description:
Meet Arun. Male approximately 8-9 years old of small-medium size Cross-Breed.

Arun is looking for an adult only and pet free home.

He is a sweet, affectionate boy but it takes time for him to get to know you.

Arun space and food guards around new people so his new home must be aware of this and give him the space he needs around the home.

Arun walks lovely on the lead and enjoys group walks with the other dogs at our kennels however he would prefer to be the only dog in the home.

Arun needs an understanding home who will give him a chance. Do you have the heart to give Arun a chance at life outside of the kennels?

name: Faye
description:
Meet Faye, a female approximately 4 years old medium/large sized Cross-Breed.

She’s nervous of new people but doesn’t take long to come around, just make sure you have plenty of treats around!

She’s a playful girl with high energy and loves nothing more than her walks.

Faye would make a very good walking companion.

Faye is very clever and very food orientated so she is easy to train.

Faye loves to play with other dogs and loves to be around people she trusts.

Faye would thrive better in a home without children as she can sometimes be unaware of her size when excited and due to her nervousness about people.

name: Hershey
description:
Hershey is a 6-month-old male large-sized cross-breed dog with a height of 64cm, a chest measuring 78cm, and a neck circumference of 46cm.

He is located in Romania and has been neutered. Hershey, along with his 8 siblings, was discovered abandoned, hungry, and alone at a chicken abattoir.

Fortunately, they were taken into foster care in a friend’s yard, where a large kennel run was constructed for them until space became available at Happy’s, a rescue center.

This sweet and lively young dog has since settled well at Happy’s. Unfortunately, one of his brothers, Casper, didn’t survive, arriving too late for assistance.

Hershey is described as typical, and his new family is expected to invest time in caring for him, and providing support in terms of development and training.

Remarkably, Hershey shows compatibility with other dogs, cats, and goats, but caution is advised around chickens.

Hershey is fully vaccinated and possesses a passport. If you believe you can meet Hershey’s needs, the recommendation is to complete a registration form, and the rehoming team at Happy’s will be in touch.

name: Kofi
description:
Our extra special boy Kofi is approximately three years old and an enormously attractive cross breed at the very bottom end of medium.

Kofi weighs just eleven kilos and measures eleven inches shoulder to paw. Having been surrendered by his owners, Kofi has been in our Cyprus shelter for one month.

Kofi is described by our shelter manager as shy and very well behaved. Having lived his life with a family, Kofi is overwhelmed by shelter life. His is a kind, loving and gentle little chap with a lovely smile.

His appearance is spectacular, and some would say cute. With a tri colour coat and white tips Kofi is so popular amongst the shelter staff and volunteers. Kofi is longing for his forever home, and his adopters will be truly blessed.

Kofi walks really nicely on his lead and thoroughly enjoys his time in the car. He seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Ree
description:
Ree is a medium sized crossbreed aged around fourteen months old. Ree fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Ree and her sister Rox were found in the middle of nowhere in Romania, near a road, obviously abandoned, without food, water, or shelter.

It was last summer, when temperatures were soaring outside. They were taken by the Animal Police and taken to Roxana’s shelter.

Ree is a loving and loyal girl with a cheeky personality. She is initially shy of new people and new situations but is growing in confidence in her foster home.

She is wary of traffic and will need a rural home or quietish area where she can have time to grow in confidence out and about.

She mixes well with other dogs but could also be the only dog in the home. She will need a cat free home and can live with children aged eight plus.

name: Johnny
description:
Johnny is a 1 year old male Cross-Breed, truly adorable little chap currently thriving in his UK foster home.

He’s neutered. At just 1 year old, lots of energy and has settled in beautifully. Johnny is a bright, cheerful soul with a wonderfully cheeky personality.

He’s making great progress with his toilet training and has just begun exploring the world on his walks. He’s good on both lead and harness, curious about everything he sees, and is gradually becoming more confident around traffic.

Johnny is living with an older female dog at the moment, but he would absolutely love a younger, playful companion to match his energy.

He cannot live with cats. He hasn’t met children yet, so we would say children aged 12+.

He is such a sweet, happy youngster who’s ready for his forever home.

name: Henry
description:
Meet Henry – The Gentle Soul Ready for His Forever Family

Status: Castrated, vaccinated, pet passport

He’s a gentle, affectionate young lad with impeccable manners and a lovely, kind nature. Having previously lived in a home, rescue life has been quite a big change for him, so he can be a little shy and overwhelmed at first.

Give him a little time, however, and you’ll discover a wonderful companion who simply loves being around people. Henry has been thoroughly enjoying spending time with our volunteers and is growing in confidence every day.

He loves a fuss, takes treats beautifully gently, and is a pleasure to spend time with.

Great with other dogs Henry has become great friends with his kennel mate, Darci, and we think he would really benefit from living with another friendly, confident dog who could help him continue to build his confidence and show him that the world isn’t such a scary place.

Henry could happily live with children and has done so previously. However, because he can be a little sensitive to busy environments, we’d love to find him a quieter family home rather than one with lots of hustle and bustle.

Calm, dog-savvy children who understand when a dog needs a little space would suit him perfectly.

He has not yet learned reliable recall, so this is something his new family will need to work on.

Like any young dog, he will also benefit from continued socialisation, training, and plenty of positive experiences as he settles into family life.

A home with another friendly dog would be wonderful for Henry, although it isn’t essential if his family can provide him with lots of companionship, reassurance, and opportunities to build his confidence.

Henry doesn’t need to be the centre of attention—he’s simply looking for a family who will love him, be patient with him, and show him all the wonderful things life has to offer.

He’s the sort of dog who will quietly become your best friend. Whether it’s joining you on woodland walks, curling up beside you after a busy day, or greeting you with his gentle wagging tail, Henry has so much love to give.

All he needs now is a family who can promise him that this time, it’s forever.

Could Henry Be the Missing Piece of Your Family?

Potential adopters must be willing to travel to Ayr to meet and collect Henry. Let’s help this lovely boy find the forever home he’s been waiting for.

name: Trixie
description:
Trixie is a small 5 month old female Jack Russell Cross puppy, born on 28th March 2026, who is expected to remain a small adult.

Trixie is currently cared for in our small, cage-free home rescue in Bulgaria and is available for adoption to families in the UK.

She was found abandoned with her two brothers on a building site in Bulgaria. Thankfully, those difficult days are now behind them, and all three puppies are safe, healthy and thriving while they wait for their forever homes.

Trixie is a happy, playful little girl with a wonderful zest for life. She loves exploring, playing with the other puppies and then curling up for cuddles when it’s time to relax.

She is friendly, affectionate and enjoys human company, making friends wherever she goes.

She is full of confidence without being overwhelming and has the bright, curious personality that makes every day an adventure.

Trixie is already showing all the qualities of a fantastic family companion and will thrive with continued training, socialisation and plenty of love as she grows.

Trixie enjoys the company of other dogs and would happily live with another friendly canine companion. Equally, she would be just as happy as the only dog in a home where she will receive lots of attention and be included in family life.

If you’re looking for a small puppy with a big personality, Trixie could be the perfect addition to your family.

At Rescue Dogs For Adoption, all of our dogs live as part of our family in a home environment rather than kennels, allowing us to understand their personalities and carefully match them with the right homes.

We consider all applicants because finding the perfect match is far more important than ticking boxes.

If you think Trixie could be the perfect addition to your family, we’d love to hear from you.

name: Harley
description:
Harley is a 6-month-old male Cross-breed, born on 29th July 2021, with a large-sized stature standing at 64cm, chest measuring 78cm, and neck circumference at 46cm.

Rescued from an unfortunate situation, Harley, along with his eight siblings, was discovered abandoned and hungry at a chicken abattoir in Romania.

After their rescue, they found temporary refuge in a friend’s yard, where a large kennel run was set up for them until space became available at Happy’s, where Harley is currently residing.

Harley, a sweet and lively young dog, has adapted well to his new environment at Happy’s. Despite the tragic loss of one of his brothers, Casper, Harley is in good health.

Neutered and up-to-date with vaccinations, he is ready for adoption. His ideal family should be willing to dedicate time to care for him, provide support for his development, and engage in training activities.

Harley has proven to be friendly and sociable, getting along well with other dogs, cats, and goats. However, caution is advised around chickens as he does not interact positively with them.

For those considering adopting Harley and meeting his needs, the rehoming process involves filling out a registration form. The rehoming team at Happy’s will then be in touch to facilitate the adoption process.

name: Miro
description:
Miro is a large, 3-year-old male Romanian Shepherd, born on 10th November 2020. He has been neutered, possesses a passport, and is up-to-date on vaccinations.

Currently located in kennels in the UK, Miro found a family in November but is now back, awaiting that special someone who can offer him a forever home.

Despite his heartbreaking return to kennels, Miro remains affectionate and is a superb cuddler. Desperate for love, he quickly forms strong bonds with those around him.

In search of an extraordinary home, Miro requires a quiet rural or semi-rural setting with a spacious and secure garden. Ideally, his new home should be an adult-only environment without other animals.

Potential adopters must have experience with large-breed Romanian Shepherds, and be willing to invest time in building a relationship with Miro, his trainer, and the team familiar with him.

Miro, being sensitive to his surroundings, needs someone patient, who can ensure he feels comfortable and safe.

While Miro can be overwhelmed by his environment, in the right home, he proves to be an exceptionally loyal companion. Engaging in scent training has not only showcased his natural ability but also helped reduce his anxiety.

It’s essential to note that Miro can be reactive on a lead and may struggle with reading other dogs. Despite his strength, he walks beautifully on a lead and is comfortable wearing a muzzle, a requirement for his safety.

Prospective adopters must commit to having him wear a muzzle at all times outside the house and a double lead.

name: Rosie
description:
Rosie is a 1 year old female cross-breed with unique and lovely markings. DOB 10/7/2023.

Abandoned in woodland with her siblings at a tender age, she found refuge in a foster shelter, where she currently resides.

Rosie, a good-sized medium dog, walks well on a lead, great with other dogs & older children.

This resilient pup has undergone thorough veterinary care, including comprehensive blood tests, ensuring her seamless integration into life in the UK.

Ideal for an experienced family well-versed in dog ownership, Rosie is best suited for a household with children over 8 years old, given her size.

She comes fully vaccinated, microchipped, and equipped with a pet passport and medical papers detailing her health history.

The commitment to her well-being extends beyond adoption, with the assurance of lifetime rescue backup and ongoing support from the dedicated rescue centre.

For households with feline companions, a cat test can be conducted to assess Rosie’s compatibility.

The rescue centre emphasises their dedication to the welfare of their dogs, offering not just a new family member but a guarantee of continuous support for Rosie’s lifetime.

name: Monty
description:
Monty is a 5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is described as a medium-sized dog and is currently in foster care in Hartlepool. He arrived in the UK in September 2025 after spending three years in Romanian foster kennels.

When Monty first arrived, he was very nervous and shy in his new surroundings. Since then, he has grown greatly in confidence and has shown himself to be a wonderful and loving dog. He is now ready to find a caring and permanent home of his own.

Monty is a very cuddly dog who forms strong bonds once he learns to trust someone. He is described as having a soft nature and being full of love. He is especially affectionate with people he knows well.

He walks nicely on a lead, which helps make his daily exercise more manageable. Although he has made great progress, he can still be nervous when meeting new people and dogs while out on walks.

Because of this, he would benefit from an understanding adopter who can continue to build his confidence at his own pace.

Monty is good with other dogs and enjoys their company. He has not been tested with cats, and he has also not been tested with children. Any introductions in these areas would need to be handled carefully and thoughtfully.

He is up to date with his vaccinations and has been neutered. Full rescue backup is provided, offering ongoing support after adoption. Monty is currently based in Hartlepool but can travel to the right home.

name: Oliver
description:
Oliver is a 1 year old male Hound Cross, a medium to large sized boy weighing around 18–20 kilograms who is currently outside the UK.

Oliver, a handsome young hound mix is with a lovely black, brown and white coat and a wonderfully easygoing nature. He was found wandering alone before being brought to safety at the Residencia Garatuxa rescue in Galicia, northern Spain.

Oliver is a confident and friendly dog who enjoys the company of people and other dogs. He is social, relaxed and not nervous or dominant, making him an easy companion to have around.

At the shelter he mixes well with the other dogs and shows a gentle, affectionate character.

He is still a young dog, around one year old or possibly even younger, so he has his whole life ahead of him and will make a wonderful addition to a family willing to give him the love and stability he deserves. He can be cat tested and child tested if required.

Oliver will be fully prepared for travel — vaccinated, microchipped, neutered and with his passport ready — and can travel to the UK to the right home.

If you are looking for a young, friendly dog who will quickly become part of the family, Oliver could be the perfect match.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Pongo
description:
Pongo is a 1-year-old male Labrador Retriever Cross. He currently weighs around 25 kg and is described as a sweet and gentle dog with a sociable nature.

Although he may appear a little shy when first meeting new people, he gradually becomes more confident once he feels safe and comfortable.

Pongo’s early life began in Italy, where he was found as a very young puppy. When he was around two months old, he and his small siblings, along with other puppies, were captured and taken to a shelter.

Life behind the bars of a shelter was not the start any young dog deserves, but fortunately his story soon took a more hopeful turn.

A kind woman in Germany decided to rescue him and offer him a chance at a better life. Thanks to her, Pongo was able to leave the shelter and move into a foster home in Germany. There he is now patiently waiting for the loving family he truly deserves.

In his foster home, Pongo is continuing to grow and learn about the world around him. He is slowly becoming accustomed to everyday things such as walking on a lead and meeting new people.

While he still needs a bit of time to build confidence, he is making steady progress and learning that people can be kind and trustworthy.

Pongo has a naturally gentle and affectionate personality. Once he gets to know someone, his sweet and friendly side quickly appears. His sociable character makes him a lovely companion who enjoys positive interactions and calm encouragement.

He is also known to get along well with other dogs and cats. This shows that he has a friendly and tolerant temperament when around other animals. With continued guidance and a patient environment, he can continue developing his social skills and confidence.

What Pongo needs most now is a family willing to offer him patience, security, and love. A calm home where he can feel safe will help him continue blossoming into the confident dog he is meant to be.

With the right people beside him, his shy side will gradually fade as his trusting and affectionate nature grows stronger.

Adopting Pongo means giving a deserving dog the stable and loving future he has been waiting for. In return, he will offer loyalty, sweetness, and companionship to the family who welcomes him into their lives.

He is simply waiting for someone to give him the chance to belong.

name: Oscar
description:
Meet Oscar, a 2 year old male English Pointer Cross who is searching for a loving forever home.

When Oscar was found, he was so thin you could count every bone in his body, and yet his tail was still wagging.

Oscar is only about two years old, but life has already asked far too much of him.

This gentle boy was found wandering the streets of Cyprus, alone, starving, and heartbreakingly thin. When we first saw him, he looked almost like a living skeleton. Every bone was visible and every step was a struggle, and yet somehow his tail still tried to wag.

Despite everything the world had done to him, Oscar still believed in kindness.

Amazingly, after a vet check, all tests were normal. Since that day, Oscar has been slowly gaining weight and strength.

Day by day he is healing. He is still painfully underweight, and the road back to health continues.

What breaks our hearts the most is how gentle he is. Oscar is incredibly loving with people. He is calm, affectionate, and grateful for every soft touch.

He gets along beautifully with other dogs and simply wants to be close to someone who cares.

After everything he has endured, Oscar deserves a family to call his own.

A home with a secure garden where he can run and feel the grass under his paws.

People who will give him patience, guidance, and love as he learns what it means to truly belong.

He loves other dogs, but he could also be the only dog if he receives the attention and affection he longs for.

Oscar has survived the worst. Now all he needs is someone to see him, really see him.

Now he deserves the chance to love and be loved.

Could you be the one who finally gives Oscar the home he has never had?

name: Jester
description:
Introducing Jester, a 4 month old male Griffon Cross who is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of around 18–20 kg.

Jester was born on 1 November 2025 as part of a litter of six boys. His mother is a Griffon cross, and he and his brothers have been raised at the Residencia Garatuxa shelter in Galicia.

During their time at the shelter, they have had regular contact with people and other dogs. This has helped them grow into confident, sociable puppies who are comfortable around activity and noise.

Jester is affectionate, playful, and curious about the world around him. Like all puppies, he will need a family ready to guide him through training and provide the love and stability every young dog deserves.

He has been tested for Mediterranean diseases and will be fully prepared for travel, vaccinated, microchipped, and with his passport ready. Jester will be ready to travel in April to his forever home.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Hamish
description:
Meet Hamish, a 4 month old male Griffon Cross who is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of around 18–20 kg when fully grown.

Hamish is one of six lively brothers born on 1 November 2025 to a Griffon cross mum. He is currently nearly four months old and, like his siblings, is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog.

Hamish has had a good start to life at the Residencia Garatuxa shelter in Galicia, northern Spain. Growing up in the shelter environment means he is already used to people, everyday activity, and different sounds around him.

He is a very sociable puppy who enjoys interacting with both humans and other dogs.

As a young puppy, Hamish will benefit from a family willing to continue his training and give him the guidance, exercise, and affection he needs as he grows.

He has been tested for Mediterranean diseases and will be fully prepared for travel, vaccinated, microchipped, and with his passport ready. Hamish will be ready to travel in April to the right home.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Lupin
description:
Meet Lupin, a 4 month old male Griffon Cross who is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of around 18–20 kg when fully grown.

Lupin is a charming young puppy born on 1 November 2025. He is one of six brothers born to a Griffon cross mum.

Lupin has spent his early months at the Residencia Garatuxa shelter in Galicia, where he has grown up surrounded by people, other dogs, and everyday shelter activity. This has helped him develop into a sociable and confident puppy.

He enjoys playing with his brothers and interacting with people, showing a friendly and open nature. Lupin will thrive in a home where he can continue learning, exploring, and becoming a much-loved family member.

He has been tested for Mediterranean diseases and will be fully prepared for travel, vaccinated, microchipped, and with his passport ready. Lupin will be ready to travel in April.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Bon Bon
description:
Bon Bon is a 1.5 year old spayed small to medium mixed breed currently in foster in Staffordshire. She is iElisa negative.

Bon Bon is a very sweet, shy-natured girl who is enjoying life in foster.

She is housetrained and sleeps through the night without issue.

Bon Bon gets along well with other dogs and could happily live with a canine companion or as the only dog in the home.

She can be a little shy at first and needs a family who will give her time and patience to build her confidence and bond with them.

Bon Bon accepts a collar and lead but will need further training to walk confidently outside the home. She has been walked in a field near her foster home and, although hesitant at first, soon enjoyed sniffing and exploring.

She enjoys time in the garden and then returning inside for snuggles on the sofa. At present she has a fairly low energy level and enjoys short play sessions followed by rest.

Bon Bon is currently more comfortable around women than men, although she shows no aggression and is simply shy.

Bon Bon would suit a quiet home with patient adopters who will allow her time to settle and continue building confidence.

name: Mylo
description:
Mylo is a 6 year old neutered small mixed breed currently in foster in Staffordshire. He weighs approximately 14kg and stands around 47cm tall. He has a distinctive stump tail and a confident little character.

Mylo previously spent a long period living as a stray before entering rescue. He has now settled well into foster care and is enjoying the comfort and routine of home life.

He is affectionate but independent and prefers interaction on his own terms. He enjoys gentle fuss, especially belly rubs, and likes spending time pottering around the house before settling down nearby.

Mylo is friendly with people but appreciates his personal space and will communicate when he has had enough attention. For this reason he would be best suited to an adult-only home.

He can interact well with other dogs he feels comfortable around but does not enjoy overly energetic behaviour, particularly from puppies. He may be happiest as the only dog, although he could potentially share with a calm and respectful companion. He can be protective of food around other dogs so feeding will need to be managed.

Mylo is housetrained and settles well in the home environment. He tolerates gentle handling but is sensitive about his tail being touched.

Mylo would suit a quiet household able to provide routine, companionship and respect for his boundaries. A secure garden would be beneficial for relaxed outdoor time as he enjoys pottering and lounging outside.

name: Roo
description:
Roo is a 1 year old spayed small mixed breed weighing around 10kg, currently in foster care in Staffordshire. She is iElisa negative.

Roo is a happy, energetic little dog with a gentle nature. She loves people and enjoys being around her humans.

She can initially be a little shy around loud noises but settles quickly with reassurance.

She is playful and lively and enjoys interaction with people and other dogs. Roo gets along well with dogs of all shapes and sizes.

Roo is housetrained with regular access to the garden and settles well in the home. She is not crate trained.

She accepts wearing a collar and lead and is beginning to get used to short walks around the garden area.

Continued lead training and confidence-building will help her become more comfortable walking outside the home.

Roo would suit an active household able to provide regular exercise, companionship and continued training as she matures.

name: Dolly
description:
Dolly is a spayed female mixed breed currently in foster care in Staffordshire. She is iElisa negative.

Dolly was rescued together with several members of her family group in Romania. The dogs were found living together in a field and clearly formed a close family unit.

She has recently arrived in the UK and is still settling into her foster home. At the moment she can be a little unsure around people but is gradually building confidence and beginning to come out of her shell.

She is becoming more comfortable around the people in the household and accepts gentle interaction.

Dolly enjoys the company of other dogs and would benefit from living with a friendly resident dog who can help her continue to gain confidence.

Dolly enjoys relaxing on the sofa and spending time near her foster family once she feels safe. She also enjoys her food and settles well into the home routine.

She will sometimes join in barking when other dogs bark.

name: Elsa
description:
Elsa is a 1.4 year old spayed female mixed breed with Husky-type characteristics, currently in Oxfordshire. She is iElisa negative.

Elsa is an affectionate and energetic young dog with a curious and intelligent nature. She enjoys human company and likes to be involved in daily activities.

She has a playful and enthusiastic personality and benefits from regular physical and mental stimulation. Although lively, she settles well after exercise and enjoys resting alongside other dogs in the home.

She is continuing to build confidence and can show assertive behaviour during energetic play.

Elsa is friendly with adults and enjoys attention. Due to her size and excitable nature, she would be best suited to a home with older children.

She enjoys rough-and-tumble play with other dogs and would benefit from living with a confident, energetic dog who matches her play style. She does not show food guarding.

She is not suitable for homes with cats or small animals due to a strong chase instinct.

She may bark at unfamiliar visitors and can appear anxious initially, but settles with calm, positive introductions.

Elsa’s housetraining is still in progress and she will require continued consistency and supervision.

She is not crate trained and becomes distressed if confined in a crate, particularly in the car, although she travels well once settled.

She walks well on a harness and collar but is strong and energetic. She may become overexcited on grassed areas.

Her recall is good in secure enclosed spaces, and she is more confident walking alongside another dog than alone.

name: Rebecca
description:
Rebecca is a beautiful black Greyhound, thought to be around 5 years old (possibly a little older), currently fostered in North Lincolnshire.

She arrived from Ireland in search of her forever home here in the UK, after an incredibly sad past. Rebecca was rescued in a terrible condition and was clearly used for breeding.

Despite everything she has endured, she has the most gentle and loving nature.

Since settling into foster, Rebecca has adapted wonderfully to home life. She adores her cosy bed, enjoys her daily walks, and gets very excited at mealtimes.

After breakfast and a walk, she’s more than happy to spend the rest of the day snoozing peacefully.

Rebecca is a calm, gentle soul who is lovely around children and has been great with the dogs she has met. She walks beautifully on the lead, although she can show a little strength when squirrels grab her attention!

Rebecca has no ear markings, so her exact age cannot be confirmed, but she is ready now to find the loving home she truly deserves.

name: Percy
description:
Percy is a large, affectionate young crossbreed aged just over 1 year old with a loving and playful nature.

Percy is incredibly people-focused and thrives on human companionship. He forms strong bonds and enjoys being close to his family, often following his people around the home and seeking affection.

In the home, Percy is calm, clean, and well behaved. He is crate trained, settles well when left, and shows no destructive behaviour. He enjoys his comforts, along with playtime, toys, and plenty of cuddles.

Percy is still learning about the world and can sometimes feel unsure in new situations or around unfamiliar dogs. However, he is making great progress with positive training and is growing in confidence every day.

He can live with another dog of a similar size following careful introductions, as he has shown he can build positive relationships. However, he would not be suitable to live with cats or small animals.

Percy walks using a halti and continues to improve with guidance. At this stage, off-lead exercise is best suited to secure fields while his training develops further.

Percy would suit a patient and committed home that can continue his training and provide a calm, supportive environment. He is a young dog with huge potential who will thrive with consistency and encouragement.

Percy is a loyal and loving companion who, once bonded, will be a constant and devoted presence in your life.

name: Brisbane
description:
Brisbane is a young, large crossbreed aged just over 1 year old with a gentle and affectionate nature.

Brisbane is a loving and people-focused dog who forms strong bonds with his humans. He enjoys being close and will happily follow you from room to room, always wanting to be near his people.

Brisbane is a double merle and has some sensory impairments, including limited vision in one eye and reduced hearing. Despite this, he navigates his environment well and lives a happy, full life.

In the home, Brisbane is calm, clean, and well behaved. He is non-destructive, settles well, and can be left alone without issue. He adapts well to everyday life and has shown he can cope in busier environments such as shops and cafés when supported correctly.

Brisbane is dog friendly and has shown he can live alongside other dogs. He is also gentle with children, although due to his sensitivity, a home with older or dog-savvy children would be more suitable.

Brisbane can become overwhelmed in new or busy situations. When this happens, he may become overexcited and struggle to regulate himself. This is not aggression, but a response to feeling unsure, and with calm handling and structure, he settles well.

He walks nicely on the lead and responds well to guidance. With consistency and a calm approach, he continues to grow in confidence.

Brisbane would suit a patient and understanding home that can provide structure, routine, and a calm environment. He needs owners who are willing to manage introductions carefully and allow him time to decompress and feel secure.

Brisbane is a gentle, loyal dog who, in the right home, will form a deeply devoted bond and become a constant companion.

Brisbane is crate trained, clean, and quiet in his crate overnight. He is not destructive at home but does need access to chew toys to keep himself entertained.

He especially enjoys filled Kongs, raw bones, and a game of tug. While he can struggle to self-settle at times, he’s learning the concept of “quiet time” and developing an off switch.

He enjoys accompanying his foster carer to work and confidently navigates busy public spaces such as shops and town centres. Brisbane is calm in loud environments and loves interacting with people. He can be left alone without issue, often just sleeping or chewing his toys.

As a Double Merle, Brisbane comes with some genetic considerations. He can both see and hear, although his left eye, which has a starburst pupil, may have some visual limitations.

Due to his lack of pigmentation, he is sensitive to the sun and can burn easily, so he requires sun protection and careful management.

name: Dorris
description:
Dorris is a 3 year old female American Bulldog Cross with a loving and playful nature who has sadly been waiting in rescue for over 2 years.

In the home, Dorris is calm, clean, and well behaved. She is non-destructive and enjoys a quiet, settled environment where she can relax, play with her toys, and spend time with her person.

She is affectionate and enjoys both playtime and cuddles, forming a strong bond with those she trusts.

Dorris is a fun and engaging dog who brings personality and joy into the home. She is happy to entertain herself with toys or chews but equally enjoys interaction and affection from her humans.

Dorris does struggle around other dogs and will need to be the only pet in the home. Walks and environments need to be carefully managed to ensure she feels safe and comfortable.

Due to her needs, Dorris requires an experienced and understanding owner who can provide structure, calm handling, and appropriate management of her environment.

Kennel life can be particularly stressful for Dorris due to the presence of other dogs, and she is often kept in a quieter area to help reduce this stress.

Dorris would suit a calm, structured home where she can feel safe and settled. She needs an owner who will advocate for her, manage her surroundings, and allow her to live a peaceful life without unnecessary pressure.

When given the right environment, Dorris is a loving, loyal, and joyful companion who simply wants to play, cuddle, and belong.

If they have been around children, what ages were the children?

How does the dog walk on the lead?She does focus on other dogs and will lunge at them, so will need to be walked in quieter areas or exercised in a secure field on her own. When she’s on her own, she’s generally well behaved on the lead, no excessive pulling. She’s quite nosy and likes a good sniff around.

How long can the dog be left at home without issue?7 hours plus. She was left for longer periods when I had to stay at work and was absolutely fine when I got home. No destruction or accidents. My neighbour did say she barked a bit when left, so she may be sorted to shorter periods or a house without many neighbours.

Is the dog destructive at home?Not at all, she is extremely well behaved girl in the house. Fully housetrained and doesn’t chew anything she shouldn’t. She was provided with a variety of chew toys though as she constantly likes to chew or play with balls etc.

Whats are they fed?I fed her raw and she loved it

name: Kalli
description:
Kalli is a young, athletic crossbreed aged just over 1 year old with a loving and energetic nature.

Kalli is very people-focused and forms strong bonds with her humans. She thrives on interaction and enjoys being close, often seeking reassurance and connection from those around her.

She is an intelligent and eager-to-please dog who is already showing great potential. Kalli knows basic commands such as sit and wait and is continuing to learn, responding well to training, especially when food rewards are involved.

Kalli is still very much a young dog and can become easily overstimulated, particularly around other dogs. She can struggle to regulate her excitement and may not always communicate appropriately, which can lead to misunderstandings. For this reason, she will need to be the only pet in the home while she continues to build confidence and develop her social skills.

She walks well on the lead in calmer environments but can become strong and determined if something catches her attention. With consistent, one-to-one training, she is continuing to improve.

Kalli can become bored if not mentally stimulated, so she will require enrichment and an active home that can meet both her physical and mental needs. She may also jump up when excited but is already learning that calm behaviour is rewarded.

Kalli would suit a home that is committed to training, structure, and consistency. She will thrive with owners who understand how to guide a young, energetic dog and are willing to invest time into her development.

Kalli is a loving and loyal dog with huge potential, and in the right home, she will grow into a deeply rewarding and devoted companion.

name: Roxy
description:
Roxy is an 18 month old female Caucasian shepherd located in Spain

This beautiful, medium-sized Caucasian Shephard is Roxy, still young at 18 months, she has the traditional dark, tan semi coat and black masked face, who has recently been saved by us from the streets.

Roxy is a very sweet girl, still a youngster, she can be nervous around new dogs to begin with until she knows they are friendly, but generally once introduced correctly she’s very playful and good with the dogs, but she can be a bit of slow burner.

Roxy walks very well on her lead and we think that she is suitable for a family with older children with or without another friendly dog as she can be a bit excitable.

Roxy is a no to cats we think, it’s not that she’s aggressive, but she chases them.Roxy is ready to travel now for the right family.

Great with people and dogs. gentle nature, and is obedient, happy to play and a pretty girl.

name: Roo
description:
Elegant Roo is a 5 year old female Greyhound. She is a friendly and gentle girl with a sensitive side. She enjoys being with her people, receiving affection, and playing with her toys.

She is social with other dogs but can be worried of some, so she will need her owner to help build her confidence and provide her with reassurance and guidance when needed.

She would love a home where she could snuggle up on the sofa after a day of sniffy adventures and enjoy the wonders of being a much-loved family dog. This gorgeous girl will make an extremely rewarding companion for anyone lucky enough to adopt her.

Roo can live in a flat as long as there is direct access to a private garden. She can live with sensible junior or secondary age children that will give her space when needed.

She could also potentially live with a calm, large-breed adult dog, subject to a successful meet at Mayhew. Roo has a very subtle lameness in her right foreleg, especially after intensive exercise.

It is possible that she has an underlying injury from her previous work as a racing greyhound. She is on long-term anti-inflammatories for this and doing very well.

Roo has been microchipped, neutered, and vaccinated and is up to date with flea and worming treatment. She has also been health checked and behaviourally assessed. Lastly, every dog adopted from us will go home with 4 weeks free pet insurance.

name: Cleo
description:
Cleo is a stunning 2 year old Cane Corso with a loyal and affectionate nature.

Cleo is a gentle and sensitive girl who forms strong bonds with her people. She is very people-focused and loves to be close, often sitting beside you or resting her head on you for comfort and reassurance.

In the home, Cleo is calm, clean, and well behaved. She is crate trained, settles beautifully, and shows no destructive behaviour. She enjoys her comforts, including relaxing with her family and playing with her favourite toys, especially her squeaky ball.

Cleo walks nicely on the lead and regularly checks in with her handler, showing a willingness to learn and stay connected. She mixes well with other dogs, particularly when introductions are handled correctly, and has shown she can live with a dog-savvy cat.

Cleo is a sensitive soul who can be wary of unfamiliar men or sudden movements. However, with calm and patient introductions, she builds trust well and relaxes into her environment.

She is currently receiving behavioural support and continues to make positive progress.

Due to her breed and temperament, Cleo requires a knowledgeable home with experience of guardian breeds. She thrives in a calm, structured environment with clear guidance and consistency.

Cleo would suit an adult-only home or one with older, dog-savvy teenagers who understand her needs and can give her the time and space to settle.

Cleo is a devoted and loyal companion who, in the right home, will become an incredibly rewarding and loving addition to the family.

name: Joey
description:
Joey is an adorable three-legged, 8-year-old French Bulldog who came into rescue due to his owner’s housing situation. He’s in an Oldies Club foster home in north-west Leicestershire, near the Derbyshire border.

He was briefly rehomed, but didn’t get along with the resident female dog, so is back at his foster home, waiting for a lovely retirement home.

Summary: Joey is a happy-go-lucky charmer who takes almost everything in his 3 legged stride. He doesn’t like cats and needs to be an only dog at home. Resident teenagers should be fine for him but not very young children.

He wants a retirement home where he usually has human company, has an hour of walkies a day, someone to watch what he eats (because he’ll try to wallop down anything!) and lots of toys, lap time and fusses.

Settled quickly in foster: Joey, also known as “Big Joe”, settled at his foster home within one day! He’s a confident dog and once he knew where the garden was, who would be feeding him and that he was allowed on the sofa, he was right at home.

Can be left sometimes: Joey does love being with someone, preferably on their lap, so he does need a home where there is usually someone around. When you do need to go out without him, he should just settle down and snooze until you’re home.

His foster carer has left him for 3 hours and watched him on a camera having a lovely sleep. He wouldn’t want this to be a daily occurrence though because he does need plenty of people time.

Needs to be the only dog at home: Joey gets on OK with other dogs when out and about and, as you can see, he’s fine with the two resident Sighthounds in his foster home.

However, this blissful state or affairs is the exception not the rule and Joey has a history of not getting on with other dogs in his home (both male and female, even after nice introductions).

As he’s already had both a foster home and an adoption fall through because he took against the resident dogs, it’s now thought he should be the only dog in his retirement home.

That way, he can be assured that all toys, food and attention are rightfully his.

Needs a cat-free home: Joey doesn’t seem to like the cats next door and his foster carer thinks he would chase them if given the opportunity.

Could live with teenagers: We were told that Joey used to live with a teenager and was happy. There are no children at his foster home but we think he should be OK to live with sensible teenagers.

Great on walks: Joey’s missing leg does not hold him back on walks at all. He walks pretty well on the lead and has good recall when off lead in enclosed spaces. He does have a tendency to eat things he shouldn’t, so he needs to be watched.

He ate some vegetables which were growing in the garden when his foster carer wasn’t looking, and would eat cat poo if he had a chance. There are cats living next door so daily vigilance in the garden is needed!

Joey munched a whole cucumber in seconds so he doesn’t need long to steal something he shouldn’t and guzzle it. For walks, he goes once or twice a day and needs about an hour of exercise each day.

Great in the car: Joey is very good in the car and he has taken the bus a few times too. He especially likes going to the pub as he’s sure to get lots of attention.

Joey’s favourite pastimes: Eating, walking, sleeping and hugs.

Joey’s ideal home: He would love a home where he can have loads of fuss and sofa snuggles. He is quite a lapdog and would rather sit on you than near you.

He doesn’t bother himself with personal space and he wants to be around people as much as possible. Daily walks and tasty food are his favourite things. He’s pretty easy to please. He needs to be your only dog.

Health notes: Joey is neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, wormed and flea treated. Joey lost his leg when he was younger and this really doesn’t impact him very much at all. He has a poultry allergy, so eats a mainly fish-based diet.

As long as he isn’t stealing anybody’s food this is easy enough to manage by just avoiding any poultry.

name: Leo
description:
EVERYONE loves Leo! If you’re looking for a real character – a dog who will give you lots of laughs, lots of fun and cuddles…this little one-eyed lion is your boy.

Leo, born in 2023 is a lively, cheeky terrier mix and as with all terriers, needs firm and consistent boundaries. People with terrier experience in particular, will love this boy’s intelligent, lively and hugely fun personality.

Leo can live with other dogs (he lives with 3 others of all ages and sizes in his foster). He hasn’t got a nervous bone in his body so can sometimes be full on, liking rough and tumble vocal play.

He might be a little domineering for a very quiet, older or nervous dog, but a great buddy for an enthusiastic kindred spirit (any size… Leo thinks he’s a Lion!).

Leo likes his dog pals but he’s more of a people’s-dog than a dog’s dog. He adores people, he adores men; he’s been lovely with his fosterer’s 7-year-old grandson. His loves are food, cuddles and walks…. dog friends come after.

So, Leo would also be perfectly happy as an only dog if he kept up regular socialising with other dog friends.

Leo is clean in the house, crate trained, can be left alone for short periods, travels beautifully (he loves a long car journey) and has behaved very nicely in a care home (where everyone fell in love with him of course).

Leo has learnt to live in a home and now knows the difference between his own toys and other objects where chewing is concerned.

Originally, Leo came from Bosnia. He came to our rescuer’s attention when he was hit by a car. Unfortunately, his eye was found to be badly damaged and had to be removed.

Leo really doesn’t mind that he only has one eye and his cheeky jaunty look suits this loveable boy perfectly!

Please note – we do not rehome dogs to families with children under the age of 10.

Leo is super adaptable and can live just about anywhere, as long as it has a garden. He loves chasing about. A busy household would be fine. A large household would be fine.

Leo will need a good amount of exercise, play and stimulation.

Leo chases cats so a household without cats would be best unless they are extremely dog savvy.

Please read about our Adoption process. We really appreciate it when potential adopters have read our advice, and these are the people who are most often successful at application stage!

Our adoption donation is £325. This includes travel to the UK, their vaccinations, pet passport, microchip and all preparation for travel. They also come with 5 weeks free insurance (excluding The Channel Isles & Isle of Man).

name: Jess
description:
Jerss is a 1 year old male medium size Labrador Retriever Cross, a little shy but very good.

Jess is a very playful, and sweet puppy, rescued with his siblings, he was in a kennel for few months and now he’s in a foster home.

He loves human people, he is a little shy at the beginning but after a while he comes close to you asking for cuddles.

He has the character of the lab, very balanced and respectful of your spaces.

His foster mum is very happy with his progress; he is really gaining confidence day by day.

Jess is learning how to walk with the leash, following the other dogs of the family. He is a really good boy.

Would you like to adopt Jess and love him forever?

Jess will be the best part of your life, he will fill your life with joy and happiness.

name: Alfie
description:
Alfie is a 2 year old neutered small mixed breed currently in foster care in Lincolnshire.

Alfie is a sensitive dog who builds trust slowly. He is cautious around new people and needs time and space to approach interactions at his own pace. Once he feels safe, he forms strong bonds and shows an affectionate and playful side.

He enjoys spending time with his foster carers and will seek out attention when comfortable. He is curious, enjoys exploring the garden and benefits from a calm and predictable routine.

Alfie can become overwhelmed if approached too quickly or if expectations are placed on him too soon. He requires patient handling and a consistent environment to help him continue building confidence.

He is housetrained and crate trained and settles well overnight. He walks well on lead and enjoys regular walks.

He is currently working on accepting the removal of his harness and will require continued support with this, as he can still be sensitive during handling around his head.

Alfie enjoys food and is motivated by it, although he prefers to eat undisturbed. He is still learning to tolerate grooming and will benefit from gentle, ongoing desensitisation.

name: Marcus
description:
Marcus is an 8 month old neutered male small to medium mixed breed currently in foster care in Lincolnshire. He is iElisa negative and measures approximately 35cm.

Marcus was previously living in a shelter environment in Romania where he shared space with several other dogs.

He is settling well into foster life and is described as friendly and non-dominant with other dogs. He mixes well with his foster siblings and shows appropriate social behaviour.

Marcus enjoys human interaction and will come for affection, but is not overly demanding. He has a calm and balanced nature and is not highly energetic.

Marcus is expected to remain small to medium in size.

He would suit a home able to continue his development and provide routine, companionship and ongoing training as he matures.

name: Courtney
description:
Courtney is a 6 year old female Mastin cross breed located in Spain.

Pretty Courtney is a big, beautiful girl, with a smooth, soft, tan coat, and soulful eyes. Our Courtney is a Mastine Cross, she stands at medium to large size, and she came to the rescue in 2023, so now its well overdue for her to find a loving home.

She has always been part of the ´front´ pack & gets along with other dogs. She only ever once clashed with another dominant female, but otherwise she enjoys being in a pack. She walks well on her lead & enjoys attention and cuddles.

Courtney is a calm, gentle girl with confidence to fit into many situations so she would thrive in a home with or without another friendly dog and older children over 12. She is not cat tested.

The rescue where Courtney is living is closing and so she is one of 35 dogs looking for a home quickly. Can you help Courtney with a loving forever home?

Great with people and dogs. gentle nature, and is obedient, and a pretty girl.

name: Hovis
description:
Hovis is a 4 year old male medium cross breed currently in the East Midlands.

He was born at the shelter on 20 March 2021 after his mother, Rosie, was rescued heavily pregnant from a public shelter. Sadly, Rosie later passed away.

Hovis has grown up in a rescue environment and is described as friendly. He has been child tested and is comfortable around children.

He lives with other dogs and is good with them. He walks on a lead and manages routine handling well.

Hovis weighs approximately 25 kg and stands around 52 cm tall. He is neutered and travel ready.

Hovis is looking for a committed home willing to support him as he transitions from shelter life into a family environment.

name: Lasi
description:
Our extra special girl Lasi is approximately two years old and a very splendid cross breed at the bottom end of medium. Lasi weighs just fourteen kilos and measures twelve inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found abandoned on the streets, Lasi has been in our Cyprus shelter for four months.

Lasi has been described by our shelter manager as calm, sweet, eager to please and will make a fabulous family dog.

Her appearance is breathtaking with a light tan coat and a graduated darker tan along her back. Gorgeous hazel eyes and beautiful ears are showstoppers.

Lasi will fit into her forever home so well and will bring years of joy and happiness to her very fortunate adopters.

Lasi walks nicely on her lead and enjoys her time in the car. She seems to mix perfectly well with children, cats and other dogs.

name: Carmel
description:
Our special pretty girl Carmel is approximately three years old and a sublime cross breed at the bottom end of medium. Carmel weighs a perfect thirteen kilos and measures eleven inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found abandoned on the streets, Carmel has been in our Cyprus shelter for three months.

Our shelter manager describes Carmel as quite adorable with a submissive personality. She has a natural kindness and empathy about her and will prove to be very low maintenance.

Carmel thoroughly enjoys human companionship and savours a cuddle and a lap. Her manners are impeccable, and she is far too good for shelter life.

Carmel is longing for her forever home with a loving family and gentle routine. With so much love to give, Carmel will be treasured for her entire life.

Carmel walks really nicely on her lead and enjoys her time in the car. She seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Bert
description:
Bert is a 4 year old large male Labrador Retriever Cross.

Bert is Black and White in colour and his coat is short in length.

Bert is a Labrador Cross and has been at the shelter a few years through no fault of his own. He was found on the street and was most likely abandoned at around 1 year old. Despite his bad start in life he is a lovely, sweet boy.

Bert is quite a busy boy who likes to keep active. He loves his walks although can be a bit strong and needs to learn some manners.

However, with regular daily exercise we are sure this will improve. Bert has probably never had a home of his own but we think he will adapt quite quickly.

Bert gets on well with other dogs, both male and female, and he would be better living with another dog for company. He also needs someone home most of the day.

Poor Bert is getting fed up of being in the shelter and really deserves his own forever home.

name: Marley
description:
Marley is a 5 year old large male Labrador.

Marley is Golden and White in colour and his coat is medium in length.

Marley’s nature is sweet, friendly and clumsy.

None of us can understand why Marley is still in the shelter waiting. He is the most friendly, loveable dog.

He has the typical Labrador mentality although he is probably not pure. He loves his walks, he loves attention and loves belly rubs.

Marley gets on with most dogs and we believe would be great with children. He could be a family dog, couples dog or a one person dog.

He can live with other dogs but possibly better suited to females and to dogs that are not dominant. He could also be an only dog.

Marley has been with us about 4 years sadly, through no fault of his own, so may take time to adapt to the outside world.

Who will give this gorgeous boy a chance at happiness?

name: Luna
description:
Luna is a 3-year-old female Cross-Breed. She is described as a medium-sized dog and weighs approximately 14.5kg. She is currently in Croatia while she waits for a permanent home to call her own.

She is a happy and energetic dog who clearly enjoys being around both people and other dogs. Luna loves to run, jump, and play, showing that she has an active and lively personality.

She is expected to become a loyal and loving companion in the right home.

Luna has already learned to walk nicely on a lead, which is a great foundation for her continued training. She is friendly with other dogs and has the potential to live in a home with them.

She can also live with children over 8 years old, making her suitable for families with older children.

She has not yet been tested with cats, but this can be arranged if needed. Luna is not fully house trained at the moment, though it is noted that she is likely to learn quickly with guidance and routine.

With patience and consistency, she should continue to make good progress in a home environment.

Luna has received extensive veterinary care to prepare her for adoption. She is microchipped, vaccinated against rabies, and has been vaccinated twice against infectious diseases.

She will also receive the Bordetella vaccine before transport, has been castrated, and has tested negative for Mediterranean diseases and Brucellosis. In addition, she will be given a kennel cough nasal vaccine before travel.

name: Molly
description:
Molly is a 1 year old large female Cross Breed.

Molly is Black in colour and her coat is long in length.

Molly’s nature is fun loving and she loves to cuddle.

The gorgeous scruffy Molly was found abandoned by a couple who took her in but then decided they couldn’t look after her so she came to the shelter.

Molly was a little nervous at first but soon got to know everyone. Molly loves charging around the compound playing with the other dogs. She adores playing with the hose so will most likely love water and swimming.

She’s a lovely, friendly, happy girl who would probably be a very good family dog or can live with just adults.

She gets on fine with the dogs she shares a kennel with and would be happier living with another dog. Needs someone home most of the day.

name: Camel
description:
Camel is an 8-year-old male Cross-Breed. He has recently returned to care due to his previous owner’s health and is currently in Leicester.

Camel is described as a gentle giant who brings joy to everyone he meets and loves nothing more than cuddles on the sofa.

He has a calm, affectionate nature and enjoys sunbathing, paddling in the pool, and eating, showing that he takes pleasure in simple comforts.

Camel has struggled with kennel life, often appearing lost and lonely, but he responds well to time, care, and enrichment.

He would be happy with garden exercise in a home that can provide love, attention, and opportunities for mental stimulation.

Camel can live with children aged 10 and above, but he is not suitable to live with cats or other dogs.

He would benefit from walks where he could meet friendly dogs in a controlled environment.

name: Reuben
description:
Reuben is a 2 year old male Hound Cross-Breed. Reuben, a gentle boy, needs a loving home.

There are few rescue stories for dogs in Cyprus that start well. It is a story of sadness and neglect. Hunting on the island means many beautiful dogs are treated like trash — neglected and starved under the misconception it will make them better hunting dogs.

Often abused physically and terrorised mentally, Reuben is sadly a classic example of this.

Found in Lefkara village, terrified and emaciated, his hip bones visibly showing. He was extremely skittish and on edge when rescued.

Once at the shelter, Reuben was allowed to decompress in a safe place, with small meals gradually building him up under veterinary instruction. What he has been through, we don’t want to imagine.

Reuben is likely a hunting dog that wasn’t performing. We’ve since discovered what a gentle, sweet, and kind boy he is — hunting is not in his nature.

He was discarded in the mountains in the hope he would perish. Somehow, this tired, skinny boy made his way down into the village, showing incredible resilience despite how terrible he must have felt.

Reuben is settling well into shelter life. He has a shy nature but is ever so kind and gentle. He is inquisitive and shy with children but friendly, and always sweet and loving with the other shelter dogs. Not cat tested.

Reuben is naturally wary of new people on first meeting, but he manages to be brave — coming forward for sniffs and fuss. He trusts and adores his rescuer, Lin Ova. With time and patience, Reuben can learn to trust.

He wants affection and loves kisses and cuddles, regardless of the terrible things he’s been through. Dogs are incredible for continuing to trust humans even after humans do horrible things to them

Reuben would be best sharing his home with another dog or two to help him settle and build trust. He could live in a home with older children aged 12+.

Reuben has a lot of learning to do but is very keen to please, very bright, and eager to learn.

Rescue backed by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-registered charity.

Please message if you think you can show Reuben what it’s like to be truly loved.

name: Breeze
description:
Breeze is a 5 year old German shorthaired pointer. She is large in size at approx. 23kg and is currently in Croatia.

Breeze is good with other dogs, likes to play and run and is very loving.

She currently lives in kennels so may need some house training. She walks well on a leash.

Breeze can live with other dogs and children over 8 years old. She cannot live with cats.

Breeze is microchipped, rabies vaccinated, infectious diseases two times vaccinated, bordatella vaccine will be recieved before transport, castrated, Mediterranean diseases tested-negative.

Brucellosis tested negative and Kennel cough nasel given before travel.

Adoption fee and home check applies, and full rescue backup is provided by Ninas Haven.

name: Minty
description:
Minty is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is described as a beautiful boy with a charming personality that has clearly helped him through some tough times. His affectionate and fun nature shines through in everything he does.

He previously spent six months in Lancram and narrowly escaped with his life, which makes his gentle and loving temperament even more special.

Despite his past, he has remained friendly and people-focused. He truly enjoys being around his humans and building a close bond.

Minty loves his walks and being outdoors, making him a great match for someone who enjoys an active lifestyle. Time spent exploring the outside world is one of his favourite things. He is happiest when he can share these moments with his special person.

At home, Minty would prefer a situation where his keeper is around for much of the time. He forms strong attachments and thrives on companionship and routine. A household where he is not left alone for long periods would suit him best.

Although he can get along with other dogs while out on walks, Minty would like to be the only dog in the home. He enjoys social moments outside but prefers a calm and focused environment indoors.

Having his humans all to himself would help him feel settled and secure.

He would be an especially good match for a retired but active person who enjoys regular walks. Someone with time, patience, and affection to give would help him truly flourish. In return, Minty offers loyalty, warmth, and plenty of loving companionship.

Minty is neutered, immunised, microchipped, and has been treated for fleas and worms. He has also been blood tested for Brucella canis and comes with a Romanian passport. A home check and adoption fee will apply as part of the adoption process.

name: Bilbo
description:
Calling all dog lovers – meet the very handsome Bilbo. Bilbo is a 5 year old male Spaniel Cross-Breed currently in Surrey, U.K., and he is looking for an adoptive or foster home.

Can live with a small dog after correct introductions.

Cat-free home, as he is not used to cats.

Bilbo is a 5 year old rescue boy who is searching for his forever (or foster) home. Currently located in Surrey, Bilbo likes his own space and will settle quite happily in his bed. He sleeps through the night and is calm and quiet.

Bilbo thrives in peaceful home environments and loves relaxing the most.

Bilbo is toilet trained, lead trained, and can be left for short periods in the house. He is non-destructive.

On walks, Bilbo shows lead frustration towards other dogs. He may pull and react out of frustration and fear. He shows no reaction towards people or strangers.

Bilbo is definitely food-motivated and will do anything for a tasty treat; this will help with his training going forward.

With correct introductions, Bilbo could live with another small dog, but he is still learning social cues and boundaries, so a patient canine companion would be ideal.

Bilbo could live with older, dog-savvy children of teenage age, as long as he has his own child-free space to go to. Bilbo likes his own space and does not like too much fuss when he is resting. He especially does not like being touched on the top of his head.
